questions.question: A singly reinforced concrete beam of balanced section is made of M20 grade concrete and Fe415 grade steel bars. The magnitudes of the maximum compressive strain in concrete and the tensile strain in the bars at ultimate state under flexure, as per IS 456: 2000 are _________ , respectively. (round off to four decimal places)
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Limit State Flexure – Balanced Section (IS 456)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Concrete grade: M20
    • Steel grade: Fe415
    • Singly reinforced balanced section
  • Aim: Find the magnitudes of maximum compressive strain in concrete and tensile strain in bars at the ultimate limit state (IS 456:2000), rounded to four decimal places.

Core Concepts:

As per IS 456:2000, Clause 38.1 (assumptions for limit state of collapse – flexure):

  • Maximum compressive strain in concrete \(= 0.0035\) (constant for all grades)
  • Plane sections remain plane → linear strain diagram
  • For a balanced section, concrete reaches 0.0035 simultaneously with steel reaching design yield strain

Design yield strain in steel (for Fe415, cold-worked/HYSD bars):\[\varepsilon_{st} = 0.002 + \dfrac{0.87\, f_y}{E_s} \]where \(E_s = 2 \times 10^5\) MPa (IS 456:2000). Strains are dimensionless.

Solution Method:

Directly use the code-prescribed concrete strain and compute steel strain from the formula above.

Alternative verification: \(x_{u,\max}/d = 0.48\) (for Fe415) \(\Rightarrow \varepsilon_{st} = 0.0035 \times \dfrac{1 - 0.48}{0.48} \approx 0.0038\) (same result).

Common pitfall: Using working-stress strains (0.0020) or forgetting the 0.002 offset.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Maximum compressive strain in concrete (IS 456:2000):\[\varepsilon_{cu} = 0.0035 \]
  2. Compute \(0.87\,f_y\):\[0.87 \times 415 = 361.05 \text{ MPa} \]
  3. Compute \(\dfrac{0.87\,f_y}{E_s}\):\[\dfrac{361.05}{200{,}000} = 0.00180525 \]
  4. Tensile strain in steel at balanced failure:\[\varepsilon_{st} = 0.002 + 0.00180525 = 0.00380525 \]
  5. Round to four decimal places:\[\varepsilon_{st} \approx 0.0038 \]
  6. Verification:\[\dfrac{x_{u,\max}}{d} = \dfrac{0.0035}{0.0035 + 0.00380525} \approx 0.479 \approx 0.48 \text{ (as per IS 456 Table G-1.1)} \]

Final Answer:

0.0035 and 0.0038 | Correct Option: (A)

questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Mix Design

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data: Variation in Water-Cement Ratio (W/C ratio) in cement concrete mix design.
  • Aim: Determine the relationship between W/C ratio, compressive strength, and workability.

Core Concepts:

  1. Abrams' Law (Water-Cement Ratio Law): The compressive strength of concrete is inversely proportional to the W/C ratio, provided the mix is of workable consistency.\[f_c = \dfrac{A}{B^{1.5(w/c)}} \]As W/C ratio \(\uparrow\), strength \(\downarrow\). Excess water creates capillary voids upon evaporation, weakening the concrete matrix.
  2. Workability: The ease with which concrete can be mixed, transported, placed, and compacted. Water acts as a lubricant between aggregate particles and fluidizes the cement paste.
    As W/C ratio \(\uparrow\), fluidity increases → workability (slump) increases.
  3. Reference: IS 456:2000, Clause 6.1.2 & IS 10262:2019.

Solution Method:

  • Analyze the impact of increasing water content on strength using Abrams' Law.
  • Analyze the impact on physical ease of movement (workability).
  • Correlate the two trends to select the correct statement.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effect on Compressive Strength:
    By Abrams' Law, strength is inversely proportional to W/C ratio.
    Increasing W/C ratio → gel/space ratio decreases (more voids).
    Result: Compressive Strength Decreases.
  2. Effect on Workability:
    Increasing W/C ratio adds more lubricating water to the mix.
    Result: Workability Increases.
  3. Combined Finding:
    With an increase in W/C ratio: Strength decreases, Workability increases → matches option (A).

Final Answer:

Compressive strength decreases but workability increases | Correct Option: (A)

questions.question: Consider the fillet-welded lap joint shown in the figure (not to scale). The length of the weld shown is the effective length. The welded surfaces meet at right angle. The weld size is 8 mm, and the permissible stress in the weld is 120 MPa. What is the safe load \( P \) (in kN, rounded off to one decimal place) that can be transmitted by this welded joint? _______________
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Connections – Fillet Weld (Lap Joint)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Weld type: Fillet weld (Lap joint)
    • Weld size: \(s = 8\text{ mm}\)
    • Permissible shear stress: \(\tau_{vw} = 120\text{ MPa}\)
    • Plate width: 50 mm, Lap length: 75 mm
    • Total effective weld length: \(L_{eff} = 75 + 50 + 75 = 200\text{ mm}\) (two side welds + one end weld)
  • Aim: Calculate the safe load \(P\).

Core Concepts:

Effective Throat Thickness (IS 800:2007, Cl. 10.5.3):\[t_t = 0.7 \times s \]

Safe Load:\[P = \tau_{vw} \times t_t \times L_{eff} \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Throat thickness:\[t_t = 0.7 \times 8 = 5.6\text{ mm} \]
  2. Effective weld length:\[L_{eff} = 75 + 50 + 75 = 200\text{ mm} \]
  3. Safe load:\[P = 120\text{ N/mm}^2 \times 5.6\text{ mm} \times 200\text{ mm} \]\[P = 120 \times 1120 = 134{,}400\text{ N} = 134.4\text{ kN} \]

Final Answer:

\(P = 134.4\text{ kN}\) | Accepted range: 134.0 to 136.0

The modulus of elasticity of steel is \( 2 \times 10^5 \) N/mm². As per IS456:2000, in which type(s) of the bars, the stress in the compression steel ( \( f_{sc} \) ) can reach the design strength ( \( 0.87f_y \) ) at the limit state of collapse?
options: Both Fe250 plain bars and Fe500 deformed bars
Neither Fe250 plain bars nor Fe500 deformed bars

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Both Fe250 plain bars and Fe500 deformed bars
structuredOptions.html: Both Fe250 plain bars and Fe500 deformed bars

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Neither Fe250 plain bars nor Fe500 deformed bars
structuredOptions.html: Neither Fe250 plain bars nor Fe500 deformed bars

questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Limit State Method

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Material behavior in limit state design)
  • Given Data:
    • Doubly reinforced RCC beam
    • Steel Options: Fe250 (Plain) or Fe500 (Deformed)
    • Modulus of Elasticity: \(E_s = 2 \times 10^5 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • Code: IS 456:2000
  • Aim: Identify which steel grade can reach its full design strength \((0.87f_y)\) in the compression zone at the limit state of collapse.

Core Concepts:

  1. Strain Compatibility (IS 456:2000 Cl. 38.1):
    • Maximum Compressive Strain in Concrete: \(\epsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\)
    • Strain in compression steel \((\epsilon_{sc})\) is governed by the strain diagram: \(\epsilon_{sc} \leq \epsilon_{cu}\)
  2. Yield Strain of Steel:
    To reach the design stress of \(0.87f_y\), the steel strain must exceed the yield strain.
    • Fe250 (Mild Steel): Has a distinct yield point.\[\epsilon_y = \dfrac{0.87 f_y}{E_s} \]
    • Fe500 (HYSD/Cold Worked): No distinct yield point. Design stress \((0.87f_y)\) is reached at:\[\epsilon_{\text{target}} = \dfrac{0.87 f_y}{E_s} + 0.002 \]

Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the minimum strain required to reach design strength \((0.87f_y)\) for both steel grades.
  2. Compare these required strains with the maximum possible strain available from the concrete failure condition \((\epsilon_{cu} = 0.0035)\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Fe250 (Plain Bars):
    \(f_y = 250 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    Strain required to reach yield \((0.87f_y)\):\[\epsilon_{250} = \dfrac{0.87 \times 250}{2 \times 10^5} = \dfrac{217.5}{200000} \approx \mathbf{0.00109} \]
    Check availability: Since the concrete failure strain is 0.0035, and \(0.00109 \ll 0.0035\), compression steel situated close to the compression face will undergo strain greater than 0.00109.
    \(\therefore\) Fe250 yields and reaches design strength.
  2. Analyze Fe500 (Deformed Bars):
    \(f_y = 500 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    Strain required to reach design stress \((0.87f_y)\) per IS 456 (Fig. 23):\[\epsilon_{500} = \dfrac{0.87 \times 500}{2 \times 10^5} + 0.002 \]\[\epsilon_{500} = \dfrac{435}{200000} + 0.002 = 0.002175 + 0.002 = \mathbf{0.004175} \]
    Check availability: The maximum possible strain (concrete crushing) is 0.0035.\[\epsilon_{\text{available}} \;(0.0035) < \epsilon_{\text{required}} \;(0.004175) \]Even if the steel were at the extreme fiber, the strain physically cannot reach 0.004175 before the concrete crushes.
    \(\therefore\) Fe500 never reaches full design strength \((0.87f_y)\) in compression.
  3. Conclusion:
    Only Fe250 plain bars can reach the design strength of \(0.87f_y\) in the compression zone.

Final Answer:

(A) Fe250 plain bars only
Final Answer: (A) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: Consider the horizontal axis passing through the centroid of the steel beam cross-section shown in the figure. What is the shape factor (rounded off to one decimal place) for the cross-section?
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Plastic Analysis

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Calculation of Shape Factor)
  • Given Data:
    • Cross-section: Cruciform (Plus/+ shape)
    • Shape composed of 5 equal squares of size \(b \times b\)
    • Horizontal width \(= 3b\), Vertical height \(= 3b\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Shape Factor \((S)\).

Core Concepts:

  1. Shape Factor \((S)\): Ratio of Plastic Section Modulus to Elastic Section Modulus.\[S = \dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e} \]
  2. Elastic Section Modulus: \(Z_e = \dfrac{I_{xx}}{y_{\max}}\)
  3. Plastic Section Modulus: First moment of area about the Equal Area Axis (Plastic Neutral Axis).\[Z_p = \dfrac{A}{2}(\bar{y}_1 + \bar{y}_2) \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Geometry Definition:
    The cross-section consists of 5 squares each of area \(b^2\). Total height \(= 3b\). Due to symmetry, the Neutral Axis (NA) and Plastic Neutral Axis (PNA) both coincide at mid-height.
  2. Calculation of Moment of Inertia \((I_{xx})\):
    The section is split into three parts:
    • Part 1 – Middle horizontal strip (width \(= 3b\), height \(= b\)):​\[I_1 = \dfrac{3b \cdot b^3}{12} = \dfrac{3}{12}b^4 = 0.25\, b^4 \]
    • Part 2 – Top square (area \(= b^2\), centroid distance from NA \(= b\)):\[I_2 = \dfrac{b \cdot b^3}{12} + b^2 \cdot b^2 = \dfrac{1}{12}b^4 + b^4 = \dfrac{13}{12}b^4 \]
    • Part 3 – Bottom square (same as top square):\[I_3 = \dfrac{13}{12}b^4 \]
    \[I_{xx} = I_1 + I_2 + I_3 = \dfrac{3}{12}b^4 + \dfrac{26}{12}b^4 = \dfrac{29}{12}b^4 \approx 2.417\, b^4 \]
  3. Calculation of Elastic Section Modulus \((Z_e)\):
    Distance to extreme fiber: \(y_{\max} = 1.5b\)\[Z_e = \dfrac{I_{xx}}{y_{\max}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{29}{12}b^4}{1.5b} = \dfrac{29}{18}\, b^3 \approx 1.611\, b^3 \]
  4. Calculation of Plastic Section Modulus \((Z_p)\):
    PNA is at the center (by symmetry). Moment of area of upper half:
    PartAreaCentroid distance from NAMoment
    Top Square\(b^2\)\(b\)\(b^3\)
    Top half of middle row\(1.5b^2\)\(0.25b\)\(0.375b^3\)
    Total——\(1.375\, b^3\)

    By symmetry, \(Q_{\text{lower}} = 1.375\, b^3\)\[Z_p = Q_{\text{upper}} + Q_{\text{lower}} = 2 \times 1.375\, b^3 = 2.75\, b^3 \]
  5. Calculation of Shape Factor:\[S = \dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e} = \dfrac{2.75\, b^3}{\dfrac{29}{18}\, b^3} = \dfrac{2.75 \times 18}{29} = \dfrac{49.5}{29} \approx 1.7068 \]\[\boxed{S \approx 1.7} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.7 | Correct option: (B)

questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Design of Concrete Mix — Characteristic Strength

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: M20 concrete as per IS 456:2000.
  • Aim: Identify the correct definition of M20 grade.

2. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000, Clause 6.1.1 — Characteristic Strength Definition:
"Characteristic strength is defined as the strength of material below which not more than 5% of the test results are expected to fall."

Concrete Grade Nomenclature: M = Mix; 20 = characteristic compressive strength of 150 mm cubes at 28 days in MPa.

ParameterIS 456:2000 Requirement
Test specimen150 mm × 150 mm × 150 mm cube
Curing period28 days
Acceptance criterion5% fractile (95% confidence)
UnitsMPa (N/mm²)

Statistical Basis:\[f_{ck} = f_m - 1.65\sigma\]where \(f_{ck}\) = characteristic strength (5% fractile), \(f_m\) = mean strength, \(\sigma\) = standard deviation.

3. Solution Method:

OptionStatementEvaluation
AAverage cube strength of 20 MPa❌ Average > Characteristic
BAverage cylinder strength of 20 MPa❌ IS 456 uses cubes, not cylinders
C5-percentile cube strength of 20 MPa✅ Matches IS 456 definition
D5-percentile cylinder strength of 20 MPa❌ IS 456 specifies cube test

Important Distinction: Indian Standard (IS) and British Standard (BS) use 150 mm cubes; ASTM/ACI use cylinders (150 mm × 300 mm). Approximate conversion: \(f_{cylinder} \approx 0.80 \times f_{cube}\).

Sanity Check: If average strength were 20 MPa with typical \(\sigma = 4\) MPa, characteristic would be \(20 - 1.65 \times 4 = 13.4\) MPa, not 20 MPa. The mean must be higher: \(f_m \approx 20 + 1.65 \times 4 = 26.6\) MPa for M20.

4. Final Answer:

M20 refers to concrete with a 5-percentile cube strength of 20 MPa | Option(s): C

Nominal shear stress\(\tau_v = \dfrac{V_u}{bd}\)
Concrete shear strength\(\tau_c\) depends on \(p_t\) (% tension steel) and \(f_{ck}\)
Shear reinforcementRequired when \(\tau_v > \tau_c\)

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

StatementAnalysisIS 456 ReferenceVerdict
(A) Excessive shear reinforcement can lead to compression failure in concreteIf too much stirrup steel is provided, concrete struts may crush before steel yields — brittle compression failure.Clause 40.1 — max shear reinforcement limit✅ TRUE
(B) Beams without shear reinforcement, even if adequately designed for flexure, can have brittle failureConcrete shear failure is sudden and brittle (diagonal tension crack propagation). IS 456 mandates minimum shear reinforcement even when \(\tau_v < \tau_c\) for ductility.Clause 26.5.1.6 — minimum shear reinforcement✅ TRUE
(C) Main (longitudinal) reinforcement plays no role in shear resistanceLongitudinal steel contributes via: (1) Dowel action, (2) Increasing \(\tau_c\) (which depends on \(p_t\)), (3) Controlling crack width.Clause 40.2.1 — \(\tau_c\) depends on \(p_t\)❌ FALSE
(D) Nominal shear stress in beams of varying depth depends on both shear force and bending momentFor haunched beams:\[\tau_v = \dfrac{V_u \pm \dfrac{M_u}{d}\tan\beta}{bd}\]showing explicit dependence on both \(V_u\) and \(M_u\).Clause 40.1.1 — beams of varying depth✅ TRUE

4. Final Answer:

Statements (A), (B), and (D) are TRUE | Option(s): A, B, D

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: Two plates are connected by fillet welds of size 10 mm and subjected to tension, as shown in the figure. The thickness of each plate is 12 mm. The yield stress and the ultimate stress of steel under tension are 250 MPa and 410 MPa, respectively. The welding is done in the workshop (partial safety factor, \( \gamma_{mw} = 1.25 \)). As per the Limit State Method of IS 800: 2007, what is the minimum length (in mm, rounded off to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm) required of each weld to transmit a factored force \( P \) equal to 275 kN?
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Welded Connections

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Design of Fillet Weld).
  • Code: IS 800:2007 (Limit State Method).
  • Given Data:
    • Factored Load \(P = 275\) kN.
    • Weld Size \(S = 10\) mm.
    • Partial Safety Factor \(\gamma_{mw} = 1.25\) (Workshop weld).
    • Material: \(f_u = 410\) MPa.
    • Configuration: Two plates connected by two longitudinal fillet welds (top and bottom).
  • Aim: Find the minimum length of each weld (rounded to higher multiple of 5 mm).

2. Core Concepts:

Design Strength of Fillet Weld (\(P_{dw}\)):\[P_{dw} = L_w \times t_t \times f_{wd}\]\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{f_u}{\sqrt{3}\, \gamma_{mw}}\]

Throat Thickness (\(t_t\)): For \(90^\circ\) fusion faces, \(t_t = 0.7 \times S\).

Load Sharing: Since there are two welds, each weld carries \(P/2\), or total capacity = \(2 \times\) individual capacity.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Design Stress (\(f_{wd}\)):\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{410}{\sqrt{3} \times 1.25} = \dfrac{410}{2.165} = 189.37 \text{ N/mm}^2\]
  2. Calculate Throat Thickness (\(t_t\)):\[t_t = 0.7 \times 10 = 7 \text{ mm}\]
  3. Calculate Required Effective Length (\(L_{eff}\)):
    Total Load Capacity required = \(275\) kN = \(275 \times 10^3\) N.
    Let \(L_{total}\) be the combined length of both welds:\[275 \times 10^3 = L_{total} \times t_t \times f_{wd}\]\[275000 = L_{total} \times 7 \times 189.37\]\[L_{total} = \dfrac{275000}{1325.59} = 207.45 \text{ mm}\]
  4. Length per Weld:
    Since there are two welds:\[L_{weld} = \dfrac{207.45}{2} = 103.72 \text{ mm}\]
  5. Rounding: The question asks to round to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm.
    The next multiple of 5 after 103.72 is 105 mm.

4. Final Answer:

Minimum length of each weld is 105 mm | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
Consider the singly reinforced section of a cantilever concrete beam under bending, as shown in the figure (M25 grade concrete, Fe415 grade steel). The stress block parameters for the section at ultimate limit state, as per IS 456: 2000 notations, are given. The ultimate moment of resistance for the section by the Limit State Method is _________________ kN.m (round off to one decimal place).
[Note: Here, \( A_s \) is the total area of tension steel bars, \( b \) is the width of the section, \( d \) is the effective depth of the bars, \( f_{ck} \) is the characteristic compressive cube strength of concrete, \( f_y \) is the yield stress of steel, and \( x_u \) is the depth of neutral axis.]
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | RCC Design (Limit State Method)

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Concrete Grade: M25 (\(f_{ck} = 25\text{ MPa}\))
    • Steel Grade: Fe415 (\(f_y = 415\text{ MPa}\))
    • Width of section (\(b\)): \(300\text{ mm}\)
    • Tension reinforcement: 3 bars of 28 mm diameter (\(\phi = 28\text{ mm}\))
    • Overall depth (\(D\)): \(600\text{ mm}\)
    • Effective cover (\(d'\)): \(45\text{ mm}\) (from top fiber to centroid of steel, as it is a cantilever under hogging moment)
  • Aim: Calculate the ultimate moment of resistance (\(M_u\)) in \(\text{kN}\cdot\text{m}\) (rounded to one decimal place).

2. Core Concepts:

  • Effective Depth (\(d\)): Distance from extreme compression fiber to centroid of tension reinforcement.\[d = D - \text{effective cover}\]
  • Tensile and Compressive Forces (IS 456:2000, Annex G):\[T = 0.87\, f_y A_{st}, \quad C = 0.36\, f_{ck}\, x_u\, b\]
  • Limiting Neutral Axis: For Fe415, \(x_{u,max} = 0.48\,d\).
  • Ultimate Moment of Resistance:\[M_u = 0.87\, f_y A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\,x_u)\]

3. Solution Method:

Common Pitfall: Many students mistakenly assume \(d = 600\text{ mm}\). However, \(600\text{ mm}\) represents the overall depth \(D\), so \(d = 600 - 45 = 555\text{ mm}\). Using \(d = 600\text{ mm}\) gives \(M_u \approx 331\text{ kN·m}\), which falls outside the official answer key range (295–305).

  1. Calculate the area of steel (\(A_{st}\)).
  2. Calculate \(T\) and find actual \(x_u\) using \(C = T\).
  3. Check if the section is under-reinforced (\(x_u < x_{u,max}\)).
  4. Calculate \(M_u\) using the tension steel lever arm equation.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Effective Depth and Area of Steel:\[d = 600 - 45 = 555\text{ mm}\]\[A_{st} = 3 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (28)^2 = 3 \times 196\pi = 1847.256\text{ mm}^2\]
  2. Calculate Force and Depth of Neutral Axis (\(x_u\)):\[T = 0.87 \times 415 \times 1847.256 = 666{,}951.785\text{ N}\]Equating \(C = T\):\[0.36 \times 25 \times 300 \times x_u = 666{,}951.785\]\[2700\,x_u = 666{,}951.785 \implies x_u = 247.019\text{ mm}\]
  3. Check Section Type:\[x_{u,max} = 0.48 \times 555 = 266.4\text{ mm}\]Since \(x_u = 247.019\text{ mm} < x_{u,max} = 266.4\text{ mm}\), the section is under-reinforced. The calculation for \(M_u\) based on steel yielding is valid.
  4. Calculate Ultimate Moment of Resistance:\[z = d - 0.42\,x_u = 555 - 0.42(247.019) = 555 - 103.748 = 451.252\text{ mm}\]\[M_u = T \times z = 666{,}951.785 \times 451.252 = 300{,}963{,}326\text{ N·mm}\]\[M_u = \dfrac{300{,}963{,}326}{10^6} \approx 301.0\text{ kN·m}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(M_u = \mathbf{301.0}\text{ kN·m}\) | Accepted key range: 295.0 to 305.0

questions.question: In the context of elastic theory of reinforced concrete, the modular ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material to Young's modulus of elasticity of concrete.
Young's modulus of elasticity of concrete to Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material.
shear modulus of reinforcement material to the shear modulus of concrete.
Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material to the shear modulus of concrete.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material to Young's modulus of elasticity of concrete.
structuredOptions.html: Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material to Young's modulus of elasticity of concrete.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Young's modulus of elasticity of concrete to Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material.
structuredOptions.html: Young's modulus of elasticity of concrete to Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: shear modulus of reinforcement material to the shear modulus of concrete.
structuredOptions.html: shear modulus of reinforcement material to the shear modulus of concrete.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material to the shear modulus of concrete.
structuredOptions.html: Young's modulus of elasticity of reinforcement material to the shear modulus of concrete.

questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Elastic Theory of RCC

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall (Definition of modular ratio)
  • Given Data: Concept question about reinforced concrete
  • Aim: Define modular ratio correctly.

Core Concepts:

In the elastic theory of reinforced concrete (working stress method), the modular ratio (m) is a fundamental concept used to transform the area of steel reinforcement into an equivalent area of concrete for analysis purposes.

Physical Meaning:
Since steel has a much higher elastic modulus than concrete, under the same strain, steel experiences much higher stress. The modular ratio accounts for this difference in stiffness when computing the transformed section properties.

IS 456:2000 Provision:
\[m = \dfrac{E_s}{E_c}\]where:
\(E_s\) = Modulus of elasticity of steel \(\approx 2 \times 10^5\) MPa (200 GPa)
\(E_c\) = Modulus of elasticity of concrete \(= 5000\sqrt{f_{ck}}\) MPa, where \(f_{ck}\) = characteristic compressive strength in MPa.

Solution Method:

The modular ratio in reinforced concrete is defined as the ratio of the Young's modulus of the reinforcement (steel) to the Young's modulus of concrete. This transformation allows analysis of the RCC section as if entirely made of concrete, with the steel area replaced by an equivalent concrete area.

Verification of Options:

OptionStatementCorrect?
(A)\(E_{steel} / E_{concrete}\)✓ Yes
(B)\(E_{concrete} / E_{steel}\)✗ No (reciprocal)
(C)\(G_{steel} / G_{concrete}\)✗ No (shear modulus, not relevant)
(D)\(E_{steel} / G_{concrete}\)✗ No (mixing different properties)

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{m = \dfrac{E_s}{E_c}}\]Correct Option: (A)

questions.question: Which of the following equations is correct for the Pozzolanic reaction?
options: Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> + Reactive Silicon dioxide + H<sub>2</sub>O \(\rightarrow\) C-S-H

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> + Reactive Silicon dioxide + H<sub>2</sub>O \(\rightarrow\) C-S-H
structuredOptions.html: Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> + Reactive Silicon dioxide + H<sub>2</sub>O \(\rightarrow\) C-S-H

questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Pozzolanic Materials

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall (Pozzolanic reaction chemistry)
  • Given Data: Question about the Pozzolanic reaction equation
  • Aim: Identify the correct reactants in the Pozzolanic reaction.

Core Concepts:

Pozzolanic Materials are siliceous or aluminous materials that by themselves possess little or no cementitious value, but in the presence of moisture, chemically react with calcium hydroxide (portlandite) to form compounds possessing cementitious properties.

Sources of Pozzolanic Materials:

  • Natural: Volcanic ash, calcined clay, diatomaceous earth
  • Artificial: Fly ash, silica fume, ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS), rice husk ash

Key Reactants in the Pozzolanic Reaction:

  1. Calcium Hydroxide \(\text{[Ca(OH)}_2\text{]}\) — Released during cement hydration
  2. Reactive Silica \(\text{(SiO}_2\text{)}\) — Present in pozzolanic materials
  3. Water \(\text{(H}_2\text{O)}\) — Necessary for the reaction

Reaction Product: C-S-H (Calcium Silicate Hydrate) — the main binding compound in cement paste.

Verification of Options:

OptionComponentsAnalysis
(A)\(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\) + Reactive Superplasticiser + \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) → C-S-H✗ Incorrect — Superplasticizers are chemical admixtures, not reactants
(B)\(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\) + Reactive Silicon dioxide + \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) → C-S-H✓ Correct — Silica (SiO₂) is the key reactive component
(C)\(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\) + Reactive Sulphates + \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) → C-S-H✗ Incorrect — Sulphates form ettringite, not C-S-H
(D)\(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\) + Reactive Sulphur + \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) → C-S-H✗ Incorrect — Sulphur is not involved in this reaction

Correct Reaction:

\[\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{Reactive SiO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C-S-H (Calcium Silicate Hydrate)}\]

This reaction consumes the harmful calcium hydroxide (a byproduct of cement hydration) and converts it into beneficial C-S-H gel, thereby improving durability and strength.

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{Reactive SiO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C-S-H}}\]Correct Option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures

questions.question: A weld is used for joining an angle section ISA 100 mm × 100 mm × 10 mm to a gusset plate of thickness 15 mm to transmit a tensile load. The permissible stress in the angle is 150 MPa and the permissible shear stress on the section through the throat of the fillet weld is 108 MPa. The location of the centroid of the angle is represented by \(C_{yy}\) in the figure, where \(C_{yy} = 28.4\) mm. The area of cross-section of the angle is 1903 mm². Assuming the effective throat thickness of the weld to be 0.7 times the given weld size, the lengths \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) (rounded-off to the nearest integer) of the weld required to transmit a load equal to the full strength of the tension member are, respectively
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Welded Connections

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Angle section ISA 100×100×10 mm; Area \(A = 1903\) mm²; Centroid distance from heel \(C_{yy} = 28.4\) mm; Permissible tensile stress \(\sigma_{at} = 150\) MPa; Permissible weld shear stress \(\tau_{vw} = 108\) MPa; Weld size \(s = 5\) mm.
  • Aim: Find top weld length \(L_1\) and bottom weld length \(L_2\) to resist the full member strength without loading eccentricity.

Core Concepts:

  • Full Strength of Member: \(T = A \times \sigma_{at}\)
  • Weld Strength per unit length (IS 800:2007): \(q = t_e \times \tau_{vw}\), where effective throat \(t_e = 0.7s\).
  • Eccentricity-Free Connection: Centre of gravity of weld group must coincide with the centroidal axis of the angle:
    \[L_1 \cdot y_1 = L_2 \cdot y_2\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Tensile load capacity:\[T = 1903 \times 150 = 285{,}450 \text{ N}\]
  2. Weld capacity per mm length:\[t_e = 0.7 \times 5 = 3.5 \text{ mm}\]\[q = 3.5 \times 108 = 378 \text{ N/mm}\]
  3. Distance of welds from centroid:
    • Top weld \(L_1\) (at heel): \(y_1 = 28.4\) mm
    • Bottom weld \(L_2\) (at toe): \(y_2 = 100 - 28.4 = 71.6\) mm
  4. Force Equilibrium:\[(L_1 + L_2) = \dfrac{285{,}450}{378} = 755.158 \text{ mm}\]
  5. Moment Equilibrium:\[L_1 \times 28.4 = L_2 \times 71.6 \implies L_1 = 2.5211\, L_2\]
  6. Solve simultaneously:\[2.5211\,L_2 + L_2 = 755.158 \implies 3.5211\,L_2 = 755.158\]\[L_2 = \dfrac{755.158}{3.5211} \approx 214.46 \text{ mm}\]\[L_1 = 755.158 - 214.46 \approx 540.69 \text{ mm}\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{L_1 \approx 541 \text{ mm}, \quad L_2 \approx 214 \text{ mm}}\] Correct Option: (A)

questions.question: A reinforced concrete beam with rectangular cross section (width = 300 mm, effective depth = 580 mm) is made of M30 grade concrete. It has 1% longitudinal tension reinforcement of Fe 415 grade steel. The design shear strength for this beam is 0.66 N/mm². The beam has to resist a factored shear force of 440 kN. The spacing of two-legged, 10 mm diameter vertical stirrups of Fe 415 grade steel is ________mm. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Shear Design (IS 456:2000)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Beam: \(b = 300\) mm, \(d = 580\) mm; M30 concrete, Fe415 steel; \(\tau_c = 0.66\) N/mm²; \(V_u = 440\) kN; 2-legged vertical stirrups, \(\phi = 10\) mm.
  • Aim: Determine the spacing \(s_v\) of vertical stirrups (in mm, to nearest integer).

Core Concepts (IS 456:2000, Cl. 40):

  • Nominal Shear Stress: \(\tau_v = \dfrac{V_u}{bd}\)
  • Shear carried by concrete: \(V_c = \tau_c \cdot b \cdot d\)
  • Shear to be resisted by stirrups: \(V_{us} = V_u - V_c\)
  • Stirrup spacing: \(s_v = \dfrac{0.87\, f_y\, A_{sv}\, d}{V_{us}}\)
  • Maximum spacing limits (Cl. 26.5.1.5): \(0.75d\), absolute max 300 mm.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Check Section Shear Stress:
    \[\tau_v = \dfrac{440 \times 10^3}{300 \times 580} = 2.528 \text{ N/mm}^2\]
    For M30: \(\tau_{c,max} = 3.5\) N/mm² (Table 20, IS 456). Since \(2.528 < 3.5\), section is safe. ✓
  2. Shear resisted by concrete:
    \[V_c = 0.66 \times 300 \times 580 = 114{,}840 \text{ N} = 114.84 \text{ kN}\]
  3. Shear to be resisted by stirrups:
    \[V_{us} = 440{,}000 - 114{,}840 = 325{,}160 \text{ N}\]
  4. Area of shear reinforcement (2-legged, \(\phi\) 10 mm):
    \[A_{sv} = 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times 10^2 = 2 \times 78.54 = 157.08 \text{ mm}^2\]
  5. Calculate stirrup spacing:
    \[s_v = \dfrac{0.87 \times 415 \times 157.08 \times 580}{325{,}160} = \dfrac{32{,}894{,}057}{325{,}160} \approx 101.16 \text{ mm}\]
  6. Maximum spacing limits check:
    CriterionLimit
    Based on depth\(0.75d = 0.75 \times 580 = 435\) mm
    Absolute maximum300 mm
    Min. shear reinforcement\(\dfrac{0.87 \times 415 \times 157.08}{0.4 \times 300} = 472.6\) mm

    Calculated \(s_v = 101.16\) mm governs (lowest value). Rounded to nearest integer: 101 mm.

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{s_v = 101 \text{ mm}}\] Accepted range: 100 to 102

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question:
Read the following statements relating to flexure of reinforced concrete beams:

I. In over-reinforced sections, the failure strain in concrete reaches earlier than the yield strain in steel.

II. In under-reinforced sections, steel reaches yielding at a load lower than the load at which the concrete reaches failure strain.

III. Over-reinforced beams are recommended in practice as compared to the under-reinforced beams.

IV. In balanced sections, the concrete reaches failure strain earlier than the yield strain in tensile steel.

Each of the above statements is either True or False.

Which one of the following combinations is correct?
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Flexure Analysis (Beam Behavior)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Understanding failure modes in RC beams)
  • Given Data: Four statements about flexural behavior of RC beams.
  • Aim: Identify which combination of True/False is correct.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 Provisions (Section 38 — Limit State of Collapse: Flexure):

Beam TypeDefinitionFailure CharacterDuctility
Under-reinforced\(x_u < x_{u,max}\)Steel yields first, then concrete crushesDuctile (desirable)
Balanced\(x_u = x_{u,max}\)Steel yields and concrete crushes simultaneouslyLimited ductility
Over-reinforced\(x_u > x_{u,max}\)Concrete crushes before steel yieldsBrittle (undesirable)

Key Strain Values (IS 456:2000): Max concrete strain at failure: \(\varepsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\) (Clause 38.1).

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

StatementAnalysisVerdict
I. In over-reinforced sections, concrete failure strain is reached before steel yields.Over-reinforced: \(x_u > x_{u,max}\). Concrete reaches \(\varepsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\) while steel strain \(\varepsilon_s < \varepsilon_{sy}\). Concrete fails first.TRUE
II. In under-reinforced sections, steel yields at a lower load than the load at which concrete reaches failure strain.Under-reinforced: steel yields first at lower load, concrete crushes at ultimate load.TRUE
III. Over-reinforced beams are recommended over under-reinforced beams.IS 456:2000 Clause 38.1 prohibits over-reinforced sections — they fail suddenly without warning. Under-reinforced sections are preferred for ductility.FALSE
IV. In balanced sections, concrete reaches failure strain earlier than steel yields.Balanced: both steel yielding and concrete crushing occur simultaneously. Neither is "earlier".FALSE

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: I (True), II (True), III (False), IV (False) | Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
For the square steel beam cross-section shown in the figure, the shape factor about z – z axis is S and the plastic moment capacity is Mp. Consider yield stress fy = 250 MPa and a = 100 mm.



The values of S and Mp (rounded-off to one decimal place) are
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Plastic Analysis of Cross-Sections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Cross-section: Square steel beam oriented diagonally (a diamond shape)
    • Side length \(a = 100 \text{ mm}\)
    • Yield stress \(f_y = 250 \text{ MPa}\)
  • Aim: Find the shape factor \(S\) about the z-z axis and the plastic moment capacity \(M_p\).

3. Core Concepts:

Shape Factor (\(S\)): Ratio of plastic section modulus to elastic section modulus: \(S = Z_p / Z_e\). It represents the reserve strength beyond initial yielding. For standard shapes: Diamond = 2.0, Rectangular = 1.5, Circular = 1.7.

Elastic Section Modulus (\(Z_e\)): Defined as \(I / y_{max}\).

Plastic Section Modulus (\(Z_p\)): Defined as \(\dfrac{A}{2}(\bar{y}_1 + \bar{y}_2)\), where \(\bar{y}_1, \bar{y}_2\) are the centroidal distances of the equal area halves from the plastic neutral axis.

Plastic Moment Capacity (\(M_p\)): As per IS 800:2007, \(M_p = Z_p \cdot f_y\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Derive/calculate \(Z_e\) for the diagonally oriented square.
  2. Derive/calculate \(Z_p\) using the geometric properties of the triangular halves.
  3. Calculate \(S = Z_p / Z_e\).
  4. Calculate \(M_p = Z_p \cdot f_y\) and convert units to kN·m.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Elastic Modulus (\(Z_e\)):
    Diagonal length \(d = a\sqrt{2}\).
    \[I_{zz} = \dfrac{a^4}{12} = \dfrac{100^4}{12} = \dfrac{10^8}{12} \text{ mm}^4 \]
    Distance to extreme fiber: \(y_{max} = \dfrac{d}{2} = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ mm}\)
    \[Z_e = \dfrac{I_{zz}}{y_{max}} = \dfrac{a^4/12}{a/\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{a^3\sqrt{2}}{12} = \dfrac{a^3}{6\sqrt{2}} \]
  2. Calculate Plastic Modulus (\(Z_p\)):
    The neutral axis bisects the square diagonally, creating two equal triangles.
    Area of one half (triangle) \(= \dfrac{a^2}{2}\).
    Centroid of each triangle from the neutral axis: \(\bar{y}_1 = \bar{y}_2 = \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{a}{3\sqrt{2}}\)
    \[Z_p = \dfrac{a^2}{2} \left(\dfrac{a}{3\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{a}{3\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{a^2}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2a}{3\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{a^3}{3\sqrt{2}} \]
    Numerical value: \(Z_p = \dfrac{100^3}{3\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1{,}000{,}000}{4.2426} = 235{,}702.26 \text{ mm}^3\)
  3. Calculate Shape Factor (\(S\)):
    \[S = \dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e} = \dfrac{a^3/(3\sqrt{2})}{a^3/(6\sqrt{2})} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2.0 \]
  4. Calculate Plastic Moment Capacity (\(M_p\)):
    \[M_p = Z_p \cdot f_y = 235{,}702.26 \text{ mm}^3 \times 250 \text{ N/mm}^2 = 58{,}925{,}565 \text{ N·mm} \]
    Convert to kN·m: \(58{,}925{,}565 \times 10^{-6} = 58.92 \text{ kN·m}\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(S = 2.0\), \(M_p = 58.9 \text{ kN·m}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: A post-tensioned concrete member of span 15 m and cross-section of 450 mm × 450 mm is prestressed with three steel tendons, each of cross-sectional area 200 mm². The tendons are tensioned one after another to a stress of 1500 MPa. All the tendons are straight and located at 125 mm from the bottom of the member. Assume the prestress to be the same in all tendons and the modular ratio to be 6. The average loss of prestress, due to elastic deformation of concrete, considering all three tendons is
questions.explanation:
Prestressed Concrete | Losses in Prestress

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Span \(L = 15 \text{ m}\)
    • Cross-section: \(b = 450 \text{ mm}\), \(D = 450 \text{ mm}\)
    • Number of tendons \(n = 3\)
    • Area of each tendon \(A_s = 200 \text{ mm}^2\)
    • Initial prestress in steel \(f_p = 1500 \text{ MPa}\)
    • Location of tendons = \(125 \text{ mm}\) from the bottom
    • Modular ratio \(m = 6\)
  • Aim: Determine the average loss of prestress due to elastic deformation of concrete for all three successively tensioned tendons.

3. Core Concepts:

Elastic Shortening Loss (IS 1343:2012): When tendons are tensioned sequentially, previously tensioned tendons undergo strain loss due to elastic shortening of concrete caused by subsequent tendons.

Note: Unless specified otherwise in GATE problems, elastic deformation is evaluated due to prestressing force only, neglecting dead load effects.

Initial Prestressing Force per Tendon: \(P = A_s \times f_p\)

Concrete Stress at Steel Level: \[f_c = \dfrac{P}{A} + \dfrac{P \cdot e^2}{I} \]

Average Elastic Shortening Loss: \[\Delta f_{avg} = \dfrac{1}{2}(n-1) \cdot m \cdot f_c \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate cross-sectional area (\(A\)) and moment of inertia (\(I\)) for the concrete section.
  2. Determine the eccentricity (\(e\)) of the tendons.
  3. Calculate the tensioning force per tendon (\(P\)).
  4. Evaluate concrete stress at the level of tendons (\(f_c\)) caused by pulling one tendon.
  5. Determine sequential losses:
    • Tendon 1 suffers loss from tensioning of Tendons 2 and 3.
    • Tendon 2 suffers loss from tensioning of Tendon 3.
    • Tendon 3 is pulled last — zero elastic shortening loss.
  6. Calculate the average of these losses.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Section Properties:
    \[A = 450 \times 450 = 202{,}500 \text{ mm}^2 \]
    \[I = \dfrac{450 \times 450^3}{12} = 3{,}417{,}187{,}500 \text{ mm}^4 \]
    Centroid from bottom: \(y_c = 225 \text{ mm}\)
    Eccentricity: \(e = 225 - 125 = 100 \text{ mm}\)
  2. Force and Concrete Stress:
    \[P = 1500 \times 200 = 300{,}000 \text{ N} \]
    \[f_c = \dfrac{300{,}000}{202{,}500} + \dfrac{300{,}000 \times 100^2}{3{,}417{,}187{,}500} \]
    \[f_c = 1.4815 + 0.8779 = 2.3594 \text{ MPa} \]
  3. Calculate Average Loss:
    Loss per subsequent tensioning event \(= m \cdot f_c = 6 \times 2.3594 = 14.156 \text{ MPa}\)
    TendonLoss (MPa)Reason
    Tendon 1\(2 \times 14.156 = 28.312\)Tendons 2 & 3 pulled after
    Tendon 2\(1 \times 14.156 = 14.156\)Tendon 3 pulled after
    Tendon 3\(0\)Pulled last

    \[\Delta f_{avg} = \dfrac{28.312 + 14.156 + 0}{3} = \dfrac{42.468}{3} = 14.156 \text{ MPa} \]
    Alternatively using the direct formula: \(\Delta f_{avg} = \dfrac{1}{2}(3-1) \times 6 \times 2.3594 = 14.156 \text{ MPa}\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14.16 MPa | Correct option: (A)

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Five activities A, B, C, D, E with durations 10, 12, 5, 14, 10 days respectively and specific preceding dependencies.
  • Aim: Calculate the total float of activity E in days.

3. Core Concepts:

Forward Pass: \(EFT_i = EST_i + \text{Duration}_i\) and \(EST_j = \max(EFT \text{ of all predecessors})\)

Backward Pass: \(LFT_i = \min(LST \text{ of all successors})\) and \(LST_i = LFT_i - \text{Duration}_i\)

Total Float: \(F_T = LST - EST\) or equivalently \(LFT - EFT\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Forward Pass to compute EST and EFT for all activities.
  2. Determine project completion time.
  3. Backward Pass to compute LFT and LST.
  4. Compute total float for activity E.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Forward Pass:

    B12—012
    C5A1015
    D14B1226
    E10B, C\(\max(12, 15) = 15\)25
  2. Project Duration:
    \[T = \max(EFT_D,\, EFT_E) = \max(26, 25) = 26 \text{ days} \]
  3. Backward Pass (terminal activities):
    \(LFT_D = 26 \Rightarrow LST_D = 26 - 14 = 12\)
    \(LFT_E = 26 \Rightarrow LST_E = 26 - 10 = 16\)
  4. Total Float of Activity E:
    \[F_{T(E)} = LST_E - EST_E = 16 - 15 = 1 \text{ day} \]
    Check: \(LFT_E - EFT_E = 26 - 25 = 1\) ✓

Final Answer: 1 day | Accepted key range: 1 to 1

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: Gypsum is typically added in cement to
questions.explanation:
Building Materials | Concrete Technology

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Gypsum added to cement.
  • Aim: Identify the primary chemical purpose of this addition.

3. Core Concepts:

Bogue's Compounds: Cement clinker contains \(C_3A\) (Tricalcium aluminate), which reacts violently and rapidly with water.

Flash Set: Premature stiffening caused by rapid hydration of \(C_3A\) with immense heat evolution.

Retardation by Gypsum: Gypsum (\(CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O\)) is interground with clinker (~3–5%). It reacts with \(C_3A\) to form an insoluble coating of ettringite (calcium sulphoaluminate) over cement grains, temporarily delaying further hydration and preventing flash/quick setting.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • Option (B) "enhance hardening": Incorrect — \(C_3S\) and \(C_2S\) dictate hardening/strength.
  • Option (C) "increase workability": Incorrect — plasticizers and admixtures control this.
  • Option (D) "decrease heat of hydration": Incorrect — low \(C_3A\) and \(C_3S\) proportions achieve this.
  • Option (A) "prevent quick setting": Correct — gypsum retards \(C_3A\)'s violent reaction, preventing flash/quick setting.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Prevent quick setting  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.question: The direct and indirect costs estimated by a contractor for bidding a project is ₹160000 and ₹20000 respectively. If the mark up applied is 10% of the bid price, the quoted price (in ₹) of the contractor is
questions.explanation:
Construction Planning & Management | Cost Estimation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Direct Cost (\(DC\)) = ₹1,60,000
    • Indirect Cost (\(IC\)) = ₹20,000
    • Markup = 10% of the bid price
  • Aim: Calculate the quoted bid price.

3. Core Concepts:

Total Estimated Cost (\(TC\)): Sum of direct and indirect costs.

Bid Price (\(B\)):\[B = TC + \text{Markup} \]Since markup is expressed as a percentage of the bid price (not cost), \(B\) appears on both sides of the equation.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate total cost \(TC = DC + IC\).
  2. Express markup as \(0.10 \times B\) and form an algebraic equation.
  3. Solve for \(B\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Total Cost\[TC = 1{,}60{,}000 + 20{,}000 = 1{,}80{,}000 \text{ ₹} \]
  2. Step 2: Bid Price Equation\[B = TC + 0.10 \times B = 1{,}80{,}000 + 0.10B \]
  3. Step 3: Solve for \(B\)\[B - 0.10B = 1{,}80{,}000 \implies 0.90B = 1{,}80{,}000 \]\[B = \dfrac{1{,}80{,}000}{0.90} = 2{,}00{,}000 \text{ ₹} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: ₹2,00,000  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.question:
Contractor X is developing his bidding strategy against Contractor Y. The ratio of Y's bid price to X's cost for the 30 previous bids in which Contractor X has competed against Contractor Y is given in the Table

Ratio of Y's bid price to X's costNumber of bids
1.026
1.0412
1.063
1.106
1.123

Based on the bidding behaviour of the Contractor Y, the probability of winning against Contractor Y at a mark up of 8% for the next project is
questions.explanation:
Construction Management | Bidding Strategy & Probability

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Competitor bids data: Ratio of Contractor Y's bid price to Contractor X's cost.
    • Total number of historical bids = \(6 + 12 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 30\)
    • Contractor X's mark-up for the next project = \(8\%\) of cost.
  • Aim: Calculate the probability of Contractor X winning the bid against Contractor Y.

3. Core Concepts:

Winning Criterion: In a standard competitive bidding process, the contractor with the lowest bid wins. Thus, Contractor X wins if \(\text{Bid}_X < \text{Bid}_Y\).

Bid Formulation: \(\text{Bid} = \text{Cost} + \text{Markup}\)

Probability Calculation: \[P(\text{X wins}) = \dfrac{\text{Number of favorable events (where X's bid} < \text{Y's bid)}}{\text{Total number of events}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the ratio of Contractor X's bid to X's cost at an \(8\%\) markup.
  2. Formulate the winning condition in terms of the ratio \(\dfrac{\text{Bid}_Y}{\text{Cost}_X}\).
  3. Count the historical occurrences from the given table where this condition is satisfied.
  4. Compute the probability percentage and select the matching option.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate Contractor X's Bid.\[\text{Bid}_X = \text{Cost}_X + (0.08 \times \text{Cost}_X) = 1.08 \times \text{Cost}_X \]
  2. Step 2: Formulate the winning condition. For X to win, \(\text{Bid}_X < \text{Bid}_Y\).\[1.08 \times \text{Cost}_X < \text{Bid}_Y \]Dividing both sides by \(\text{Cost}_X\):\[\dfrac{\text{Bid}_Y}{\text{Cost}_X} > 1.08 \]
  3. Step 3: Analyze the historical data to find favorable outcomes (ratio strictly greater than \(1.08\)).
    Ratio \(\dfrac{\text{Bid}_Y}{\text{Cost}_X}\)Number of BidsCondition Met?
    1.026No
    1.0412No
    1.063No
    1.106Yes
    1.123Yes
    Favorable bids \(= 6 + 3 = 9\) bids.
  4. Step 4: Compute probability.\[P(\text{X wins}) = \dfrac{9}{30} = 0.30 \text{ or } 30\% \]
  5. Step 5: Evaluate options. \(30\%\) is greater than \(0\%\) but less than \(50\%\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(30\%\)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures

questions.question:
A prismatic cantilever prestressed concrete beam of span length, \( L = 1.5 \) m has one straight tendon placed in the cross-section as shown in the following figure (not to scale). The total prestressing force of 50 kN in the tendon is applied at \( d_c = 50 \) mm from the top in the cross-section of width, \( b = 200 \) mm and depth, \( d = 300 \) mm.



If the concentrated load, \( P = 5 \) kN, the resultant stress (in MPa, in integer) experienced at point 'Q' will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Design of Concrete Structures | Prestressed Concrete

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Beam type: Cantilever, Span \(L = 1.5\text{ m}\) (fixed end on the left)
    • Cross-section: \(b = 200\text{ mm}\), \(d = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • Tendon location: \(d_c = 50\text{ mm}\) from the top fiber
    • Prestressing force \((P_0)\) = \(50\text{ kN}\)
    • External load \((P)\) = \(5\text{ kN}\) concentrated at the free end
    • Point Q: Located at the top fiber of the fixed support (maximum moment location)
  • Aim: Find the resultant longitudinal stress at point Q in MPa.

3. Core Concepts:

Sign Convention: Compression is Positive (+), Tension is Negative (−). (Standard IS 1343 convention for prestressed concrete).

Cross-sectional Properties: Area \(A = b \times d\)    Section Modulus \(Z = \dfrac{bd^2}{6}\)

Stress due to Prestress (\(P_0\)):

  • Axial compression \(= +\dfrac{P_0}{A}\)
  • The tendon is above the neutral axis (eccentricity \(e\)), creating an internal moment \(M_p = P_0 \times e\) that bends the beam upwards, putting top fibers in additional compression.

Stress due to External Load (\(P\)):

  • Downward point load on a cantilever creates a hogging moment at the support (\(M_e = P \times L\)).
  • Hogging moment puts the top fibers in tension.

Superposition Principle: \(\sigma_{\text{Resultant}} = \sigma_{\text{Axial}} + \sigma_{\text{Bending (Prestress)}} + \sigma_{\text{Bending (External)}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate cross-sectional properties (\(A, Z\)).
  2. Determine eccentricity (\(e\)) of the tendon from the Neutral Axis.
  3. Calculate stresses at the top fiber at the fixed support due to prestress.
  4. Calculate stresses at the same point due to the external load.
  5. Sum the stresses to find the resultant. (Self-weight neglected as concrete density is not provided.)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Section Properties\[A = 200 \times 300 = 60{,}000\text{ mm}^2 \]\[Z_{top} = \dfrac{200 \times 300^2}{6} = 3{,}000{,}000\text{ mm}^3 = 3 \times 10^6\text{ mm}^3 \]Distance of Neutral Axis from top \(= \dfrac{d}{2} = 150\text{ mm}\)
    Eccentricity \(e = 150 - 50 = 100\text{ mm}\) (above NA)
  2. Step 2: Stresses due to Prestressing at Top Fiber (Point Q)
    Direct stress:\[+\dfrac{P_0}{A} = +\dfrac{50 \times 10^3}{60{,}000} = +0.833\text{ MPa} \]Prestress moment: \(M_p = P_0 \times e = 50 \times 10^3 \times 100 = 5 \times 10^6\text{ N·mm}\)
    Bending stress due to \(M_p\):\[+\dfrac{M_p}{Z} = +\dfrac{5 \times 10^6}{3 \times 10^6} = +1.667\text{ MPa} \]Total prestress stress at Q \(= 0.833 + 1.667 = +2.500\text{ MPa}\) (Compression)
  3. Step 3: Stresses due to External Load at Top Fiber (Point Q)
    Bending moment at fixed end: \(M_e = P \times L = 5 \times 1.5 = 7.5\text{ kN·m} = 7.5 \times 10^6\text{ N·mm}\)
    Bending stress due to \(M_e\):\[-\dfrac{M_e}{Z} = -\dfrac{7.5 \times 10^6}{3 \times 10^6} = -2.500\text{ MPa (Tension)} \]
  4. Step 4: Resultant Stress\[\sigma_{\text{Resultant}} = (+2.500) + (-2.500) = 0\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0 MPa  |  Accepted key range: 0 to 0

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
A column is subjected to a total load (P) of 60 kN supported through a bracket connection, as shown in the figure (not to scale).



The resultant force in bolt R (in kN, round off to one decimal place) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Eccentric Bolted Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Total applied load, \(P = 60\text{ kN}\)
    • Arrangement: 2 columns of 3 bolts each. Total bolts, \(n = 6\)
    • Pitch, \(p = 30\text{ mm}\) (vertical distance between bolts)
    • Gauge, \(g = 40 + 40 = 80\text{ mm}\) (horizontal distance between bolt columns)
  • Aim: Find the resultant force in bolt R (middle bolt in the right column) in kN.
  • Sanity Check & Correction Note: Visual Ambiguity: The left witness line for the \(100\text{ mm}\) dimension appears to align with the right column of bolts. If taken literally, the eccentricity from the CG would be \(140\text{ mm}\), leading to an answer outside the official key. Matching the official range (27.0–29.0 kN) requires \(100\text{ mm}\) to be the eccentricity \(e\) measured directly from the Center of Gravity (CG) of the bolt group. We proceed with \(e = 100\text{ mm}\) from the CG.

3. Core Concepts:

According to the Elastic Method for in-plane eccentric connections (IS 800:2007):

  • Direct Shear Force (\(F_D\)): Primary load shared equally among all bolts.\[F_D = \dfrac{P}{n} \]
  • Torsional Shear Force (\(F_T\)): Moment \(M = P \times e\) causes a rotational force on each bolt proportional to its radial distance \(r\) from the CG.\[F_T = \dfrac{M \times r}{\sum r^2} \]
  • Resultant Force (\(F_R\)): Vector addition of \(F_D\) and \(F_T\).

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate \(\sum r^2\)
    The CG of the 6-bolt group is exactly midway between the two columns and the middle row.
    • 4 Corner bolts: \(x = \pm 40\text{ mm}\), \(y = \pm 30\text{ mm}\)\[r_{\text{corner}}^2 = 40^2 + 30^2 = 1600 + 900 = 2500\text{ mm}^2 \]
    • 2 Middle bolts (including Bolt R): \(x = \pm 40\text{ mm}\), \(y = 0\)\[r_{\text{mid}}^2 = 40^2 + 0^2 = 1600\text{ mm}^2 \]
    \[\sum r^2 = 4(2500) + 2(1600) = 10000 + 3200 = 13200\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate Direct Shear (\(F_D\))\[F_D = \dfrac{60\text{ kN}}{6} = 10\text{ kN} \]Direction: Downward (parallel to \(P\)).
  3. Step 3: Calculate Torsional Shear on Bolt R (\(F_T\))
    Bolt R is at the middle-right position with radial distance \(r = 40\text{ mm}\).
    Moment: \(M = P \times e = 60\text{ kN} \times 100\text{ mm} = 6000\text{ kN·mm}\)\[F_T = \dfrac{6000 \times 40}{13200} = \dfrac{240000}{13200} = 18.18\text{ kN} \]Direction: A downward load \(P\) on the right side causes a clockwise moment. For bolt R on the positive x-axis, clockwise rotation induces a strictly downward tangential force.
  4. Step 4: Calculate Resultant Force (\(F_R\))
    Since both \(F_D\) and \(F_T\) act vertically downward on Bolt R:\[F_R = F_D + F_T = 10 + 18.18 = 28.18\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 28.2 kN  |  Accepted key range: 27.0 to 29.0

questions.question:
A prismatic steel beam is shown in the figure.



The plastic moment, \( M_p \) calculated for the collapse mechanism using static method and kinematic method is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Plastic Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A prismatic, simply supported steel beam of length \(L\) (\(L/3 + 2L/3\)) loaded with a point load \(P\) at point B.
  • Aim: To find the relationship between the plastic moment capacities \(M_p\) obtained through the static (equilibrium) method and the kinematic (mechanism) method.

3. Core Concepts:

Statically Determinate Beams: The bending moment diagram is independent of section properties.

Static Method (Lower Bound Theorem): Provides the maximum load that can be safely supported without violating the yield criterion anywhere in the structure.

Kinematic Method (Upper Bound Theorem): Equates external work done by loads to internal work dissipated at plastic hinges during collapse.

Uniqueness Theorem (IS 800:2007 Annex B): If a structural mechanism satisfies equilibrium, yield conditions, and mechanism conditions simultaneously, the calculated collapse load is the exact true collapse load. Because a simply supported beam is determinate, formation of a single plastic hinge guarantees an exact solution, making \(M_{p,\text{static}} = M_{p,\text{kinematic}}\).

4. Solution Method:

Calculate \(M_p\) using both independent methods to mathematically verify their equivalency.

  1. Evaluate maximum internal bending moment statically.
  2. Set up virtual work formulation for collapse mechanism kinematically.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Static Method:
    Maximum bending moment occurs under the point load. Using standard statics for a simply supported beam with load \(P\) placed at distances \(a = L/3\) and \(b = 2L/3\):
    \[M_{\max} = \dfrac{P\,a\,b}{L} = \dfrac{P \cdot (L/3) \cdot (2L/3)}{L} = \dfrac{2PL}{9} \]At collapse, \(M_{\max}\) reaches the plastic moment \(M_p\):
    \[M_{p,\text{static}} = \dfrac{2PL}{9} \]
  2. Kinematic Method:
    Assuming a plastic hinge forms at B (under the load), let the virtual downward deflection at B be \(\delta\).
    Rotation at hinge A: \(\theta_A = \dfrac{\delta}{L/3} = \dfrac{3\delta}{L}\)
    Rotation at hinge C: \(\theta_C = \dfrac{\delta}{2L/3} = \dfrac{1.5\delta}{L}\)
    Rotation of the plastic hinge at B: \(\theta_B = \theta_A + \theta_C = \dfrac{4.5\delta}{L}\)
    Equating Internal Work (\(W_I\)) and External Work (\(W_E\)):
    \[W_I = W_E \implies M_p \cdot \theta_B = P \cdot \delta \]\[M_{p,\text{kinematic}} \cdot \left(\dfrac{4.5\delta}{L}\right) = P \cdot \delta \implies M_{p,\text{kinematic}} = \dfrac{PL}{4.5} = \dfrac{2PL}{9} \]
  3. Comparison:
    \[M_{p,\text{static}} = \dfrac{2PL}{9} = M_{p,\text{kinematic}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(M_{p,\text{static}} = \dfrac{2PL}{9} = M_{p,\text{kinematic}}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.question:
A rectangular cross-section of a reinforced concrete beam is shown in the figure. The diameter of each reinforcing bar is 16 mm. The values of modulus of elasticity of concrete and steel are 2.0×10⁴ MPa and 2.1×10⁵ MPa, respectively.



The distance of the centroidal axis from the centerline of the reinforcement (x) for the uncracked section (in mm, round off to one decimal place) is ______________
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) | Working Stress Method & Uncracked Sections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Width of beam (\(b\)): \(200\text{ mm}\)
    • Overall depth (\(D\)): \(350\text{ mm}\)
    • Effective cover to reinforcement: \(35\text{ mm}\)
    • Diameter of reinforcing bars (\(\phi\)): \(16\text{ mm}\)
    • Number of bars (\(n\)): \(3\)
    • Modulus of elasticity of concrete (\(E_c\)): \(2.0 \times 10^4\text{ MPa}\)
    • Modulus of elasticity of steel (\(E_s\)): \(2.1 \times 10^5\text{ MPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the distance of the centroidal axis from the centerline of the reinforcement (\(x\)) for the uncracked section (in mm).

Sanity Check & Correction: The "350 mm" dimension is interpreted as the overall total depth (\(D\)), giving effective depth \(d = 350 - 35 = 315\text{ mm}\). This yields \(x \approx 129.4\text{ mm}\), perfectly matching the official answer key.

3. Core Concepts:

Uncracked Section Analysis: Per IS 456 principles, both concrete in compression and tension are considered effective for the uncracked transformed section.

Modular Ratio (\(m\)): Used to convert steel area into an equivalent concrete area.\[m = \dfrac{E_s}{E_c} \]

Transformed Area: The equivalent additional area of concrete replacing the steel is \((m-1)A_{st}\).

Centroid:\[\bar{y} = \dfrac{\sum (A_i y_i)}{\sum A_i} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the area of steel reinforcement (\(A_{st}\)) and the modular ratio (\(m\)).
  2. Calculate the equivalent transformed area of steel \((m-1)A_{st}\).
  3. Find the depth of the centroidal axis from the top compression fiber (\(y_{top}\)).
  4. Subtract \(y_{top}\) from the effective depth (\(d\)) to find \(x\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute properties:\[m = \dfrac{2.1 \times 10^5}{2.0 \times 10^4} = 10.5 \]\[A_{st} = 3 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (16)^2 = 3 \times 201.062 = 603.186\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Equivalent areas and centroids (taking top fiber as reference \(y = 0\)):
    ComponentArea (mm²)Centroid from top (mm)
    Gross Concrete (\(A_c = b \times D\))\(200 \times 350 = 70{,}000\)\(350/2 = 175\)
    Transformed Steel (\(A_{eq} = (m-1)A_{st}\))\(9.5 \times 603.186 = 5730.267\)\(d = 315\)
  3. Centroidal axis from top (\(y_{top}\)):\[y_{top} = \dfrac{(70{,}000 \times 175) + (5730.267 \times 315)}{70{,}000 + 5730.267} = \dfrac{12{,}250{,}000 + 1{,}805{,}034}{75{,}730.267} = \dfrac{14{,}055{,}034}{75{,}730.267} = 185.593\text{ mm} \]
  4. Calculate \(x\):\[x = d - y_{top} = 315 - 185.593 = 129.407\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 129.4 mm | Accepted key range: 129.0 to 130.0

questions.question: An equipment has been purchased at an initial cost of ₹160000 and has an estimated salvage value of ₹10000. The equipment has an estimated life of 5 years. The difference between the book values (in ₹, in integer) obtained at the end of 4th year using straight line method and sum of years digit method of depreciation is ______________
questions.explanation:
Construction Management | Engineering Economics (Depreciation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Initial Cost (\(C_i\)): ₹ 1,60,000
    • Salvage Value (\(C_s\)): ₹ 10,000
    • Estimated Life (\(N\)): 5 years
  • Aim: Find the absolute difference between the Book Value (BV) at the end of the 4th year evaluated using the Straight Line Method (SLM) and the Sum of Years Digit Method (SYD).

3. Core Concepts:

Depreciable Amount (\(D\)): \(D = C_i - C_s\)

Straight Line Method (SLM): Depreciation is constant every year.\[ d_{SLM} = \frac{D}{N} \]

Sum of Years Digit Method (SYD): An accelerated depreciation technique.\[ S_N = \frac{N(N+1)}{2} \]\[ d_{SYD,\,m} = D \times \frac{N - m + 1}{S_N} \quad \text{(where } m \text{ is the specific year)} \]

Book Value (\(BV\)):\[ BV_m = C_i - \text{Cumulative Depreciation up to year } m \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the common Depreciable Amount (\(D\)).
  2. Compute the Book Value after 4 years using SLM.
  3. Compute the Book Value after 4 years using SYD.
  4. Subtract the two to find the absolute difference.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Depreciable Amount:\[ D = 160000 - 10000 = 150000 \text{ ₹} \]
  2. Book Value by SLM at End of Year 4:
    Annual depreciation: \(d_{SLM} = 150000 / 5 = \) ₹ 30,000
    Accumulated depreciation (4 years): \(4 \times 30000 = \) ₹ 1,20,000\[ BV_{SLM,\,4} = 160000 - 120000 = 40000\text{ ₹} \]
  3. Book Value by SYD at End of Year 4:
    Sum of digits: \(S_N = 5+4+3+2+1 = 15\)
    Year (\(m\))FractionDepreciation (₹)
    1\(5/15\)50,000
    2\(4/15\)40,000
    3\(3/15\)30,000
    4\(2/15\)20,000

    Accumulated depreciation (4 years): ₹ 50,000 + 40,000 + 30,000 + 20,000 = ₹ 1,40,000\[ BV_{SYD,\,4} = 160000 - 140000 = 20000 \text{ ₹} \]Shortcut check: Year 5 depreciation \(= 150000 \times \dfrac{1}{15} = \) ₹ 10,000. So \(BV_4 = C_s + d_5 = 10000 + 10000 = \) ₹ 20,000. ✓
  4. Absolute Difference:\[ \Delta BV = 40000 - 20000 = 20000 \text{ ₹} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: ₹ 20,000 | Accepted key range: 20000 to 20000

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A reinforcing steel bar, partially embedded in concrete, is subjected to a tensile force \(P\). The figure that appropriately represents the distribution of the magnitude of bond stress (represented as hatched region), along the embedded length of the bar, is
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Bond Stress Distribution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A single reinforcing bar partially embedded in concrete, subjected to axial pull \(P\).
  • Aim: Identify the theoretical distribution of bond stress along the embedded length.

3. Core Concepts:

Elastic Bond Theory: Bond stress (\(\tau_b\)) is directly proportional to the relative slip (\(s\)) between steel and concrete: \(\tau_b \propto s\).

Slip Distribution:

  • At the loaded end: Axial force in steel = maximum (\(P\)). Local strain and slip are at their peak → bond stress is maximum.
  • At the unloaded (embedded) end: Force fully transferred to concrete. Force in steel = 0, slip = 0 → bond stress is zero.
  • Intermediate region: Stress decays smoothly from maximum to zero following an exponential/hyperbolic pattern (solution to \(\dfrac{d^2s}{dx^2} \propto s\)).

4. Analysis of Options:

OptionDescriptionVerdict
(A)Bell curve — peak near the middle, zero at both ends❌ Applies to physical bond breakdown; not classical elastic theory
(B)Maximum stress at the unloaded end❌ Impossible — no force or slip at the embedded end
(C)Maximum at loaded end, decaying exponentially to zero at embedded end✓ Correct — matches elastic slip model
(D)Constant or bulging distribution❌ Incorrect

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Maximum bond stress at the loaded end, decaying to zero at the embedded end (exponential distribution). | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
The flange and web plates of the doubly symmetric built-up section are connected by continuous 10 mm thick fillet welds as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The moment of inertia of the section about its principal axis X-X is 7.73 × 10⁶ mm⁴. The permissible shear stress in the fillet welds is 100 N/mm². The design shear strength of the section is governed by the capacity of the fillet welds.



The maximum shear force (in kN, round off to one decimal place) that can be carried by the section, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Connections (Fillet Welds)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Cross-section: Built-up section with top/bottom flanges and two vertical web plates.
    • Flange dimensions: Width \(b = 100\) mm, Thickness \(t_f = 10\) mm.
    • Overall depth: \(D = 120\) mm.
    • Moment of inertia about NA: \(I_{xx} = 7.73 \times 10^6\) mm⁴.
    • Weld size: \(s = 10\) mm (continuous fillet welds).
    • Permissible weld shear stress: \(\tau_{vf} = 100\) N/mm².
    • Design criterion: Section capacity governed by fillet weld shear strength.
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum vertical shear force \(V\) (in kN) the built-up section can sustain.

3. Core Concepts:

Longitudinal Shear Flow (\(q\)): The horizontal shear force per unit length transferred between flange and web(s):\[q = \dfrac{V \cdot A\bar{y}}{I_{xx}} \]

Weld Shear Capacity (\(q_w\)): Total strength of continuous fillet welds per unit length:\[q_w = n \cdot t_e \cdot \tau_{vf} \]where \(n\) = number of continuous weld lines and \(t_e\) = effective throat thickness.

IS 800:2007 Provision: Effective throat thickness for standard 90° fusion welding: \(t_e = 0.7 \times s\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the number of weld lines \(n\) from the section diagram.
  2. Calculate effective throat thickness \(t_e\).
  3. Calculate the first moment of area (\(A\bar{y}\)) for the top flange about the neutral axis.
  4. Equate theoretical shear flow to total weld shear capacity and solve for \(V\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Weld Properties

  • Number of weld lines per flange: \(n = 4\) (each of the two web plates is welded on both inner and outer sides).
  • Effective throat thickness: \(t_e = 0.7 \times 10 = 7\) mm.
  • Total weld capacity per unit length:\[q_w = n \cdot t_e \cdot \tau_{vf} = 4 \times 7 \times 100 = 2800 \text{ N/mm} \]

Step 2: First Moment of Area (\(A\bar{y}\))

  • Area of top flange: \(A = 100 \times 10 = 1000\) mm².
  • Neutral axis at mid-depth: \(120 / 2 = 60\) mm from the top fiber.
  • Centroid of top flange: \(10/2 = 5\) mm from the top fiber.
  • Lever arm: \(\bar{y} = 60 - 5 = 55\) mm.\[A\bar{y} = 1000 \times 55 = 55000 \text{ mm}^3 \]

Step 3: Equate Shear Flow to Weld Capacity

\[\dfrac{V \cdot A\bar{y}}{I_{xx}} = q_w \]\[V = \dfrac{q_w \cdot I_{xx}}{A\bar{y}} = \dfrac{2800 \times 7.73 \times 10^6}{55000} \]\[V = 393527 \text{ N} \approx \mathbf{393.5 \text{ kN}} \]

Verification: Using \(t_e = 0.707 \times 10 = 7.07\) mm gives \(V \approx 397.4\) kN. Both values lie within the accepted GATE range, confirming the structural model of \(n = 4\) welds.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 393.5 kN | Accepted key range: 393.5 to 399.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q43

questions.question:
The singly reinforced concrete beam section shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale) is made of M25 grade concrete and Fe500 grade reinforcing steel. The total cross-sectional area of the tension steel is 942 mm².



As per Limit State Design of IS 456:2000, the design moment capacity (in kN.m, round off to two decimal places) of the beam section, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Cement Concrete | Limit State Design of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Width of beam: \(b = 300\) mm
    • Effective depth: \(d = 450\) mm
    • Area of tension steel: \(A_{st} = 942\) mm²
    • Concrete grade: M25 → \(f_{ck} = 25\) MPa
    • Steel grade: Fe500 → \(f_y = 500\) MPa
  • Aim: Calculate the design moment capacity \(M_u\) (in kN·m), rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Depth of Actual Neutral Axis (\(x_u\)): Equating total compressive force to total tensile force (IS 456:2000, Annex G):\[C = T \implies 0.36\, f_{ck}\, b\, x_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st} \]

Limiting Depth of Neutral Axis (\(x_{u,max}\)): For Fe500 steel (IS 456):\[x_{u,max} = 0.46\, d \]

Section Classification & Moment of Resistance: If \(x_u < x_{u,max}\), the section is under-reinforced (failure initiated by steel yielding):\[M_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\, x_u) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the actual depth of the neutral axis (\(x_u\)).
  2. Compute the limiting depth (\(x_{u,max}\)) and compare to classify the section.
  3. Calculate the design moment capacity (\(M_u\)) using the appropriate lever arm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Actual Depth of Neutral Axis (\(x_u\))

\[x_u = \dfrac{0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}}{0.36\, f_{ck}\, b} = \dfrac{0.87 \times 500 \times 942}{0.36 \times 25 \times 300} = \dfrac{409770}{2700} = 151.767 \text{ mm} \]

Step 2: Limiting Depth of Neutral Axis (\(x_{u,max}\))

\[x_{u,max} = 0.46 \times 450 = 207 \text{ mm} \]

Since \(x_u = 151.767\) mm \(< x_{u,max} = 207\) mm → Section is under-reinforced.

Step 3: Design Moment Capacity (\(M_u\))

\[M_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\, x_u) \]\[= 409770 \times (450 - 0.42 \times 151.767) \]\[= 409770 \times (450 - 63.742) \]\[= 409770 \times 386.258 \text{ N·mm} \]\[= 158{,}276{,}934 \text{ N·mm} = \mathbf{158.28 \text{ kN·m}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 158.28 kN·m | Accepted key range: 158.00 to 158.60

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q44

questions.question: A simply supported prismatic concrete beam of rectangular cross-section, having a span of 8 m, is prestressed with an effective prestressing force of 600 kN. The eccentricity of the prestressing tendon is zero at supports and varies linearly to a value of e at the mid-span. In order to balance an external concentrated load of 12 kN applied at the mid-span, the required value of e (in mm, round off to the nearest integer) of the tendon, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Prestressed Concrete | Load Balancing Concept

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Span: \(L = 8\) m \(= 8000\) mm
    • Effective prestressing force: \(P = 600\) kN
    • Tendon profile: Linear (V-shaped) — eccentricity 0 at supports and \(e\) at mid-span.
    • External concentrated load at mid-span: \(W = 12\) kN
  • Aim: Find the eccentricity \(e\) (in mm) required to perfectly balance the external load \(W\).

3. Core Concepts:

Load Balancing Concept: A prestressing tendon with a sharp V-profile at mid-span creates an equivalent upward concentrated load \(W_p\) that counters external downward point loads:\[W_p = \dfrac{4Pe}{L} \]To balance the external load, set \(W_p = W\).

4. Solution Method:

Equate the equivalent upward prestress load to the external concentrated load and solve for the unknown eccentricity \(e\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Set up the load-balancing equation

\[W = \dfrac{4Pe}{L} \]

Step 2: Solve for \(e\)

\[12 = \dfrac{4 \times 600 \times e}{8000} = \dfrac{2400\,e}{8000} = 0.3\,e \]\[e = \dfrac{12}{0.3} = \mathbf{40 \text{ mm}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 40 mm | Accepted key range: 39 to 41

questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: The ratio of the plastic moment capacity of a beam section to its yield moment capacity is termed as
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Design of Steel Structures

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Ratio = \(\dfrac{\text{Plastic moment capacity}}{\text{Yield moment capacity}}\)
  • Aim: Match this ratio to the correct technical term.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Yield Moment: \(M_y = Z_e \cdot f_y\) (onset of yielding at extreme fibers)
  • Plastic Moment: \(M_p = Z_p \cdot f_y\) (entire cross-section yielded)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

\[\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{M_p}{M_y} = \dfrac{Z_p \cdot f_y}{Z_e \cdot f_y} = \dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e} \]

By definition, the ratio \(\dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e}\) is the Shape Factor (\(\nu\)).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Shape Factor | Correct option: (C)
