questions.question: The maximum applied load on a cylindrical concrete specimen of diameter 150 mm and length 300 mm tested as per the split tensile strength test guidelines of IS 5816:1999 is 157 kN. The split tensile strength (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) of the specimen is _________.
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Testing of Concrete | Split Tensile Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Diameter of specimen, \(d = 150\text{ mm}\)
    • Length of specimen, \(L = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • Maximum applied load, \(P = 157\text{ kN}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the split tensile strength in MPa.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 5816:1999 Formula: \[f_{ct} = \dfrac{2P}{\pi d L} \] where \(P\) is in Newtons and dimensions are in mm, yielding \(\mathrm{N/mm^2 = MPa}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Unit Conversion: \(P = 157\text{ kN} = 157{,}000\text{ N}\)
  2. Denominator: \[\pi \times 150 \times 300 = 45{,}000\pi \approx 141{,}371.67\text{ mm}^2 \]
  3. Split Tensile Strength: \[f_{ct} = \dfrac{2 \times 157{,}000}{141{,}371.67} \approx 2.221\text{ MPa} \approx 2.2\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.2 MPa | Accepted key range: 2.0 to 2.4

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question:
A concrete beam of span 15 m, 150 mm wide and 350 mm deep is prestressed with a parabolic cable as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). Coefficient of friction for the cable is 0.35, and coefficient of wave effect is 0.0015 per meter.



If the cable is tensioned from one end only, the percentage loss (round off to one decimal place) in the cable force due to friction, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Prestressed Concrete (Losses)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Span of beam, \(L = 15\text{ m}\)
    • Cross-section: Width \(b = 150\text{ mm}\), Depth \(d = 350\text{ mm}\)
    • Eccentricity at supports, \(e_1 = 50\text{ mm} = 0.05\text{ m}\) (above centroid)
    • Eccentricity at midspan, \(e_2 = 70\text{ mm} = 0.07\text{ m}\) (below centroid)
    • Coefficient of friction, \(\mu = 0.35\)
    • Wave effect coefficient, \(k = 0.0015\text{ /m}\)
    • Tensioning condition: Jacked from one end only
  • Aim: Find the percentage loss in cable force due to friction and wave effect.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 1343:2012 Provisions: Loss of prestress due to friction at distance \(x\) from the jacking end: \[P_x = P_0\, e^{-(\mu\alpha + kx)} \] For small values of \((\mu\alpha + kx)\), this simplifies to: \[\text{Loss} = P_0(\mu\alpha + kx) \]

Percentage Loss: \[\%\text{ Loss} = (\mu\alpha + kx) \times 100 \]

Parabolic Profile Geometry: Total dip \(h = e_1 + e_2\). Slope at supports: \(\theta = \dfrac{4h}{L}\). Total cumulative angle change: \(\alpha = 2\theta\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the total vertical dip (\(h\)) of the parabolic cable.
  2. Calculate the slope (\(\theta\)) at the support using parabolic geometry.
  3. Compute the total angular change (\(\alpha\)) over the entire span.
  4. Apply the simplified frictional loss formula over distance \(x = L\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Calculate Total Dip (\(h\))

\[h = e_1 + e_2 = 50 + 70 = 120\text{ mm} = 0.12\text{ m} \]

Step 2: Calculate Slope at Supports (\(\theta\))

\[\theta = \dfrac{4h}{L} = \dfrac{4 \times 0.12}{15} = \dfrac{0.48}{15} = 0.032\text{ radians} \]

Step 3: Calculate Cumulative Angle Change (\(\alpha\))
The tangent goes from \(+\theta\) at the jacking end to \(-\theta\) at the far end:

\[\alpha = 2\theta = 2 \times 0.032 = 0.064\text{ radians} \]

Step 4: Calculate Percentage Loss (using \(x = L = 15\text{ m}\))

Loss ComponentFormulaValue
Frictional Loss Factor\(\mu\alpha = 0.35 \times 0.064\)0.0224
Wobble Loss Factor\(kL = 0.0015 \times 15\)0.0225
Total Loss Factor\(\mu\alpha + kL\)0.0449
\[\%\text{ Loss} = 0.0449 \times 100 = 4.49\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.49% | Accepted key range: 3.8 to 4.7

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question:
The cross-section of the reinforced concrete beam having an effective depth of 500 mm is shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The grades of concrete and steel used are M35 and Fe550, respectively. The area of tension reinforcement is 400 mm². It is given that corresponding to 0.2% proof stress, the material safety factor is 1.15 and the yield strain of Fe550 steel is 0.0044.



As per IS 456:2000, the limiting depth (in mm, round off to the nearest integer) of the neutral axis measured from the extreme compression fiber, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Limit State Design of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Effective depth of beam, \(d = 500\text{ mm}\)
    • Concrete Grade: M35 (\(f_{ck} = 35\text{ MPa}\))
    • Steel Grade: Fe550 (\(f_y = 550\text{ MPa}\))
    • Area of tension reinforcement, \(A_{st} = 400\text{ mm}^2\)
    • Material safety factor for steel, \(\gamma_{ms} = 1.15\)
    • Yield strain of Fe550 steel, \(\epsilon_{su} = 0.0044\)
  • Aim: Determine the limiting depth of the neutral axis (\(x_{u,max}\)) from the extreme compression fiber, rounded to the nearest integer.

3. Core Concepts:

According to IS 456:2000 (Annex G), the limit state of collapse in flexure assumes that plane sections remain plane, resulting in a linear strain profile.

  • Maximum compressive strain in concrete at the outermost fiber: \(\epsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\)
  • The limiting (balanced) depth \(x_{u,max}\) occurs when \(\epsilon_{cu}\) and \(\epsilon_{su}\) are reached simultaneously.

Using similar triangles on the linear strain diagram: \[\dfrac{x_{u,max}}{d - x_{u,max}} = \dfrac{\epsilon_{cu}}{\epsilon_{su}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Establish \(\epsilon_{cu}\) and \(\epsilon_{su}\).
  2. Set up the similar triangles equation from the strain profile at the limiting state.
  3. Solve for \(x_{u,max}\) and substitute \(d = 500\text{ mm}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Identify Strains

  • Concrete extreme fiber strain: \(\epsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\)
  • Steel design yield strain (given): \(\epsilon_{su} = 0.0044\)

Step 2: Apply Strain Compatibility

\[\dfrac{x_{u,max}}{0.0035} = \dfrac{500 - x_{u,max}}{0.0044} \]

Step 3: Solve for \(x_{u,max}\)

\[0.0044 \cdot x_{u,max} = 0.0035 \cdot (500 - x_{u,max}) \] \[0.0044 \cdot x_{u,max} = 1.75 - 0.0035 \cdot x_{u,max} \] \[(0.0044 + 0.0035) \cdot x_{u,max} = 1.75 \] \[0.0079 \cdot x_{u,max} = 1.75 \] \[x_{u,max} = \dfrac{1.75}{0.0079} = 221.52\text{ mm} \]

Step 4: Rounding
Rounding to the nearest integer: \(x_{u,max} = 222\text{ mm}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 222 mm | Accepted key range: 220 to 224

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
Two steel plates are lap jointed in a workshop using 6 mm thick fillet weld as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The ultimate strength of the weld is 410 MPa.



As per Limit State Design of IS 800:2007, the design capacity (in kN, round off to three decimal places) of the welded connection, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Connections (Welding)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Joint Type: Lap joint (two steel plates)
    • Weld Type: Fillet weld (wrap-around on 3 sides)
    • Size of weld, \(s = 6\text{ mm}\)
    • Location: Workshop (shop weld \(\Rightarrow \gamma_{mw} = 1.25\))
    • Ultimate strength of weld, \(f_u = 410\text{ MPa}\)
    • Weld segment lengths: Top = \(200\text{ mm}\), Vertical = \(120\text{ mm}\), Bottom = \(200\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Find the design capacity of the welded connection in kN, rounded to three decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007 (Clause 10.5):

  • Effective throat thickness: \(t_t = K \cdot s\). For a standard \(90^\circ\) fusion angle, \(K = 0.7\).
  • Design shear strength of fillet weld: \(f_{wd} = \dfrac{f_u}{\sqrt{3} \cdot \gamma_{mw}}\)
  • Total design capacity: \(P_{dw} = L_w \cdot t_t \cdot f_{wd}\), where \(L_w\) is the total effective length.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the effective throat thickness (\(t_t\)).
  2. Calculate the total effective length of the weld (\(L_w\)).
  3. Calculate the design strength of the weld material (\(f_{wd}\)).
  4. Compute the total capacity in Newtons and convert to kN.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Throat Thickness (\(t_t\))

\[t_t = 0.7 \times 6 = 4.2\text{ mm} \]

Step 2: Effective Length (\(L_w\))

\[L_w = 200\text{ (top)} + 120\text{ (vertical)} + 200\text{ (bottom)} = 520\text{ mm} \]

Step 3: Design Strength of Weld (\(f_{wd}\))

\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{410}{\sqrt{3} \times 1.25} = \dfrac{410}{2.16506} \approx 189.3705\text{ N/mm}^2 \]

Step 4: Design Capacity (\(P_{dw}\))

\[P_{dw} = L_w \times t_t \times f_{wd} = 520 \times 4.2 \times 189.3705 \] \[P_{dw} = 2184 \times 189.3705 = 413{,}583.6\text{ N} = 413.584\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 413.584 kN | Accepted key range: 410.000 to 420.000

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q8
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: Assuming that there is no possibility of shear buckling in the web, the maximum reduction permitted by IS 800-2007 in the (low-shear) design bending strength of a semi-compact steel section due to high shear is
options: governed by the area of the flange

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: governed by the area of the flange
structuredOptions.html: governed by the area of the flange

questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Design of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Cross-section: Semi-compact steel section
    • Shear state: High shear (\(V > 0.6V_d\))
  • Aim: Find the maximum reduction permitted by IS 800:2007 in the design bending strength due to high shear.

3. Core Concepts:

  • IS 800:2007 (Clause 8.2.1.2 & 8.2.1.3): High shear force reduces the moment-carrying capacity of a section because the web must simultaneously carry substantial shear and bending stresses.
  • High shear condition: \(V > 0.6V_d\), where \(V_d\) is the design shear strength.
  • For Plastic and Compact sections, design bending strength \(M_d\) is reduced using: \(M_{dv} = M_d - \beta(M_d - M_{fd})\)
  • For Semi-compact sections, bending strength relies strictly on elastic extreme fiber yielding (\(M_d = Z_e f_y / \gamma_{m0}\)). They do not develop a plastic hinge — IS 800 does not mandate the interaction formula reduction for semi-compact sections.

4. Solution Method:

Check the specific provision of IS 800:2007 regarding semi-compact sections under combined bending and high shear.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. The problem states the section is semi-compact.
  2. Under low shear (\(V \le 0.6V_d\)): bending strength \(= Z_e f_y / \gamma_{m0}\).
  3. Under high shear (\(V > 0.6V_d\)): IS 800:2007 Clause 8.2.1.3 limits application of reduction factor \(\beta\) to plastic and compact sections only.
  4. Since a semi-compact section fails by elastic yielding before plastic mechanism formation, its capacity is fundamentally elastic.
  5. IS 800 prescribes no high-shear reduction formula for semi-compact sections \(\implies\) allowable reduction = 0%.

6. Final Answer:

Maximum reduction = Zero | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q9
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: In the reinforced beam section shown in the figure (not drawn to scale), the nominal cover provided at the bottom of the beam as per IS 456-2000, is
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Detailing of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Distance from bottom concrete face to centroid of main reinforcement = 50 mm
    • Main tension reinforcement: 3 bars of 16 mm diameter (\(\phi_{main} = 16\) mm)
    • Stirrups: 2-legged, 12 mm diameter @ 90 mm c/c (\(\phi_{stirrup} = 12\) mm)
  • Aim: Calculate the nominal cover provided at the bottom of the beam.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Nominal Cover (IS 456:2000, Clause 26.4.1): Distance from the extreme outer concrete surface to the outermost surface of reinforcing steel (links, stirrups, or main bars — whichever is outermost).
  • Effective Cover: Distance from the extreme outer concrete surface to the centroid of the main tension reinforcement.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the effective cover from the given data.
  2. Subtract the radius of the main bar to find the clear distance to the bottom of the main bar.
  3. Subtract the stirrup diameter (since stirrup wraps around main bar) to find the clear cover to outermost steel.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effective Cover \((d_{eff}) = 50\) mm
  2. Radius of main bar: \(r_{main} = \dfrac{16}{2} = 8\) mm
  3. Distance from bottom face to bottommost edge of main bar:\[C_{main} = d_{eff} - r_{main} = 50 - 8 = 42\text{ mm} \]
  4. The stirrup encloses the main bars and sits between them and the bottom concrete face. Outer dimension of stirrup \(= \phi_{stirrup} = 12\) mm.
  5. Nominal Cover:\[C_{nom} = C_{main} - \phi_{stirrup} = 42 - 12 = 30\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Nominal Cover \(= 30\) mm | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: If the section shown in the figure turns from fully-elastic to fully-plastic, the depth of neutral axis (N.A.), \( \bar{y} \), decreases by
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Bending of Beams (Plastic Analysis)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    • T-section with top Flange: \(60\text{ mm} \times 5\text{ mm}\)
    • Web: \(5\text{ mm} \times 60\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Determine the decrease in the depth of the neutral axis (\(\bar{y}\)) from the top fiber when the section transitions from fully-elastic to fully-plastic.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Elastic Neutral Axis (E.N.A.): Passes through the centroid of the cross-section.
  • Plastic Neutral Axis (P.N.A.): Divides the total cross-sectional area into two equal halves (Equal Area Axis) under pure bending without axial load.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the total cross-sectional area.
  2. Find the depth of the E.N.A. by calculating the centroidal distance from the top fiber.
  3. Find the depth of the P.N.A. by locating the axis that bisects the total area.
  4. Subtract the P.N.A. depth from the E.N.A. depth to find the decrease.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Area Calculations

  • Flange Area \((A_1) = 60\text{ mm} \times 5\text{ mm} = 300\text{ mm}^2\)
  • Web Area \((A_2) = 5\text{ mm} \times 60\text{ mm} = 300\text{ mm}^2\)
  • Total Area \((A) = A_1 + A_2 = 600\text{ mm}^2\)

Step 2: Depth of Elastic Neutral Axis (\(\bar{y}_e\))

Taking moments of area about the top edge (\(y = 0\)):

  • Centroid of flange: \(y_1 = 5/2 = 2.5\text{ mm}\)
  • Centroid of web: \(y_2 = 5 + (60/2) = 35\text{ mm}\)
\[\bar{y}_e = \dfrac{A_1 y_1 + A_2 y_2}{A} = \dfrac{(300 \times 2.5) + (300 \times 35)}{600} = \dfrac{750 + 10500}{600} = \dfrac{11250}{600} = 18.75\text{ mm} \]

Step 3: Depth of Plastic Neutral Axis (\(\bar{y}_p\))

The P.N.A. requires the area above to equal the area below: \(A_{\text{top}} = A_{\text{bottom}} = A/2 = 300\text{ mm}^2\).
Notice that the area of the top flange alone is exactly \(300\text{ mm}^2\).
Therefore, the equal area axis lies exactly at the junction of the flange and the web.

\[\bar{y}_p = 5\text{ mm} \]

Step 4: Decrease in Neutral Axis Depth

\[\text{Decrease} = \bar{y}_e - \bar{y}_p = 18.75\text{ mm} - 5\text{ mm} = 13.75\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Decrease \(= 13.75\) mm | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
A 16 mm thick gusset plate is connected to the 12 mm thick flange plate of an I-section using fillet welds on both sides as shown in the figure (not drawn to scale). The gusset plate is subjected to a point load of 350 kN acting at a distance of 100 mm from the flange plate. Size of fillet weld is 10 mm.

The maximum resultant stress (in MPa, round off to 1 decimal place) on the fillet weld along the vertical plane would be ________
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Eccentric Welded Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Two vertical fillet welds on both sides of a 16 mm gusset plate.
    • Length of each weld \((d) = 500\text{ mm}\)
    • Size of weld \((s) = 10\text{ mm}\)
    • Point load \((P) = 350\text{ kN}\)
    • Eccentricity from weld plane \((e) = 100\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Determine the maximum resultant (equivalent) stress on the fillet weld.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Throat Thickness: \(t_t = 0.7 \times s\)
  • Eccentricity Perpendicular to Weld Plane: This load causes direct shear stress \((q)\) acting downwards and normal bending stress \((f_a)\) perpendicular to the throat plane.
  • IS 800:2007 (Cl. 10.5.10.1.1) Equivalent Stress: The maximum combined effect on the weld throat is checked using the von Mises yield criterion approach:\[f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + 3q^2} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine throat thickness and calculate the effective weld area to find direct shear stress \((q)\).
  2. Calculate the Section Modulus \((Z)\) of the weld group along the vertical plane.
  3. Calculate the bending moment \((M)\) and find the resulting normal stress \((f_a = M/Z)\).
  4. Calculate the equivalent stress \(f_e\) and round to one decimal place.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Properties of the Weld Group

  • Throat thickness: \(t_t = 0.7 \times 10\text{ mm} = 7\text{ mm}\)
  • Total weld area: \(A = 2 \times (d \times t_t) = 2 \times 500 \times 7 = 7000\text{ mm}^2\)
  • Section modulus of two vertical welds:\[Z = 2 \times \left( \dfrac{t_t \times d^2}{6} \right) = 2 \times \dfrac{7 \times 500^2}{6} = 583{,}333.33\text{ mm}^3 \]

Step 2: Direct Shear Stress (\(q\))

\[q = \dfrac{P}{A} = \dfrac{350 \times 10^3}{7000} = 50\text{ MPa} \]

Step 3: Normal Bending Stress (\(f_a\))

\[M = P \times e = 350 \times 10^3\text{ N} \times 100\text{ mm} = 35 \times 10^6\text{ N}\cdot\text{mm} \]\[f_a = \dfrac{M}{Z} = \dfrac{35 \times 10^6}{583{,}333.33} = 60\text{ MPa} \]

Step 4: Equivalent Resultant Stress (\(f_e\))

Using the IS 800:2007 equivalent stress formulation:

\[f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + 3q^2} = \sqrt{60^2 + 3(50)^2} \]\[f_e = \sqrt{3600 + 7500} = \sqrt{11100} = 105.356\text{ MPa} \approx 105.4\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Maximum Equivalent Stress \(= 105.4\) MPa | Accepted key range: 105.3 to 105.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
The network of a small construction project awarded to a contractor is shown in the following figure. The normal duration, crash duration, normal cost, and crash cost of all the activities are shown in the table. The indirect cost incurred by the contractor is INR 5000 per day.

If the project is targeted for completion in 16 days, the total cost (in INR) to be incurred by the contractor would be ________
questions.explanation:
Construction Management | Project Crashing & Optimization

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Project network with paths and activity details (Normal Duration \(t_n\), Crash Duration \(t_c\), Normal Cost \(C_n\), Crash Cost \(C_c\)).
    • Indirect Cost = INR 5000 / day.
    • Target project duration = 16 days.
  • Aim: Find the total cost (Direct + Indirect) incurred to complete the project in exactly 16 days.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Cost Slope: The rate of increase in direct cost per day of crashing an activity.\[\text{Cost Slope} = \dfrac{\text{Crash Cost} - \text{Normal Cost}}{\text{Normal Duration} - \text{Crash Duration}} \]
  • Critical Path: The longest continuous path in the network, dictating the overall project duration.
  • Crashing Strategy: To reduce project duration, always crash the critical activity (or combination of activities for parallel critical paths) that has the minimum total cost slope.
  • Total Cost: \(\text{Total Cost} = \text{Total Normal Cost} + \text{Total Crashing Cost} + (\text{Indirect Cost/day} \times \text{Duration})\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the Cost Slope for all activities.
  2. Determine all network paths and identify the critical path(s) under normal conditions.
  3. Calculate the initial Total Direct Cost under normal conditions.
  4. Crash the network step-by-step, targeting minimum cost slopes, until the project duration reaches the 16-day target.
  5. Compute the final Total Cost.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Calculate Cost Slopes and Normal Direct Cost

  • P: \((25000 - 15000) / (6 - 4) = 10000 / 2 = 5000\) INR/day
  • Q: \((12000 - 6000) / (5 - 2) = 6000 / 3 = 2000\) INR/day
  • R: \((9500 - 8000) / (5 - 3) = 1500 / 2 = 750\) INR/day
  • S: \((10000 - 7000) / (6 - 3) = 3000 / 3 = 1000\) INR/day
  • T: \((9000 - 6000) / (3 - 2) = 3000 / 1 = 3000\) INR/day
  • U: \((6000 - 4000) / (2 - 1) = 2000 / 1 = 2000\) INR/day
  • V: \((28000 - 20000) / (4 - 2) = 8000 / 2 = 4000\) INR/day
  • Total Normal Direct Cost \(= \sum C_n = 15k + 6k + 8k + 7k + 6k + 4k + 20k = 66{,}000\) INR

Step 2: Identify Paths and Normal Duration

  • Path 1: \(P - Q - U - V \Rightarrow 6 + 5 + 2 + 4 = 17\) days
  • Path 2: \(P - R - T - V \Rightarrow 6 + 5 + 3 + 4 = \mathbf{18}\) days (Critical Path)
  • Path 3: \(P - S - V \Rightarrow 6 + 6 + 4 = 16\) days

Normal duration is 18 days. We must crash it by 2 days.

Step 3: Crashing Iteration 1 (18 days → 17 days)

  • Target the critical path: \(P - R - T - V\).
  • Available activities to crash with cost slopes: P (5000), R (750), T (3000), V (4000).
  • Activity R has the minimum cost slope (750 INR/day). Crash R by 1 day.
  • Cost incurred = 750 INR.
  • New Path lengths: P-Q-U-V = 17 days, P-R-T-V = 17 days, P-S-V = 16 days.

Step 4: Crashing Iteration 2 (17 days → 16 days)

Now we have two parallel critical paths: \(P - Q - U - V\) (17) and \(P - R - T - V\) (17). We must crash both simultaneously by 1 day. Valid options:

  • Crash common activity P: 5000 INR
  • Crash common activity V: 4000 INR
  • Crash parallel activities (R + Q): \(750 + 2000 = 2750\) INR
  • Crash parallel activities (R + U): \(750 + 2000 = 2750\) INR
  • Crash parallel activities (T + Q): \(3000 + 2000 = 5000\) INR

The minimum cost option is to crash R and Q (or R and U) together.
Cost incurred = 2750 INR.
New Path lengths: All three paths are now exactly 16 days. Target achieved!

Step 5: Compute Final Total Cost

  • Total Crashing Cost \(= 750 + 2750 = 3500\) INR
  • Total Direct Cost \(= 66{,}000 + 3{,}500 = 69{,}500\) INR
  • Total Indirect Cost \(= 16 \text{ days} \times 5000 \text{ INR/day} = 80{,}000\) INR
  • Total Cost \(= 69{,}500 + 80{,}000 = 1{,}49{,}500\) INR

6. Final Answer:

Total Cost \(= \mathbf{1{,}49{,}500}\) INR | Accepted key range: 149500 to 149500

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: A box measuring 50 cm × 50 cm × 50 cm is filled to the top with dry coarse aggregate of mass 187.5 kg. The water absorption and specific gravity of the aggregate are 0.5% and 2.5, respectively. The maximum quantity of water (in kg, round off to 2 decimal places) required to fill the box completely is ________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering / Concrete Technology | Aggregate Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Box dimensions: \(L = 50\text{ cm},\ W = 50\text{ cm},\ H = 50\text{ cm}\)
    • Mass of dry coarse aggregate \((M_s) = 187.5\) kg
    • Water absorption of aggregate \(= 0.5\%\)
    • Specific gravity of aggregate \((G_s) = 2.5\)
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum quantity of water (in kg) required to completely fill the box.

3. Core Concepts:

The water required will fulfill two purposes:

  1. Water absorbed into the permeable pores of the dry aggregates (Water Absorption).
  2. Water filling the empty void spaces between the aggregate particles (Void Volume).
  • Volume of Box (\(V\)): \(V = V_s + V_v\) (Volume of Solid Aggregates + Volume of Voids)
  • True Volume of Solids: \(V_s = \dfrac{M_s}{G_s \times \rho_w}\)
  • Density of Water (\(\rho_w\)): \(1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the total geometrical volume of the box (\(V\)).
  2. Calculate the absolute volume occupied by the solid aggregates (\(V_s\)).
  3. Find the volume of voids in the box (\(V_v = V - V_s\)).
  4. Convert the void volume into the mass of water required to fill it.
  5. Calculate the mass of water absorbed by the aggregates.
  6. Sum both water masses to get the final total quantity.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Total Box Volume

\[V = 0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m} = 0.125\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 2: Volume of Solid Aggregate

\[V_s = \dfrac{187.5\text{ kg}}{2.5 \times 1000\text{ kg/m}^3} = \dfrac{187.5}{2500} = 0.075\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Volume and Mass of Water to Fill Voids

\[V_v = V - V_s = 0.125 - 0.075 = 0.050\text{ m}^3 \]\[M_{\text{voids}} = V_v \times \rho_w = 0.050\text{ m}^3 \times 1000\text{ kg/m}^3 = 50.00\text{ kg} \]

Step 4: Mass of Water Absorbed

\[M_{\text{absorbed}} = 0.5\%\text{ of }M_s = \dfrac{0.5}{100} \times 187.5 = 0.9375\text{ kg} \]

Step 5: Total Water Required

\[\text{Total Water} = M_{\text{voids}} + M_{\text{absorbed}} = 50.00 + 0.9375 = 50.9375\text{ kg} \approx 50.94\text{ kg} \]

6. Final Answer:

Total Water \(= 50.94\) kg | Accepted key range: 50.50 to 51.20

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A steel column is restrained against both translation and rotation at one end and is restrained only against rotation but free to translate at the other end. Theoretical and design (IS:800-2007) values, respectively, of effective length factor of the column are
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Steel Structures (Compression Members)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: A steel column with specific end conditions:
    • End 1: Restrained against translation AND rotation (Fixed).
    • End 2: Restrained against rotation but FREE to translate (Guided/Slider).
  • Aim: Find the Theoretical and Design values (as per IS:800-2007) for the effective length factor (\(K\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Effective Length (\(L_{eff}\)): The distance between points of zero moment (inflection points) in a column. \(L_{eff} = K \cdot L\).

IS 800:2007 (Table 11 — Effective Length of Prismatic Compression Members): Recommends specific values for theoretical limits and practical design scenarios. Practical (design) values are typically higher to account for the fact that perfect fixity is unachievable in actual structural connections.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Match the given boundary conditions to the standard cases in IS 800:2007 Table 11.
  2. The case is: "Effectively held in position and restrained against rotation at one end, and at the other end restrained against rotation but not held in position." (Fixed-Guided).
  3. Extract the corresponding Theoretical and Recommended (Design) values.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Identify the column case.
    This is commonly known as a Fixed–Guided column (like an expanding pipe column or a sliding frame joint).
  2. Step 2: Consult IS 800:2007 Table 11 (Serial No. 4).
    • Theoretical value of effective length factor \((K_{\text{theo}})\): 1.0
    • Recommended design value of effective length factor \((K_{\text{design}})\): 1.2

Note on physical intuition: A fixed-guided column effectively acts like a fixed-fixed column of double the length if you mirror it about the sliding end. The inflection points are separated exactly by \(1.0L\) theoretically. Real-world joint flexibility necessitates increasing this to \(1.2L\) for safe buckling capacity design.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(1.0\) and \(1.2\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: If the fineness modulus of a sample of fine aggregates is 4.3, the mean size of the particles in the sample is between
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Aggregates (Sieve Analysis)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Fineness modulus (FM) of a fine aggregate sample = 4.3
  • Aim: Determine the range of the mean particle size.

3. Core Concepts:

Fineness Modulus (FM): An empirical factor obtained by adding the cumulative percentages of aggregate retained on each of the standard sieves and dividing by 100.

Standard Sieve Series (Fine Aggregates): The standard sequence is: 150 \(\mu\)m, 300 \(\mu\)m, 600 \(\mu\)m, 1.18 mm, 2.36 mm, 4.75 mm.

Index Mapping: The FM directly corresponds to an "average index" of the standard sieves.

FM (Index)Sieve Size
1150 \(\mu\)m
2300 \(\mu\)m
3600 \(\mu\)m
41.18 mm
52.36 mm
64.75 mm

4. Solution Method:

  1. Map the standard sieves to their corresponding integer Fineness Modulus values.
  2. Place the given FM (4.3) between the two closest integer values.
  3. The mean particle size will lie between the sieve sizes corresponding to those integers.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Map indices to standard sieves (see table in Core Concepts above).
  2. Step 2: Bracket the given FM.
    The given FM = 4.3 lies between the indices 4 and 5 \((4 < 4.3 < 5)\).
  3. Step 3: Translate indices back to physical sieve sizes.
    Index 4 corresponds to 1.18 mm.
    Index 5 corresponds to 2.36 mm.
    Therefore, the mean size of the particles in the sample is between 1.18 mm and 2.36 mm.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(1.18\text{ mm}\) and \(2.36\text{ mm}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
The characteristic compressive strength of concrete required in a project is 25 MPa and the standard deviation in the observed compressive strength expected at site is 4 MPa. The average compressive strength of cubes tested at different water-cement (w/c) ratios using the same material as is used for the project is given in the table.
w/c (%)45505560
Average compressive strength of cubes (MPa)35252015

The water-cement ratio (in percent, round off to the lower integer) to be used in the mix is ______
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Mix Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Characteristic compressive strength, \(f_{ck} = 25\) MPa
    • Standard deviation, \(s = 4\) MPa
    • Experimental data table mapping \(w/c\) (%) to Average Compressive Strength (MPa)
  • Aim: Find the optimal water-cement ratio (in percent, rounded to the lower integer) for the mix design.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 (Mix Design Target): A concrete mix must be designed for a Target Mean Compressive Strength (\(f_{cm}\)) to ensure that no more than 5% of test results fall below the characteristic strength.

Formula: \(f_{cm} = f_{ck} + 1.65 \times s\)

Interpolation: The relation between strength and \(w/c\) ratio is inversely proportional. Linear interpolation is adequate between close intervals.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the target mean strength using IS code provisions.
  2. Bracket the target strength within the provided table data.
  3. Linearly interpolate to find the exact \(w/c\) ratio.
  4. Round to the lower integer. (Note: Rounding to a lower \(w/c\) ratio provides a higher concrete strength, making it the safer, correct engineering practice.)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Target Mean Strength:\[f_{cm} = 25 \text{ MPa} + 1.65(4 \text{ MPa}) = 25 + 6.6 = 31.6 \text{ MPa} \]
  2. Locate Brackets in Table:
    • At \(w/c = 45\%\), Strength \(= 35\) MPa
    • At \(w/c = 50\%\), Strength \(= 25\) MPa
    Our target (\(31.6\) MPa) lies between 45% and 50%.
  3. Linear Interpolation:\[\dfrac{w/c - 45}{50 - 45} = \dfrac{31.6 - 35}{25 - 35} \]\[\dfrac{w/c - 45}{5} = \dfrac{-3.4}{-10} = 0.34 \]\[w/c - 45 = 1.7 \implies w/c = 46.7\% \]
  4. Rounding Protocol:
    The question dictates rounding to the lower integer.
    Lower integer of \(46.7\%\) → \(46\%\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 46 | Accepted key range: 46 to 46

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: The critical bending compressive stress in the extreme fibre of a structural steel section is 1000 MPa. It is given that the yield strength of the steel is 250 MPa, width of flange is 250 mm and thickness of flange is 15 mm. As per the provisions of IS:800-2007, the non-dimensional slenderness ratio of the steel cross-section is
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Beams (Plastic Analysis & Buckling)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Elastic critical bending compressive stress, \(f_{cr,b} = 1000\) MPa
    • Yield strength of steel, \(f_y = 250\) MPa
    • Flange width, \(b_f = 250\) mm (Auxiliary data)
    • Flange thickness, \(t_f = 15\) mm (Auxiliary data)
  • Aim: Determine the non-dimensional slenderness ratio (\(\lambda_{LT}\)) for lateral torsional buckling as per IS 800:2007.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007 Provisions: According to Clause 8.2.2 (Design Bending Strength for laterally unsupported beams), the susceptibility of a beam to lateral-torsional buckling is measured by the equivalent non-dimensional lateral torsional slenderness ratio, \(\lambda_{LT}\).

Formula: The code defines this ratio as:

\[\lambda_{LT} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\beta_b Z_p f_y}{M_{cr}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{f_y}{f_{cr,b}}} \]

(Where \(\beta_b = 1.0\) for plastic/compact sections, which the provided flange dimensions guarantee, but the stress-based formula isolates this directly.)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify the formula linking yield stress and elastic critical buckling stress.
  2. Ensure both stress parameters are in the same units (MPa).
  3. Compute the ratio and take the square root. Flange dimensions are provided as distractors or to implicitly verify section classification, but are mathematically bypassed when exactly \(f_{cr,b}\) is given.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Extract the required parameters for the IS 800 formula.
    \(f_y = 250\) MPa, \(f_{cr,b} = 1000\) MPa
  2. Step 2: Substitute into the non-dimensional slenderness equation.\[\lambda_{LT} = \sqrt{\dfrac{250}{1000}} \]
  3. Step 3: Simplify the fraction and evaluate the square root.\[\lambda_{LT} = \sqrt{0.25} = 0.50 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(0.50\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question:
In the context of provisions relating to durability of concrete, consider the following assertions:

Assertion (1): As per IS 456-2000, air entrainment to the extent of 3% to 6% is required for concrete exposed to marine environment.

Assertion (2): The equivalent alkali content (in terms of Na₂O equivalent) for a cement containing 1% and 0.6% of Na₂O and K₂O, respectively, is approximately 1.4% (rounded to 1 decimal place).

Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: Assertion (1) is FALSE and Assertion (2) is TRUE
Assertion (1) is TRUE and Assertion (2) is FALSE
Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are FALSE
Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are TRUE

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Assertion (1) is FALSE and Assertion (2) is TRUE
structuredOptions.html: Assertion (1) is FALSE and Assertion (2) is TRUE

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Assertion (1) is TRUE and Assertion (2) is FALSE
structuredOptions.html: Assertion (1) is TRUE and Assertion (2) is FALSE

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are FALSE
structuredOptions.html: Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are FALSE

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are TRUE
structuredOptions.html: Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are TRUE

questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Durability and Cement Chemistry

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Exposure Condition: Marine Environment
    • Cement alkali content: \(\text{Na}_2\text{O} = 1\%\), \(\text{K}_2\text{O} = 0.6\%\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the validity of two assertions based on IS 456-2000 and calculate the equivalent alkali content.

3. Core Concepts:

IS Code Provisions for Durability: As per IS 456-2000, Clause 8.2.2.3, air-entraining admixtures are explicitly required for concrete exposed to freezing and thawing cycles. For marine environments, durability is achieved by limiting the maximum water-cement ratio, maintaining a minimum cement content, and using higher grades of concrete (Severe/Very Severe/Extreme exposure as per Table 5). Thus, air-entrainment of 3% to 6% is not a mandate for marine exposure.

Equivalent Alkali Content: Expressed to evaluate the risk of Alkali-Silica Reaction (ASR). It unifies the content of both Sodium Oxide (\(\text{Na}_2\text{O}\)) and Potassium Oxide (\(\text{K}_2\text{O}\)) based on their molecular weights.

  • Molecular weight of \(\text{Na}_2\text{O} \approx (2 \times 23) + 16 = 62\) g/mol
  • Molecular weight of \(\text{K}_2\text{O} \approx (2 \times 39.1) + 16 = 94.2\) g/mol
  • Conversion Factor \(= \dfrac{62}{94.2} \approx 0.658\)
\[\text{Na}_2\text{O}_{eq} = \text{Na}_2\text{O} + 0.658 \times \text{K}_2\text{O} \]

4. Solution Method & Execution:

  1. Step 1: Check Assertion (1)
    Air-entrainment of 3% to 6% is required for freezing and thawing, not for the marine environment.
    Conclusion: Assertion (1) is FALSE.
  2. Step 2: Check Assertion (2)
    Given: \(\text{Na}_2\text{O} = 1\%\), \(\text{K}_2\text{O} = 0.6\%\)\[\text{Equivalent Alkali} = 1\% + (0.658 \times 0.6\%) = 1\% + 0.3948\% = 1.3948\% \approx 1.4\% \]Conclusion: Assertion (2) is TRUE.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Assertion (1) is FALSE and Assertion (2) is TRUE | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
A rolled I-section beam is supported on a 75 mm wide bearing plate as shown in the figure. Thicknesses of flange and web of the I-section are 20 mm and 8 mm, respectively. Root radius of the I-section is 10 mm. Assume: material yield stress, fᵧ = 250 MPa and partial safety factor for material, γₘ₀ = 1.10.


As per IS: 800-2007, the web bearing strength (in kN, round off to 2 decimal places) of the beam is ______
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Plate Girders & Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Bearing plate length: \(b_1 = 75\) mm
    • Flange thickness: \(t_f = 20\) mm
    • Web thickness: \(t_w = 8\) mm
    • Root radius: \(R = 10\) mm
    • Yield stress: \(f_y = 250\) MPa
    • Partial safety factor: \(\gamma_{m0} = 1.10\)
  • Aim: Calculate the local web bearing strength of the beam (in kN).

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007 (Clause 8.7.4 — Bearing Strength of Web):

\[F_w = \dfrac{(b_1 + n_2) \cdot t_w \cdot f_y}{\gamma_{m0}} \]

Dispersion: \(n_2\) represents the length obtained by load dispersion through the flange to the web toe of the fillet. The assumed dispersion slope is 1:2.5 (1 vertical to 2.5 horizontal).

End Support Condition: Since the bearing plate is flush with the end of the beam, the dispersion spreads inward in only one direction.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the depth of dispersion \(h\) to the critical cross-section (the fillet's root).
  2. Calculate the horizontal dispersion length \(n_2\).
  3. Calculate the effective structural bearing length of the web, \(L_{eff} = b_1 + n_2\).
  4. Multiply by web area and material properties to find the nominal strength.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Critical Depth (\(h\)):\[h = t_f + R = 20\text{ mm} + 10\text{ mm} = 30\text{ mm} \]
  2. Dispersion Length (\(n_2\)):\[n_2 = 2.5 \times h = 2.5 \times 30 = 75\text{ mm} \]
  3. Effective Web Length (\(L_{eff}\)): (End support — one-sided dispersion)\[L_{eff} = b_1 + n_2 = 75\text{ mm} + 75\text{ mm} = 150\text{ mm} \]
  4. Effective Bearing Area (\(A_b\)):\[A_b = L_{eff} \times t_w = 150\text{ mm} \times 8\text{ mm} = 1200\text{ mm}^2 \]
  5. Design Web Bearing Strength (\(F_w\)):\[F_w = \dfrac{1200\text{ mm}^2 \times 250\text{ N/mm}^2}{1.10} = 272{,}727.27\text{ N} = 272.73\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 272.73 kN | Accepted key range: 272.60 to 272.80

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: When a specimen of M25 concrete is loaded to a stress level of 12.5 MPa, a strain of 500×10⁻⁶ is recorded. If this load is allowed to stand for a long time, the strain increases to 1000×10⁻⁶. In accordance with the provisions of IS:456-2000, considering the long-term effects, the effective modulus of elasticity of the concrete (in MPa) is ______
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Concrete Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Applied stress level: \(\sigma = 12.5\) MPa
    • Short-term (instantaneous) strain: \(\varepsilon_i = 500 \times 10^{-6}\)
    • Long-term total strain: \(\varepsilon_{\text{total}} = 1000 \times 10^{-6}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the effective modulus of elasticity (\(E_{ce}\)) for the concrete considering long-term effects.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 (Clause 6.2.3.1): Accounts for time-dependent deformation (creep) when determining the effective modulus.

\[E_{ce} = \dfrac{E_c}{1 + \theta} \]

where \(\theta\) is the creep coefficient \(\left(\theta = \dfrac{\text{Creep Strain}}{\text{Elastic Strain}}\right)\) and \(E_c\) is the short-term elastic modulus.

Shortcut: \(E_{ce}\) simplifies completely to the applied stress divided by the total accumulated long-term strain.

4. Solution Method:

Divide the applied stress (\(\sigma\)) by the long-term total strain (\(\varepsilon_{\text{total}}\)) to directly obtain \(E_{ce}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify the steady stress and long-term strain:\[\sigma = 12.5\text{ MPa}, \quad \varepsilon_{\text{total}} = 1000 \times 10^{-6} = 0.001 \]
  2. Calculate the effective modulus:\[E_{ce} = \dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{\text{total}}} = \dfrac{12.5}{0.001} = 12500\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 12500 MPa | Accepted key range: 12500 to 12500

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: A steel column of ISHB 350 @72.4 kg/m is subjected to a factored axial compressive load of 2000 kN. The load is transferred to a concrete pedestal of grade M20 through a square base plate. Consider bearing strength of concrete as \( 0.45f_{ck} \), where \( f_{ck} \) is the characteristic strength of concrete. Using limit state method and neglecting the self weight of base plate and steel column, the length of a side of the base plate to be provided is
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Design of Steel Structures — Column Base Plate (IS 800:2007)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Factored axial load: \(P_u = 2000 \text{ kN}\)
    • Concrete grade: M20 (\(f_{ck} = 20 \text{ MPa}\))
    • Bearing strength \(= 0.45 f_{ck}\)
    • Square base plate; neglect self-weight of plate & column
  • Aim: Find the side length of the square base plate.

3. Core Concepts:

Bearing pressure on the concrete pedestal must not exceed \(0.45 f_{ck}\) (IS 800:2007 Clause 7.4.1). Uniform pressure is assumed under limit state.

\[A_{\text{req}} = \dfrac{P_u}{0.45 f_{ck}} \]

Note: \(1 \text{ MPa} = 10^3 \text{ kN/m}^2\) — consistent unit conversion is essential.

4. Solution Method:

Direct area calculation → side length \(= \sqrt{A}\). Choose the next higher standard size.

Common pitfall: Forgetting unit conversion (kN vs MPa) or including column self-weight (explicitly neglected).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Bearing Strength\[0.45 \times 20 = 9 \text{ MPa} = 9 \times 10^3 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Required Area\[A = \dfrac{2000}{9 \times 10^3} = 0.2222 \text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Step 3: Side Length\[L = \sqrt{0.2222} = 0.4714 \text{ m} = 47.14 \text{ cm} \]
  4. Step 4: Rounding up to the nearest practical size: 48 cm.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 48 cm | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: The Le Chatelier apparatus is used to determine
questions.explanation:
Materials Engineering | Cement Testing (IS 4031)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Le Chatelier apparatus
  • Aim: Identify what property it determines.

3. Core Concepts:

The Le Chatelier test measures expansion due to free lime/magnesia, thereby determining the soundness of cement.

  • IS 4031 (Part 3): Soundness by Le Chatelier → maximum permissible expansion = 10 mm.
  • Other tests: Vicat apparatus → setting time; Blaine apparatus → fineness; cube moulds → compressive strength.

4. Solution Method:

Direct recall of standard cement test apparatus-to-purpose mapping. No calculation required.

Pitfall: Confusing with Vicat (uses needles for consistency/setting) or Blaine (air permeability for fineness).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Recall: Le Chatelier mould = split cylinder with indicator pointers.
  2. Purpose: Detects unsoundness — excessive expansion after boiling.
  3. Eliminate others: Compressive → cube moulds; Fineness → Blaine; Setting → Vicat.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Soundness of cement | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: The deformation in concrete due to sustained loading is
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Properties of Hardened Concrete (IS 456:2000)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Deformation in concrete due to sustained loading.
  • Aim: Identify the phenomenon.

3. Core Concepts:

Creep = time-dependent deformation under constant sustained stress (IS 456 Clause 6.2.5).

  • Shrinkage: Volume reduction due to drying — load-independent.
  • Hydration: Chemical reaction between cement and water.
  • Segregation: Separation of constituents in fresh concrete.

The creep coefficient \(\theta\) is used in long-term deflection calculations per IS 456.

4. Solution Method:

Keyword matching: sustained loading → creep (not shrinkage, which is load-independent).

Pitfall: Mixing creep and shrinkage — both are long-term phenomena but have different causes.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Sustained load is present → eliminates shrinkage and hydration.
  2. Concrete under constant stress → viscoelastic (time-dependent) behaviour → creep.
  3. IS 456 confirms: long-term deformation under sustained loading = creep.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Creep | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q9
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: Two rectangular under-reinforced concrete beam sections X and Y are similar in all aspects except that the longitudinal compression reinforcement in section Y is 10% more. Which one of the following is the correct statement?
options: Section X has less flexural strength and is less ductile than section Y
Section X has less flexural strength but is more ductile than section Y
Sections X and Y have equal flexural strength but different ductility
Sections X and Y have equal flexural strength and ductility

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Section X has less flexural strength and is less ductile than section Y
structuredOptions.html: Section X has less flexural strength and is less ductile than section Y

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Section X has less flexural strength but is more ductile than section Y
structuredOptions.html: Section X has less flexural strength but is more ductile than section Y

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Sections X and Y have equal flexural strength but different ductility
structuredOptions.html: Sections X and Y have equal flexural strength but different ductility

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Sections X and Y have equal flexural strength and ductility
structuredOptions.html: Sections X and Y have equal flexural strength and ductility

questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Flexure in Beams (IS 456:2000 Annex G)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Two identical under-reinforced rectangular sections X and Y.
    • Section Y has 10% more longitudinal compression reinforcement: \(A_{sc,Y} = 1.1\, A_{sc,X}\).
    • Same \(A_{st}\), \(b\), \(d\), and material grades for both sections.
  • Aim: Compare flexural strength and ductility of sections X and Y.

3. Core Concepts:

Under-reinforced sections: Tension steel yields before concrete crushes.

Equilibrium:

\[T = 0.87 f_y A_{st} = 0.36 f_{ck}\, b\, x_u + (f_{sc} - f_{cc})\, A_{sc} \]
  • Increasing \(A_{sc}\) → \(x_u\) decreases (less concrete compression needed to maintain equilibrium).
  • Moment increases due to additional compression steel couple: \(M_u = M_{u,\text{conc}} + A_{sc}(f_{sc})(d - d')\).
  • Ductility: Smaller \(x_u/d\) → higher ultimate curvature (\(\phi_u \propto 1/x_u\)) → more ductile.

4. Solution Method:

Compare the effect of extra \(A_{sc}\) on \(x_u\), \(M_u\), and ductility.

Pitfall: Assuming compression steel does not affect strength — it does via the additional moment couple.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Section X (less \(A_{sc}\)): larger \(x_u\) required to balance the same \(T\) → higher \(x_u/d\).
  2. Section Y (more \(A_{sc}\)): smaller \(x_u\), additional \(M_u\) from compression steel couple → higher \(M_u\).
  3. Smaller \(x_u\) in Y → higher ultimate curvature → Y is more ductile.
  4. Conclusion: Section X has lower flexural strength and is less ductile than Section Y.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Section X has less flexural strength and is less ductile than section Y | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: In a fillet weld, the direct shear stress and bending tensile stress are 50 MPa and 150 MPa, respectively. As per IS 800: 2007, the equivalent stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) will be _______
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Fillet Weld Design per IS 800:2007

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Direct shear stress \(\tau_{vf} = 50 \text{ MPa}\)
    Bending tensile stress \(\sigma_{bf} = 150 \text{ MPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate equivalent stress \(f_e\) per IS 800:2007

3. Core Concepts:

  • IS 800:2007 Clause 10.5.10.1.1: Equivalent stress for combined loading
    \[f_e = \sqrt{\sigma_{bf}^2 + 3\tau_{vf}^2} \]
  • Design check: \(f_e \leq \dfrac{f_u}{\sqrt{3}\gamma_{mw}}\) (not required here)
  • Standard assumption: Stresses are at critical section of weld throat

4. Solution Method:

  • Direct substitution into IS 800 formula
  • Pitfall Alert: Do not use von Mises without the factor of 3 for shear; ensure stress units consistent (MPa)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply IS 800:2007 formula:
    \[f_e = \sqrt{(150)^2 + 3(50)^2} \]
  2. Compute stepwise:
    \[f_e = \sqrt{22500 + 3(2500)} = \sqrt{22500 + 7500} = \sqrt{30000} \]
  3. Final calculation:
    \[f_e = 173.20508 \text{ MPa} \approx 173.21 \text{ MPa (to two decimals)} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer(for NAT): \(173.21\) MPa | Accepted range: 173.10 to 173.30

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: An RCC short column (with lateral ties) of rectangular cross section of 250 mm × 300 mm is reinforced with four numbers of 16 mm diameter longitudinal bars. The grades of steel and concrete are Fe415 and M20, respectively. Neglect eccentricity effect. Considering limit state of collapse in compression (IS 456 : 2000), the axial load carrying capacity of the column (in kN, up to one decimal place), is _______
questions.explanation:
RCC Design | Limit State of Collapse: Compression

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Cross section: \(b = 250 \text{ mm},\ D = 300 \text{ mm}\)
    • Reinforcement: 4 bars of 16 mm diameter
    • Materials: Fe415 (\(f_y = 415 \text{ MPa}\)), M20 (\(f_{ck} = 20 \text{ MPa}\))
    • Constraint: Neglect eccentricity effect
  • Aim: Find the axial load carrying capacity (\(P_u\)) in kN.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Area of Steel (\(A_{sc}\)): Cross-sectional area of longitudinal bars.
  • Area of Concrete (\(A_c\)): Gross area (\(A_g\)) minus area of steel (\(A_{sc}\)).
  • Standard Code Formula (IS 456 Cl 39.3): \(P_u = 0.4 f_{ck}A_c + 0.67 f_y A_{sc}\) — accounts for minimum accidental eccentricity up to \(0.05D\).
  • Pure Axial Formula (when eccentricity is explicitly neglected): \(P_0 = 0.45 f_{ck}A_c + 0.75 f_y A_{sc}\).

Note: GATE accepted both interpretations. The pure axial formula is used here as the problem explicitly states to neglect eccentricity.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(A_g\) and \(A_{sc}\).
  2. Deduct \(A_{sc}\) from \(A_g\) to find \(A_c\).
  3. Substitute into the pure axial load capacity equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate Areas\[A_g = 250 \times 300 = 75{,}000 \text{ mm}^2 \]\[A_{sc} = 4 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (16)^2 = 4 \times 201.06 = 804.25 \text{ mm}^2 \]\[A_c = 75{,}000 - 804.25 = 74{,}195.75 \text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Apply Capacity Formula (Neglecting Eccentricity)\[P_0 = 0.45 f_{ck} A_c + 0.75 f_y A_{sc} \]\[P_0 = 0.45(20)(74{,}195.75) + 0.75(415)(804.25) \]\[P_0 = 667{,}761.75 \text{ N} + 250{,}322.81 \text{ N} \]\[P_0 = 918{,}084.56 \text{ N} \approx 918.1 \text{ kN} \]

    Using the standard code formula \(P_u = 0.4f_{ck}A_c + 0.67f_yA_{sc}\) gives 817.2 kN. Both interpretations were rewarded.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 918.1 kN | Accepted key range: 815 to 830 OR 905 to 920

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: An RCC beam of rectangular cross section has factored shear of 200 kN at its critical section. Its width b is 250 mm and effective depth d is 350 mm. Assume design shear strength \( \tau_c \) of concrete as 0.62 N/mm² and maximum allowable shear stress \( \tau_{c,max} \) in concrete as 2.8 N/mm². If two legged 10 mm diameter vertical stirrups of Fe250 grade steel are used, then the required spacing (in cm, up to one decimal place) as per limit state method will be _______
questions.explanation:
RCC Design | Limit State of Collapse: Shear

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(b = 250 \text{ mm},\ d = 350 \text{ mm}\)
    • Factored Shear: \(V_u = 200 \text{ kN} = 200{,}000 \text{ N}\)
    • \(\tau_c = 0.62 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • \(\tau_{c,max} = 2.8 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • Stirrups: 2-legged, 10 mm dia, Fe250 steel (\(f_y = 250 \text{ MPa}\))
  • Aim: Find the required spacing \(s_v\) in cm.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Nominal Shear Stress: \(\tau_v = \dfrac{V_u}{bd}\) (Must be \(< \tau_{c,max}\) to prevent diagonal compression failure)
  • Shear Resisted by Concrete: \(V_c = \tau_c b d\)
  • Shear Resisted by Stirrups: \(V_{us} = V_u - V_c\)
  • Spacing of Vertical Stirrups (IS 456 Cl 40.4): \(s_v = \dfrac{0.87 f_y A_{sv} d}{V_{us}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Verify section is safe in diagonal compression.
  2. Determine required shear reinforcement force (\(V_{us}\)).
  3. Calculate area of stirrup legs (\(A_{sv}\)).
  4. Calculate required spacing (\(s_v\)) in mm, then convert to cm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Verify Section Safety\[\tau_v = \dfrac{200 \times 1000}{250 \times 350} = 2.286 \text{ N/mm}^2 \]Since \(\tau_v\ (2.286) < \tau_{c,max}\ (2.8)\), the section is safe.
  2. Step 2: Force Components\[V_c = 0.62 \times 250 \times 350 = 54{,}250 \text{ N} = 54.25 \text{ kN} \]\[V_{us} = 200 - 54.25 = 145.75 \text{ kN} = 145{,}750 \text{ N} \]
  3. Step 3: Stirrup Properties
    For 2-legged 10 mm dia stirrup:\[A_{sv} = 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (10)^2 = 157.08 \text{ mm}^2 \]
  4. Step 4: Required Spacing\[s_v = \dfrac{0.87 \times 250 \times 157.08 \times 350}{145{,}750} = \dfrac{11{,}957{,}715}{145{,}750} \approx 82.04 \text{ mm} \]Unit Conversion:\[s_v = 82.04 \text{ mm} = 8.204 \text{ cm} \approx 8.2 \text{ cm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.2 cm | Accepted key range: 7.0 to 9.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
The dimensions of a symmetrical welded I-section are shown in the figure.



The plastic section modulus about the weaker axis (in cm³, up to one decimal place) is _______
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Plastic Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Symmetrical I-section
    • Flange width: \(b_f = 140 \text{ mm}\), Flange thickness: \(t_f = 9 \text{ mm}\)
    • Web depth: \(d_w = 200 \text{ mm}\), Web thickness: \(t_w = 6.1 \text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Find the plastic section modulus (\(Z_p\)) about the weaker axis in cm³.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Weaker Axis: For a standard I-section, the weaker axis is the vertical axis (\(y\text{-}y\)) passing through the center of the web.
  • Plastic Neutral Axis (PNA): Due to symmetry about the \(y\text{-}y\) axis, the PNA coincides with the geometric centroidal axis, splitting the total area equally.
  • Plastic Section Modulus:\[Z_p = \sum A_i |\bar{x}_i| = 2 \times (\text{First moment of area of one half about PNA}) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Split the section vertically down the center of the web.
  2. Identify elements on one half: half-top flange, half-bottom flange, and half-web.
  3. Compute the area and centroid distance for each half-element.
  4. Sum the moments of area, double it, and convert to cm³.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Elements of the right-half section

    Top Flange (right half):
    Width \(= 140/2 = 70 \text{ mm}\)
    \(A_{f1} = 70 \times 9 = 630 \text{ mm}^2\)
    \(\bar{x}_{f1} = 70/2 = 35 \text{ mm}\)

    Bottom Flange (right half):
    \(A_{f2} = 630 \text{ mm}^2,\ \bar{x}_{f2} = 35 \text{ mm}\)

    Web (right half):
    Thickness \(= 6.1/2 = 3.05 \text{ mm}\)
    \(A_w = 200 \times 3.05 = 610 \text{ mm}^2\)
    \(\bar{x}_w = 3.05/2 = 1.525 \text{ mm}\)
  2. Step 2: Compute \(Z_{py}\)\[ Z_{py} = 2 \times [(A_{f1}\bar{x}_{f1}) + (A_{f2}\bar{x}_{f2}) + (A_w\bar{x}_w)] \]\[ Z_{py} = 2 \times [(630 \times 35) + (630 \times 35) + (610 \times 1.525)] \]\[ Z_{py} = 2 \times [22{,}050 + 22{,}050 + 930.25] \]\[Z_{py} = 2 \times 45{,}030.25 = 90{,}060.5 \text{ mm}^3 \]
  3. Step 3: Unit Conversion\[Z_{py} = \dfrac{90{,}060.5}{10^3} = 90.06 \text{ cm}^3 \approx 90.1 \text{ cm}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 90.1 cm³ | Accepted key range: 88.0 to 92.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: The setting time of cement is determined using
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Cement Testing

  • Taxonomy: Recall — direct factual knowledge about cement testing apparatus.
  • Given Data: Question asks about the apparatus for determining setting time of cement.
  • Aim: Identify the correct testing apparatus from the given options.

3. Core Concepts:

IS Code Reference: IS 4031 — Methods of physical tests for hydraulic cement.

Cement Setting Time:

  • Initial Setting Time: Time from mixing water until the cement paste begins to lose plasticity (typically 30–45 min for OPC).
  • Final Setting Time: Time until the paste completely loses plasticity and gains sufficient rigidity (typically 10 h for OPC).

Standard Apparatus Reference:

PropertyApparatusIS Reference

OptionApparatusPurpose

(B)BriquetteTensile strength of cement mortar

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A structural member subjected to compression, has both translation and rotation restrained at one end, while only translation is restrained at the other end. As per IS 456 : 2000, the effective length factor recommended for design is
questions.explanation:
Structural Design (Concrete) | Compression Members — Effective Length

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension — IS 456:2000 code provision for effective length factor.
  • Given Data:
    EndTranslationRotation
    One endRestrainedRestrained
    Other endRestrainedFree

    End 1: Fixed (both translation & rotation restrained); End 2: Pinned (translation restrained, rotation free).

  • Aim: Find the effective length factor as per IS 456:2000.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 Reference: Clause 25.1.2 and Table 28 (Effective Length of Compression Members).\[L_{eff} = k \cdot L\]where \(k\) = effective length factor, \(L\) = unsupported length.

IS 456:2000 Table 28 — Effective Length Factors:

S.No.End ConditionFactor \(k\)
1Both ends fixed (translation & rotation restrained)0.65
2Both ends fixed, free to translate (sway)1.20
3One end fixed, other end pinned0.80
4One end fixed, other end fixed but free to translate1.00
5One end fixed, other end free2.00
6Both ends pinned1.00

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Interpret Boundary Conditions:
    EndTranslation RestrainedRotation RestrainedSupport Type
    End 1YesYesFixed
    End 2YesNoPinned
  2. Match with IS 456:2000 Table 28:
    Row 3 — One end fixed, other end pinned → \(k = 0.80\)

Sanity Check: The progression \(0.65 < 0.80 < 1.00 < 2.00\) is physically consistent with decreasing end restraint (Fixed-Fixed → Fixed-Pinned → Pinned-Pinned → Fixed-Free).

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Effective length factor = 0.80 | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: As per IS 456 : 2000, the minimum percentage of tension reinforcement (up to two decimal places) required in reinforced-concrete beams of rectangular cross-section (considering effective depth in the calculation of area) using Fe500 grade steel is ______
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Minimum Tension Reinforcement per IS 456:2000

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: Rectangular beam; Steel grade Fe500 (\(f_y = 500\text{ MPa}\)); area calculated using effective depth \(d\); Code: IS 456:2000.
  • Aim: Calculate minimum percentage of tension reinforcement (to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 Clause 26.5.1.1: Minimum tension reinforcement:\[\dfrac{A_{st,min}}{b \times d} = \dfrac{0.85}{f_y}\]Minimum percentage reinforcement:\[p_{t,min} = \dfrac{0.85}{f_y} \times 100\]

Critical Note: The question specifies "using effective depth in calculation of area" → denominator is \(b \times d\) (not \(b \times D\)).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply IS 456:2000 Clause 26.5.1.1:\[p_{t,min} = \dfrac{0.85}{f_y} \times 100\]
  2. Substitute \(f_y = 500\text{ MPa}\):\[p_{t,min} = \dfrac{0.85}{500} \times 100 = 0.0017 \times 100 = 0.17\%\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.17% | Accepted range: 0.17 to 0.17

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q22
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: A reinforced-concrete slab with effective depth of 80 mm is simply supported at two opposite ends on 230 mm thick masonry walls. The centre-to-centre distance between the walls is 3.3 m. As per IS 456 : 2000, the effective span of the slab (in m, up to two decimal places) is ______
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Effective Span of Slabs per IS 456:2000

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Slab effective depth: \(d = 80\text{ mm} = 0.08\text{ m}\)
    • Support width (masonry wall): \(230\text{ mm} = 0.23\text{ m}\)
    • Centre-to-centre distance between walls: \(3.3\text{ m}\)
    • Code: IS 456:2000
  • Aim: Calculate effective span of simply supported slab (in m).

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 Clause 22.2(a): Effective span for simply supported slabs:\[l_{eff} = \min\left\{l_0 + d,\ \text{centre-to-centre of supports}\right\}\]where \(l_0\) = clear span, \(d\) = effective depth of slab.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate clear span (\(l_0\)):\[l_0 = 3.3 - 0.23 = 3.07\text{ m}\]
  2. First candidate (clear span + effective depth):\[l_1 = l_0 + d = 3.07 + 0.08 = 3.15\text{ m}\]
  3. Second candidate (c/c distance):\[l_2 = 3.3\text{ m}\]
  4. Apply IS 456:2000 Clause 22.2(a):\[l_{eff} = \min\{3.15,\ 3.3\} = 3.15\text{ m}\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.15 m | Accepted range: 3.15 to 3.15

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: A fillet weld is simultaneously subjected to factored normal and shear stresses of 120 MPa and 50 MPa, respectively. As per IS 800 : 2007, the equivalent stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) is ______
questions.explanation:
Steel Design | Equivalent Stress in Fillet Welds per IS 800:2007

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Factored normal stress: \(f_a = 120\text{ MPa}\)
    • Factored shear stress: \(q = 50\text{ MPa}\)
    • Code: IS 800:2007
  • Aim: Calculate equivalent stress in fillet weld (in MPa).

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007 Clause 10.5.10.1.1: Equivalent stress for combined loading in fillet welds:\[f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + 3q^2}\]where \(f_a\) = normal stress perpendicular to weld throat; \(q\) = shear stress on weld throat.

Pitfall: Do not use \(f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + q^2}\) — the factor of 3 with the shear term is essential (von Mises criterion).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Write the formula:\[f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + 3q^2}\]
  2. Substitute values:\[f_e = \sqrt{(120)^2 + 3 \times (50)^2}\]
  3. Compute terms:\[(120)^2 = 14400, \quad (50)^2 = 2500, \quad 3 \times 2500 = 7500\]
  4. Sum and evaluate:\[f_e = \sqrt{14400 + 7500} = \sqrt{21900} = 147.99\text{ MPa}\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 147.99 MPa | Accepted range: 147.50 to 148.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question:
Four bolts P, Q, R and S of equal diameter are used for a bracket subjected to a load of 130 kN as shown in the figure.



The force in bolt P is
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Steel Structures (Bolted Connections)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Four bolts arranged in a rectangle: P, Q, R, S
    • Eccentric load (\(P\)) = 130 kN acting vertically downwards
    • Horizontal gauge distance between bolts = 100 mm
    • Vertical pitch distance between bolts = 240 mm
    • Eccentricity (\(e\)) of the load from the centre-line of the bolt group = 200 mm
  • Aim: To find the resultant force on the most stressed bolt (Bolt P).

3. Core Concepts:

Eccentric Bolted Connection (In-plane bending): An eccentric load \(P\) can be resolved into a direct downward shear force acting at the centre of gravity (CG) of the bolt group, and a twisting moment \(M = P \times e\).

Direct Shear Force (\(F_d\)): Distributed equally among all identical bolts: \(F_d = \dfrac{P}{n}\), acting parallel to the applied load.

Torsional Shear Force (\(F_t\)): Proportional to the radial distance (\(r\)) of the bolt from the CG: \(F_t = \dfrac{M \cdot r}{\sum r^2}\). Its direction is perpendicular to the radial vector.

Resultant Force (\(F_R\)): Vector sum of \(F_d\) and \(F_t\) using Cartesian components.

4. Solution Method:

  • Identify the coordinates of Bolt P relative to the CG to find its radial distance \(r\).
  • Compute the direct shear force component \(F_{dy}\).
  • Compute the torsional moment \(M\).
  • Determine the \(x\) and \(y\) components of the torsional shear force (\(F_{tx}\) and \(F_{ty}\)) for Bolt P.
  • Calculate the resultant force \(F_R\) using the combined orthogonal components.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Geometry of the Bolt Group:
    Taking the CG of the 4 bolts as the origin \((0,0)\):
    • Horizontal distance from CG to bolt: \(x = \dfrac{100}{2} = 50\text{ mm}\)
    • Vertical distance from CG to bolt: \(y = \dfrac{240}{2} = 120\text{ mm}\)
    • Radial distance squared for one bolt: \(r^2 = x^2 + y^2 = 50^2 + 120^2 = 2500 + 14400 = 16900\text{ mm}^2\)
    • For 4 bolts: \(\sum r^2 = 4 \times 16900 = 67600\text{ mm}^2\)
  2. Direct Shear Force (\(F_d\)):\[F_{d} = \dfrac{P}{n} = \dfrac{130\text{ kN}}{4} = 32.5\text{ kN}\](Acts vertically downwards, so \(F_{dy} = 32.5\text{ kN}\))
  3. Torsional Shear Force on Bolt P:
    • Moment: \(M = P \times e = 130\text{ kN} \times 200\text{ mm} = 26000\text{ kN·mm}\) (Clockwise)
    • Bolt P is in the top-right quadrant at \((50, 120)\). Since \(M\) is clockwise, the torsional force vector at P points rightward and downward.
    • Horizontal component: \(F_{tx} = \dfrac{M \cdot y}{\sum r^2} = \dfrac{26000 \times 120}{67600} = 46.154\text{ kN}\) (Rightwards)
    • Vertical component: \(F_{ty} = \dfrac{M \cdot x}{\sum r^2} = \dfrac{26000 \times 50}{67600} = 19.231\text{ kN}\) (Downwards)
  4. Resultant Force on Bolt P (\(F_R\)):
    • Total horizontal force: \(\Sigma F_x = F_{tx} = 46.154\text{ kN}\)
    • Total vertical force: \(\Sigma F_y = F_{dy} + F_{ty} = 32.5 + 19.231 = 51.731\text{ kN}\)
    \[F_R = \sqrt{(\Sigma F_x)^2 + (\Sigma F_y)^2} = \sqrt{(46.154)^2 + (51.731)^2}\]\[F_R = \sqrt{2130.19 + 2676.10} = \sqrt{4806.29} \approx 69.32\text{ kN}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 69.32 kN | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: A singly-reinforced rectangular concrete beam of width 300 mm and effective depth 400 mm is to be designed using M25 grade concrete and Fe500 grade reinforcing steel. For the beam to be under-reinforced, the maximum number of 16 mm diameter reinforcing bars that can be provided is
questions.explanation:
Civil Engineering | Reinforced Concrete Design (Limit State Method)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Width of beam (\(b\)) = 300 mm
    • Effective depth (\(d\)) = 400 mm
    • Concrete Grade = M25 (\(f_{ck} = 25\text{ MPa}\))
    • Steel Grade = Fe500 (\(f_y = 500\text{ MPa}\))
    • Bar diameter (\(\phi\)) = 16 mm
  • Aim: To determine the maximum integer number of 16 mm bars that keeps the beam strictly under-reinforced (\(A_{st} \le A_{st,lim}\)).

3. Core Concepts (IS 456:2000):

Limiting Neutral Axis Depth (\(x_{u,max}\)): For Fe500, \(x_{u,max} = 0.46d\) (IS 456:2000, Clause 38.1).

Balanced Section: The maximum area of tension steel (\(A_{st,lim}\)) allowed before a section becomes over-reinforced is found by equating total compression to total tension at the limiting neutral axis depth.

  • Compressive force: \(C = 0.36\, f_{ck}\, b\, x_{u,max}\)
  • Tensile force: \(T = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st,lim}\)

Under-Reinforced Condition: Requires provided steel area \(A_{st} \le A_{st,lim}\).

4. Solution Method:

  • Calculate \(x_{u,max}\).
  • Equate \(C = T\) to compute the limiting area of steel \(A_{st,lim}\).
  • Calculate the cross-sectional area of a single 16 mm bar (\(a_{st}\)).
  • Divide \(A_{st,lim}\) by \(a_{st}\) to find the limiting number of bars.
  • Round down to the nearest whole integer to ensure the section stays under-reinforced.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Limiting Neutral Axis (\(x_{u,max}\)):\[x_{u,max} = 0.46 \times 400\text{ mm} = 184\text{ mm}\]
  2. Limiting Area of Steel (\(A_{st,lim}\)):
    Equating forces \(C = T\):\[0.36\, f_{ck}\, b\, x_{u,max} = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st,lim}\]\[0.36 \times 25 \times 300 \times 184 = 0.87 \times 500 \times A_{st,lim}\]\[496800\text{ N} = 435 \cdot A_{st,lim}\]\[A_{st,lim} = \dfrac{496800}{435} = 1142.07\text{ mm}^2\]
  3. Area of one 16 mm bar (\(a_{st}\)):\[a_{st} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (16)^2 \approx 201.06\text{ mm}^2\]
  4. Maximum Number of Bars (\(n\)):\[n = \dfrac{A_{st,lim}}{a_{st}} = \dfrac{1142.07}{201.06} = 5.68\text{ bars}\]Since an integer number of bars is required, and providing 6 bars (\(6 \times 201.06 = 1206.36\text{ mm}^2\)) would exceed the limit and make the section over-reinforced, we must round down.\[n_{max} = 5\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5 | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
A 6 m long simply-supported beam is prestressed as shown in the figure.



The beam carries a uniformly distributed load of 6 kN/m over its entire span. If the effective flexural rigidity \( EI = 2 \times 10^4 \text{ kNm}^2 \) and the effective prestressing force is 200 kN, the net increase in length of the prestressing cable (in mm, up to two decimal places) is ______
questions.explanation:
Pre-stressed Concrete | Deflection & Strain

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Simply-supported span: \(L = 6\text{ m}\)
    • Effective flexural rigidity: \(EI = 2 \times 10^4\text{ kNm}^2\)
    • Effective prestressing force: \(P = 200\text{ kN}\)
    • Constant eccentricity: \(e = 50\text{ mm} = 0.05\text{ m}\) (below the neutral axis)
    • Applied UDL: \(w = 6\text{ kN/m}\) over entire span
  • Aim: Calculate the net increase in length of the prestressing cable (in mm) strictly due to flexural curvature.

3. Core Concepts:

Flexural Strain: The longitudinal strain at depth \(y\) from the neutral axis due to pure bending is:\[\varepsilon_x = \dfrac{y}{\rho} = \dfrac{M_{net} \cdot y}{EI}\]

Cable Elongation: The change in length of a fiber (cable) at eccentricity \(e\) from the neutral axis is the integral of bending strain across the span:\[\Delta L = \int_{0}^{L} \varepsilon_x\, dx = \int_{0}^{L} \dfrac{M_{net} \cdot e}{EI}\, dx = \dfrac{e}{EI} \int_{0}^{L} M_{net}\, dx\]

Note: Since the cross-sectional area \(A\) is not provided, the primary uniform axial compressive shortening (\(-PL/AE\)) is considered negligible compared to bending deformation.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify moments: Applied downward UDL causes positive (sagging) bending; prestress force causes negative (hogging) bending.
  2. The integral \(\displaystyle \int M_{net}\,dx\) is equivalent to calculating the net Area of the Bending Moment Diagrams (BMD).
  3. Compute area of UDL BMD and area of Prestress BMD.
  4. Use the derived flexural strain formula to find the elongation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Area of Moment Diagram due to UDL (\(A_1\)):
    The BMD for UDL is a parabola with maximum ordinate \(M_{max} = \dfrac{wL^2}{8}\).\[A_1 = \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot L \cdot M_{max} = \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot L \cdot \dfrac{wL^2}{8} = \dfrac{wL^3}{12}\]\[A_1 = \dfrac{6 \times 6^3}{12} = \dfrac{6 \times 216}{12} = 108\text{ kNm}^2\quad\text{(tension at cable level)}\]
  2. Area of Moment Diagram due to Prestress (\(A_2\)):
    The BMD for a straight eccentric cable is a rectangle with constant ordinate \(M_p = P \cdot e\).\[A_2 = P \cdot e \cdot L = 200 \times 0.05 \times 6 = 60\text{ kNm}^2\quad\text{(compression at cable level)}\]
  3. Net Bending Moment Area (\(A_{net}\)):\[A_{net} = A_1 - A_2 = 108 - 60 = 48\text{ kNm}^2\]
  4. Net Increase in Cable Length (\(\Delta L\)):\[\Delta L = \dfrac{A_{net} \cdot e}{EI} = \dfrac{48 \times 0.05}{2 \times 10^4} = \dfrac{2.4}{20000} = 0.00012\text{ m}\]Convert to mm: \(0.00012 \times 1000 = 0.12\text{ mm}\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.12 mm | Accepted key range: 0.10 to 0.12
