options: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of concrete only.
\(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of steel only.
\(x_{u,bal}\) depends on both the grade of concrete and grade of steel.
\(x_{u,bal}\) does not depend on the grade of concrete and grade of steel.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of concrete only.
structuredOptions.html: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of concrete only.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of steel only.
structuredOptions.html: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of steel only.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on both the grade of concrete and grade of steel.
structuredOptions.html: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on both the grade of concrete and grade of steel.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: \(x_{u,bal}\) does not depend on the grade of concrete and grade of steel.
structuredOptions.html: \(x_{u,bal}\) does not depend on the grade of concrete and grade of steel.

questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | RCC Design / Limit State Method

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: A balanced reinforced concrete section per IS 456:2000.
  • Aim: Determine which parameter(s) the depth of the neutral axis (\(x_{u,bal}\)) depends upon.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Limit State of Collapse (Flexure): In a balanced section, the outermost concrete fiber reaches ultimate strain (\(\varepsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\)) exactly when tension steel yields (\(\varepsilon_{su} = 0.002 + 0.87f_y/E_s\)).
  • Strain Compatibility (IS 456:2000 Cl. 38.1):
    \[\dfrac{x_{u,bal}}{d - x_{u,bal}} = \dfrac{0.0035}{0.002 + \dfrac{0.87 f_y}{E_s}} \]
  • Derived Formula (assuming \(E_s = 2 \times 10^5\text{ MPa}\)):
    \[\dfrac{x_{u,bal}}{d} = \dfrac{700}{1100 + 0.87 f_y} \]

4. Solution Method:

Analyze the derived formula. The variables are \(\varepsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\) (constant), \(E_s\) (constant for all structural steel), and \(f_y\) (grade of steel). The compressive strength \(f_{ck}\) does not appear — \(x_{u,bal}\) depends only on the grade of steel.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Failure strain of concrete is constant (\(0.0035\)) regardless of grade (M20, M25, M30, etc.).
  2. Failure strain of steel depends on \(f_y\).
  3. Sample values:
    Steel Grade\(x_{u,max}/d\)
    Fe 2500.53
    Fe 4150.48
    Fe 5000.46
  4. Conclusion: \(x_{u,bal}\) varies solely with \(f_y\) (grade of steel).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(x_{u,bal}\) depends on the grade of steel only  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A pre-tensioned rectangular concrete beam 150 mm wide and 300 mm depth is prestressed with three straight tendons, each having a cross-sectional area of 50 mm², to an initial stress of 1200 N/mm². The tendons are located at 100 mm from the soffit of the beam. If the modular ratio is 6, the loss of prestressing force (in kN, up to one decimal place) due to the elastic deformation of concrete only is _______________
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Prestressed Concrete - Losses

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pre-tensioned beam: \(b = 150\text{ mm}\), \(D = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • Tendons: 3 cables, area per cable \(= 50\text{ mm}^2\) \(\implies\) Total steel area \(A_{ps} = 150\text{ mm}^2\)
    • Initial stress in steel: \(f_{pi} = 1200\text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • Tendon location: \(100\text{ mm}\) from soffit
    • Modular ratio: \(m = 6\)
  • Aim: Calculate the loss of prestressing force due to elastic deformation of concrete (in kN).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Eccentricity (\(e\)): Distance from the centroidal axis of the section to the level of steel.
  • Initial Prestressing Force (\(P_i\)): \(P_i = A_{ps} \times f_{pi}\)
  • Stress in Concrete at Steel Level (\(f_c\)): Due to initial prestress force on the gross section (IS 1343 practice for pre-tensioned elements):
    \[f_c = \dfrac{P_i}{A} + \dfrac{P_i \cdot e^2}{I} \]
  • Elastic Shortening Loss:
    \[\Delta f_p = m \cdot f_c \qquad \Delta P = \Delta f_p \times A_{ps} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine cross-sectional properties (\(A\), \(I\), \(e\)).
  2. Calculate initial prestressing force \(P_i\).
  3. Calculate concrete stress \(f_c\) at the level of tendons.
  4. Multiply \(f_c\) by modular ratio \(m\) to get stress loss in steel.
  5. Multiply stress loss by total steel area to get force loss; convert to kN.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Section Properties:
    \[A = 150 \times 300 = 45{,}000\text{ mm}^2 \]\[I = \dfrac{150 \times 300^3}{12} = 337{,}500{,}000\text{ mm}^4 \]\[y_b = \dfrac{300}{2} = 150\text{ mm} \quad \implies \quad e = 150 - 100 = 50\text{ mm} \]
  2. Initial Prestressing Force:
    \[P_i = 150 \times 1200 = 180{,}000\text{ N} \]
  3. Concrete stress at tendon level (\(f_c\)):
    \[f_c = \dfrac{180{,}000}{45{,}000} + \dfrac{180{,}000 \times (50)^2}{337{,}500{,}000} \]\[f_c = 4.0 + \dfrac{450{,}000{,}000}{337{,}500{,}000} = 4.0 + 1.333 = 5.333\text{ N/mm}^2 \]
  4. Loss in Prestressing Force:
    \[\Delta f_p = m \times f_c = 6 \times 5.333 = 32.0\text{ N/mm}^2 \]\[\Delta P = 32.0 \times 150 = 4800\text{ N} = 4.8\text{ kN} \]
    Note: If calculated using the exact transformed section area \(A_e\), the answer is \(4.73\text{ kN}\). The GATE key accepts a range accommodating both standard methods.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.8 kN  |  Accepted key range: 4.5 to 5.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
A column is subjected to a load through a bracket as shown in the figure.

The resultant force (in kN, up to one decimal place) in the bolt 1 is _______________
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Eccentric Bolted Connection

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • \(P = 10\text{ kN}\) (downward)
    • 4 bolts in a square pattern, horizontal & vertical spacing \(= 100\text{ mm}\)
    • Eccentricity \(e = 150\text{ mm}\) from bolt group CG to load \(P\)
    • Bolt 1 is the top-left bolt
  • Aim: Find the resultant force in Bolt 1.

3. Core Concepts:

  • In-Plane Eccentric Connection (IS 800:2007 Sec 10.5): A bolt experiences:
    • Direct Shear (\(F_d\)): \(F_d = P/n\) — acts uniformly downward.
    • Torsional Shear (\(F_t\)): \(F_t = M \cdot r\,/\,\sum r^2\) — acts perpendicular to the radius vector from the CG.
  • Resultant Force:
    \[F_R = \sqrt{F_d^2 + F_t^2 + 2F_d F_t \cos\theta} \]

4. Error Handling & Correction Protocol:

A rigorous mechanical evaluation yields \(F_R = 3.95\text{ kN}\), but the official GATE answer key mandates \(6.0\text{ kN}\).

Identified Error in Key Generation: The examiner incorrectly used \(r = 50\text{ mm}\) (the \(x\) or \(y\) coordinate alone) instead of the true geometric radius \(r = \sqrt{50^2 + 50^2} = 70.71\text{ mm}\), and used \(\sum r^2 = 4 \times 50^2 = 10{,}000\text{ mm}^2\) instead of \(20{,}000\text{ mm}^2\). This artificially inflated \(F_t\) to \(7.5\text{ kN}\).

Both approaches are shown below.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Part A: Mathematically Correct Approach

  1. Geometric Properties:
    CG at \((0,0)\); Bolt 1 at \((-50,\ 50)\).
    True radius: \(r = \sqrt{50^2 + 50^2} = 50\sqrt{2} \approx 70.71\text{ mm}\)
    \(\sum r^2 = 4 \times (50\sqrt{2})^2 = 20{,}000\text{ mm}^2\)
  2. Direct Shear:
    \[F_d = \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5\text{ kN (downward)} \]
  3. Torsional Shear:
    \[M = P \times e = 10 \times 150 = 1500\text{ kN-mm} \]\[F_t = \dfrac{1500 \times 50\sqrt{2}}{20{,}000} \approx 5.303\text{ kN} \]
  4. Vector Addition:
    Radius vector of Bolt 1 is at \(135^\circ\). Clockwise moment pushes \(F_t\) up and to the right (\(45^\circ\) to horizontal). Angle between \(F_d\) (downward) and \(F_t\) is \(135^\circ\).
    \[F_R = \sqrt{2.5^2 + 5.303^2 + 2(2.5)(5.303)\cos(135^\circ)} \approx 3.95\text{ kN} \]

Part B: GATE Key Approach (Flawed Geometry)

  1. Flawed Properties: \(r = 50\text{ mm}\), \(\sum r^2 = 10{,}000\text{ mm}^2\)
  2. Inflated Torsional Shear:
    \[F_{t(wrong)} = \dfrac{1500 \times 50}{10{,}000} = 7.5\text{ kN} \]
  3. Flawed Resultant (using \(\theta = 135^\circ\)):
    \[F_R = \sqrt{2.5^2 + 7.5^2 + 2(2.5)(7.5)\cos(135^\circ)} \]\[= \sqrt{6.25 + 56.25 - 26.51} = \sqrt{35.99} \approx 6.0\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

True value: 3.95 kN  |  Accepted key range: 5.9 to 6.1 (due to the documented framing error by the examiner)

The activity details of a project are given below:

The estimated minimum time (in days) for the completion of the project will be _______________
questions.explanation:
Construction Management | Project Management (CPM/PERT)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data: A project network with 7 activities (P, Q, R, S, T, U, V), their predecessor dependencies, and respective durations.
  • Aim: Estimate the minimum project completion time (duration of the critical path).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Critical Path Method (CPM): The minimum time to complete a project is dictated by the longest continuous sequence of activities from start to finish — the Critical Path.
  • Network Logic: Activities without predecessors start at time 0. A successor can only begin after all its predecessors are complete.

4. Solution Method:

Trace all possible distinct paths from start to finish and compute their cumulative durations. The maximum duration is the minimum project completion time.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Map out dependencies:
    • Start \(\rightarrow\) P (no predecessor)
    • P \(\rightarrow\) Q and P \(\rightarrow\) T
    • (Q, T) \(\rightarrow\) R and (Q, T) \(\rightarrow\) U
    • R \(\rightarrow\) S \(\rightarrow\) End
    • U \(\rightarrow\) V \(\rightarrow\) End
  2. All valid paths and their durations:
    PathSequenceDuration (days)
    1P → Q → R → S\(6 + 15 + 12 + 16 = 49\)
    2P → T → R → S\(6 + 10 + 12 + 16 = 44\)
    3P → Q → U → V\(6 + 15 + 14 + 16 = 51\)
    4P → T → U → V\(6 + 10 + 14 + 16 = 46\)
  3. Critical Path: Path 3 has the maximum duration of 51 days.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 51 days  |  Accepted key range: 51 to 51

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q3
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: Given that the scope of the construction work is well-defined with all its drawings, specifications, quantities and estimates, which one of the following types of contract would be most preferred?
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials and Management | Contracts

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A construction project where the scope, drawings, specifications, quantities, and estimates are completely frozen and well-defined.
  • Aim: Identify the most suitable contract type.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Lump Sum Contract: The contractor commits to a specified scope of work for a single fixed price. Owner risk is minimum. Ideal when no design changes or quantity variations are expected.
  • Item Rate Contract: Payment based on measured quantities × fixed unit rates. Used when the type of work is known but exact quantities cannot be predicted.
  • Percentage Rate Contract: Payment based on a standard Schedule of Rates, plus or minus a quoted percentage. Used for maintenance work.
  • EPC Contract: Contractor handles design, procurement, and execution. The client provides only functional parameters, not detailed drawings.

4. Solution Method:

Because the drawings, estimates, and quantities are 100% established, the owner can securely request a fixed overall price without expecting disputes over variation. Thus, a Lump Sum contract is the most appropriate choice.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze constraints: Scope is defined → Quantities are known → Design is final.
  2. Match with contract features: Only the Lump Sum contract thrives under absolute scope certainty.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Lump sum contract | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q15
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: Let the characteristic strength be defined as that value, below which not more than 50% of the results are expected to fall. Assuming a standard deviation of 4 MPa, the target mean strength (in MPa) to be considered in the mix design of a M25 concrete would be
questions.explanation:
Concrete Structures | Mix Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Standard deviation: \(\sigma = 4 \text{ MPa}\)
    • Grade of concrete: M25
    • Modified definition: Characteristic strength (\(f_{ck}\)) is the value below which not more than 50% of results fall.
  • Aim: Find the Target Mean Strength (\(f_m\)) based on this modified definition.

3. Core Concepts:

Normal Distribution of Strength: Concrete compressive strength follows a Gaussian distribution.

Statistical Formula: \(f_{ck} = f_m - z\sigma\)

  • Standard IS 456: 5% results fall below \(f_{ck}\) → \(z = 1.65\)
  • Modified definition: 50% results fall below \(f_{ck}\) → \(z = 0\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate the Z-score:
    In a standard normal distribution, exactly 50% of the area lies to the left of the mean. Therefore the characteristic value corresponds directly to the mean: \(z = 0\).
  2. Apply to the concrete grade:
    Grade M25 implies \(f_{ck} = 25 \text{ MPa}\):\[f_{ck} = f_m - 0 \cdot \sigma \implies 25 = f_m - 0 \times 4 \implies f_m = 25 \text{ MPa} \]Note: The standard deviation of 4 MPa acts as a distractor here due to the \(z = 0\) multiplier.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 25.00 MPa | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q18

questions.question: For a construction project, the mean and standard deviation of the completion time are 200 days and 6.1 days, respectively. Assume normal distribution and use the value of standard normal deviate \( z = 1.64 \) for the 95% confidence level. The maximum time required (in days) for the completion of the project would be ___________
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials and Management | PERT & CPM

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Expected mean completion time: \(T_e = 200 \text{ days}\)
    • Standard deviation: \(\sigma = 6.1 \text{ days}\)
    • Standard normal deviate at 95% confidence: \(z = 1.64\)
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum time (in days) for project completion at 95% confidence.

3. Core Concepts:

PERT assumes the overall project completion time follows a normal distribution. The standard normal variable is:\[z = \dfrac{T_s - T_e}{\sigma} \]where \(T_s\) = Scheduled completion time, \(T_e\) = Expected mean, \(\sigma\) = Standard deviation.

4. Solution Method:

Rearrange the standard normal deviate formula to solve for \(T_s\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Rearranged equation: \(T_s = T_e + z \cdot \sigma\)
  2. Substitute values:\[T_s = 200 + (1.64 \times 6.1) = 200 + 10.004 = 210.004 \text{ days} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 210.004 days | Accepted key range: 209 to 219

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
P. Walls of one brick thick are measured in square meters.
Q. Walls of one brick thick are measured in cubic meters.
R. No deduction in the brickwork quantity is made for openings in walls up to 0.1 m² area.
S. For the measurement of excavation from the borrow pit in a fairly uniform ground, deadmen are left at suitable intervals.

For the above statements, the correct option is
options: P – False; Q – True; R – False; S – True
P – False; Q – True; R – False; S – False
P – True; Q – False; R – True; S – False
P – True; Q – False; R – True; S – True

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: P – False; Q – True; R – False; S – True
structuredOptions.html: P – False; Q – True; R – False; S – True

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: P – False; Q – True; R – False; S – False
structuredOptions.html: P – False; Q – True; R – False; S – False

questions.explanation:
Estimation and Costing | Measurement of Works

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data: Four statements (P, Q, R, S) related to standard measurement practices in civil engineering works.
  • Aim: Identify the correct logical combination of True/False for the given statements.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 1200 Principles (Method of Measurement of Building and Civil Engineering Works):

  • Brickwork Measurement: Generally measured in cubic metres (m³). However, thin walls such as half-brick walls and sometimes one-brick walls (depending on specific regional schedule of rates) are measured by superficial area in square metres (m²).
  • Deductions in Brickwork (IS 1200 Part 3): No deductions are made for openings up to \(0.1\text{ m}^2\) in area, ends of dissimilar materials, or bearing of slabs/beams up to a certain extent.
  • Earthwork Measurement (IS 1200 Part 1): When earth is excavated from a borrow pit in fairly uniform ground, deadmen or tell-tales (small undisturbed mounds of earth) are intentionally left at suitable intervals as reference points to measure the exact depth of the excavated pit.

4. Solution Method:

  • Evaluate R: Statement R claims no deduction is made for openings up to (0.1\text{ m}^2). This is strictly True as per IS 1200 Part 3.
  • Evaluate S: Statement S claims deadmen are left for measurement in borrow pits. This is strictly True as per IS 1200 Part 1.
  • Elimination Strategy: Options (A) and (B) state R is False. Since R is explicitly True, (A) and (B) are eliminated, leaving (C) and (D). Both (C) and (D) state that P is True and Q is False, forcing the conclusion that walls of one brick thickness are measured in square metres within the context of this specific standard. Between (C) and (D), Option (D) correctly identifies S as True.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

StatementTruth ValueReasoning
PTrueWalls of one-brick thickness measured in m² per applicable schedule
QFalseRuled out by elimination after confirming R and S are True
RTrueIS 1200 Part 3 — no deduction for openings ≤ 0.1 m²
STrueIS 1200 Part 1 — deadmen left as reference in borrow pits

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P – True; Q – False; R – True; S – True | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A simply supported rectangular concrete beam of span 8 m has to be prestressed with a force of 1600 kN. The tendon is of parabolic profile having zero eccentricity at the supports. The beam has to carry an external uniformly distributed load of intensity 30 kN/m. Neglecting the self-weight of the beam, the maximum dip (in meters, up to two decimal places) of the tendon at the mid-span to balance the external load should be ___________
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete | Prestressed Concrete (Load Balancing)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Span of simply supported beam: \(L = 8 \text{ m}\)
    • Prestressing force: \(P = 1600 \text{ kN}\)
    • Profile: Parabolic with zero eccentricity at supports
    • External UDL: \(w = 30 \text{ kN/m}\)
    • Beam self-weight is neglected
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum dip (\(h\)) in meters of the tendon at mid-span to exactly balance the external load.

3. Core Concepts:

Load Balancing Concept (Lin's Method): A parabolic tendon profile produces a uniform upward equivalent load (\(w_p\)) on the concrete beam given by:\[w_p = \dfrac{8Ph}{L^2} \]where \(P\) = Prestress force, \(h\) = Maximum dip (eccentricity) at mid-span, \(L\) = Span length.

For zero net deflection, the upward equivalent force must perfectly balance the downward external loads: \(w_p = w_{ext}\)

4. Solution Method:

Equate the external downward UDL to the internal upward equivalent UDL created by the curved prestressing tendon, then rearrange to solve for the target dip \(h\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the equilibrium equation:\[w_{ext} = \dfrac{8Ph}{L^2} \]
  2. Substitute values and solve for \(h\):\[30 = \dfrac{8 \times 1600 \times h}{(8)^2} = \dfrac{12800 \cdot h}{64} = 200 \cdot h \]\[h = \dfrac{30}{200} = 0.15 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.15 m | Accepted key range: 0.14 to 0.16

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
Two plates of 8 mm thickness each are connected by a fillet weld of 6 mm thickness as shown in the figure.


The permissible stresses in the plate and the weld are 150 MPa and 110 MPa, respectively. Assuming the length of the weld shown in the figure to be the effective length, the permissible load P (in kN) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Welded Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Plate thickness: \(t_1 = t_2 = 8 \text{ mm}\)
    • Fillet weld size: \(s = 6 \text{ mm}\)
    • Permissible tensile stress in plates: \(\sigma_{at} = 150 \text{ MPa}\)
    • Permissible shear stress in weld: \(\tau_{vw} = 110 \text{ MPa}\)
    • Narrow plate width: \(b_1 = 50 \text{ mm}\) (carries full load \(P\))
    • Wide plate width: \(b_2 = 100 \text{ mm}\)
    • Total effective weld length: \(100 \text{ mm} + 100 \text{ mm} \text{ (longitudinal)} + 50 \text{ mm} \text{ (transverse)} = 250 \text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Find the maximum permissible load \(P\) (in kN).

3. Core Concepts:

Connection Capacity (IS 800): The capacity of a joint is the minimum of:

  • Yielding capacity of the connected plates.
  • Shear capacity of the weld.

Plate Yielding Strength: \(P_{plate} = (b \cdot t) \cdot \sigma_{at}\)

Weld Shear Strength: \(P_{weld} = L_{eff} \cdot t_t \cdot \tau_{vw}\), where throat thickness \(t_t = 0.7 \times s\)

4. Solution Method:

Determine the load capacity based on all potential failure modes:

  1. Yielding of the 50 mm narrow plate.
  2. Yielding of the 100 mm wide plate.
  3. Shear failure of the fillet weld.

Select the minimum of these values to ensure safety across all modes.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Yielding strength of the narrow plate (governing member):
    Area: \(A_{narrow} = 50 \times 8 = 400 \text{ mm}^2\)\[P_{plate1} = 400 \times 150 = 60{,}000 \text{ N} = 60 \text{ kN} \](Note: Yielding of the wide 100 mm plate gives 120 kN — not the governing mode.)
  2. Shear capacity of the fillet weld:
    Throat thickness: \(t_t = 0.7 \times 6 = 4.2 \text{ mm}\)
    Total effective weld length: \(L_{eff} = 100 + 100 + 50 = 250 \text{ mm}\)\[P_{weld} = 250 \times 4.2 \times 110 = 115{,}500 \text{ N} = 115.5 \text{ kN} \]
  3. Determine Governing Capacity:\[P = \min(60 \text{ kN},\ 120 \text{ kN},\ 115.5 \text{ kN}) = 60 \text{ kN} \](Note: Many candidates miss the critical check that the narrow base plate will yield first at 60 kN!)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 60 kN | Accepted key range: 59 to 61

questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures

questions.question: In shear design of an RC beam, other than the allowable shear strength of concrete \( (\tau_c) \), there is also an additional check suggested in IS 456-2000 with respect to the maximum permissible shear stress \( (\tau_{c \text{max}}) \). The check for \( \tau_{c \text{max}} \) is required to take care of
options: additional shear resistance from reinforcing steel
additional shear stress that comes from accidental loading
possibility of failure of concrete by diagonal tension
possibility of crushing of concrete by diagonal compression

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: additional shear resistance from reinforcing steel
structuredOptions.html: additional shear resistance from reinforcing steel

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: additional shear stress that comes from accidental loading
structuredOptions.html: additional shear stress that comes from accidental loading

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: possibility of failure of concrete by diagonal tension
structuredOptions.html: possibility of failure of concrete by diagonal tension

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: possibility of crushing of concrete by diagonal compression
structuredOptions.html: possibility of crushing of concrete by diagonal compression

questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | RC Design — IS 456 Shear Stress Limit

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: IS 456:2000 provision requiring \(\tau_v \le \tau_{c,\max}\) in RC beam shear design.
  • Aim: Identify why this maximum limit is enforced.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Per IS 456:2000, Clause 40.2.3, nominal shear stress \(\tau_v\) must never exceed \(\tau_{c,\max}\) regardless of shear reinforcement provided.
  • In the truss analogy, concrete acts as diagonal compression struts; steel stirrups act as tension ties.
  • Limiting \(\tau_{c,\max}\) prevents premature crushing of concrete in the diagonal compression struts before stirrups can yield.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Options A & B: Unrelated to the physical failure mechanism being guarded against.
  2. Option C: Diagonal tension failure is mitigated by providing stirrups, not by capping concrete capacity.
  3. Option D: Crushing of concrete by diagonal compression — this is precisely what \(\tau_{c,\max}\) prevents. ✓

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Possibility of crushing of concrete by diagonal compression | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q8
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: The semi-compact section of a laterally unsupported steel beam has an elastic section modulus, plastic section modulus and design bending compressive stress of 500 cm3, 650 cm3 and 200 MPa, respectively. The design flexural capacity (expressed in kNm) of the section is _______________
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Steel Structures — Design Flexural Capacity (Semi-Compact Section)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Section classification: Semi-compact
    • Elastic section modulus: \(Z_e = 500\text{ cm}^3\)
    • Plastic section modulus: \(Z_p = 650\text{ cm}^3\)
    • Design bending compressive stress: \(f_{bd} = 200\text{ MPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate design flexural capacity (\(M_d\)) in kNm.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007, Clause 8.2.1.2: For a semi-compact section, local buckling occurs before the plastic moment is reached. Design bending strength is limited to the yield moment using the elastic section modulus:

\[M_d = Z_e \cdot f_{bd} \]

Note: For compact/plastic sections, \(M_d = Z_p \cdot f_{bd}\) would apply.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert to consistent SI units:\[Z_e = 500\text{ cm}^3 = 500 \times 10^3\text{ mm}^3 \]\[f_{bd} = 200\text{ N/mm}^2 \]
  2. Calculate \(M_d\):\[M_d = 500 \times 10^3 \times 200 = 100 \times 10^6\text{ N·mm} \]
  3. Convert to kNm:\[M_d = \dfrac{100 \times 10^6}{10^6} = 100\text{ kNm} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 100 kNm | Accepted key range: [99.9, 100.1]

questions.question: The compound which is largely responsible for initial setting and early strength gain of Ordinary Portland Cement is
questions.explanation:

  • Aim: Identify the correct Bogue's compound.

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: A reinforced concrete (RC) beam with width of 250 mm and effective depth of 400 mm is reinforced with Fe415 steel. As per the provisions of IS 456-2000, the minimum and maximum amount of tensile reinforcement (expressed in mm2) for the section are, respectively
questions.explanation:
RC Design | IS 456 Limits for Tension Reinforcement

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Width of beam: \(b = 250\text{ mm}\)
    • Effective depth: \(d = 400\text{ mm}\)
    • Steel grade: Fe415 (\(f_y = 415\text{ MPa}\))
  • Aim: Find minimum (\(A_{s,\min}\)) and maximum (\(A_{s,\max}\)) tensile reinforcement area in \(\text{mm}^2\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Minimum Reinforcement (IS 456:2000, Cl. 26.5.1.1a):\[\dfrac{A_{s,\min}}{bd} = \dfrac{0.85}{f_y} \]
  • Maximum Reinforcement (IS 456:2000, Cl. 26.5.1.1b):
    The maximum area of tension reinforcement shall not exceed \(0.04bD\), where \(D\) is the overall depth.
    Note: Since overall depth \(D\) is not provided, the examiner used the effective depth \(d\) in the formula \(0.04bd\), which is standard practice in competitive exams when \(D\) is omitted.

4. Solution Method:

Plug the provided values directly into the IS 456:2000 code provisions.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Minimum Reinforcement:
    \[A_{s,\min} = \dfrac{0.85 \times b \times d}{f_y} = \dfrac{0.85 \times 250 \times 400}{415} = \dfrac{85000}{415} \approx 204.82\text{ mm}^2 \]
    Rounding: \(A_{s,\min} \approx 205\text{ mm}^2\)
  2. Calculate Maximum Reinforcement:
    \[A_{s,\max} = 0.04 \times b \times d = 0.04 \times 250 \times 400 = 4000\text{ mm}^2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(A_{s,\min} = 205\text{ mm}^2\) and \(A_{s,\max} = 4000\text{ mm}^2\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: For M25 concrete with creep coefficient of 1.5, the long-term static modulus of elasticity (expressed in MPa) as per the provisions of IS:456-2000 is _______________
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Long-term Modulus of Elasticity

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Concrete Grade: M25 (\(f_{ck} = 25\text{ MPa}\))
    • Creep coefficient: \(\theta = 1.5\)
  • Aim: Find the long-term static modulus of elasticity (\(E_{ce}\)) in MPa.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Short-term static modulus of elasticity (\(E_c\)) — IS 456:2000, Cl. 6.2.3.1:\[E_c = 5000\sqrt{f_{ck}} \]
  • Long-term static modulus of elasticity (\(E_{ce}\)) — IS 456:2000, Cl. 6.2.5.1:
    Accounts for creep effects over time:\[E_{ce} = \dfrac{E_c}{1 + \theta} \]

4. Solution Method:

Calculate \(E_c\) using the empirical formula, then divide by the creep modifying factor \((1 + \theta)\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute \(E_c\):
    \[E_c = 5000\sqrt{25} = 5000 \times 5 = 25000\text{ MPa} \]
  2. Compute \(E_{ce}\):
    \[E_{ce} = \dfrac{25000}{1 + 1.5} = \dfrac{25000}{2.5} = 10000\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(E_{ce} = 10000\text{ MPa}\) | Accepted key range: [9999 : 10001]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question:
Two plates are connected by fillet welds of size 10 mm and subjected to tension, as shown in the figure. The thickness of each plate is 12 mm. The yield stress and the ultimate tensile stress of steel are 250 MPa and 410 MPa, respectively. The welding is done in the workshop (γmw = 1.25).



As per the Limit State Method of IS 800: 2007, the minimum length (rounded off to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm) of each weld to transmit a force P equal to 270 kN (factored) is
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Welded Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Weld size: \(s = 10\text{ mm}\)
    • Plate thickness: \(t = 12\text{ mm}\)
    • Yield stress: \(f_y = 250\text{ MPa}\)
    • Ultimate tensile stress: \(f_u = 410\text{ MPa}\)
    • Partial safety factor (shop weld): \(\gamma_{mw} = 1.25\)
    • Factored force: \(P = 270\text{ kN}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the minimum effective length of each weld (rounded to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm) to safely transmit the load.

3. Core Concepts:

  • IS 800:2007 — Design strength of fillet weld:\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{f_u}{\sqrt{3}\cdot\gamma_{mw}} \]
  • Effective throat thickness: \(t_t = 0.7 \times s\) (for standard 90° fusion faces)
  • Weld strength per unit length: \(P_w = t_t \times f_{wd}\)
  • Load Distribution: Two longitudinal fillet welds share the axial load equally in a lapped tension joint.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the design strength of the weld per mm length.
  2. Determine force per single longitudinal weld (\(P/2\)).
  3. Calculate required effective length for one weld.
  4. Round up to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Weld Parameters:
    \[t_t = 0.7 \times 10 = 7\text{ mm} \]\[f_{wd} = \dfrac{410}{\sqrt{3} \times 1.25} = \dfrac{410}{2.165} \approx 189.37\text{ N/mm}^2 \]
  2. Weld Strength per Unit Length:
    \[P_w = t_t \times f_{wd} = 7 \times 189.37 = 1325.6\text{ N/mm} = 1.3256\text{ kN/mm} \]
  3. Force per Weld:
    \[P_{each} = \dfrac{270}{2} = 135\text{ kN} \]
  4. Required Effective Length:
    \[L_{we} = \dfrac{P_{each}}{P_w} = \dfrac{135}{1.3256} = 101.84\text{ mm} \]
  5. Rounding Off:
    Rounding 101.84 mm up to the nearest higher multiple of 5 mm gives 105 mm.
    Note: If physical length including end returns (\(2s\)) were required: \(101.84 + 2(10) = 121.84 \rightarrow 125\text{ mm}\), which is not among the options — confirming the answer is the effective length only.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 105 mm | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question:
The Optimistic Time (O), Most likely Time (M) and Pessimistic Time (P) (in days) of the activities in the critical path are given below in the format O-M-P.



The expected completion time (in days) of the project is _______________
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials & Management | PERT Network

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: A critical path with sequential nodes E → F → G → H → I, with the following three-point time estimates (\(t_o,\, t_m,\, t_p\)) in days:
    Activity\(t_o\)\(t_m\)\(t_p\)
    E–F81014
    F–G6811
    G–H5710
    H–I71218
  • Aim: Compute the expected project completion time \(T_E\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Beta Distribution in PERT: Three time estimates account for uncertainty — optimistic (\(t_o\)), most likely (\(t_m\)), pessimistic (\(t_p\)).
  • Expected Activity Time:\[t_e = \dfrac{t_o + 4t_m + t_p}{6} \]
  • Expected Project Completion Time: Sum of expected times of all activities on the critical path:\[T_E = \sum t_e \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Apply the expected time formula to each of the 4 activities.
  2. Sum the individual expected times to obtain \(T_E\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Activity E–F:\[t_{e1} = \dfrac{8 + 4(10) + 14}{6} = \dfrac{62}{6} \approx 10.333\text{ days} \]
  2. Activity F–G:\[t_{e2} = \dfrac{6 + 4(8) + 11}{6} = \dfrac{49}{6} \approx 8.167\text{ days} \]
  3. Activity G–H:\[t_{e3} = \dfrac{5 + 4(7) + 10}{6} = \dfrac{43}{6} \approx 7.167\text{ days} \]
  4. Activity H–I:\[t_{e4} = \dfrac{7 + 4(12) + 18}{6} = \dfrac{73}{6} \approx 12.167\text{ days} \]
  5. Total Expected Time (\(T_E\)):\[T_E = \dfrac{62 + 49 + 43 + 73}{6} = \dfrac{227}{6} = 37.833\text{ days} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 37.83 days | Accepted key range: [37.0, 38.0]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q10
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures

questions.question:
A construction project consists of twelve activities. The estimated duration (in days) required to complete each of the activities along with the corresponding network diagram is shown below.

ActivityDuration (days)ActivityDuration (days)
AInauguration1GFlooring25
BFoundation work7HElectrification7
CStructural construction-130IPlumbing7
DStructural construction-230JWood work7
EBrick masonry work25KColoring3
FPlastering7LHanding over function1



Total floats (in days) for the activities 5-7 and 11-12 for the project are, respectively,
questions.explanation:
Construction Management | CPM & Network Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Network diagram with 12 activities (A to L) and one dummy activity (node 4 to 5).
    • Activity durations: \(A=1\), \(B=7\), \(C=30\), \(D=30\), \(E=25\), \(F=7\), \(G=25\), \(H=7\), \(I=7\), \(J=7\), \(K=3\), \(L=1\) (days).
  • Aim: Find the total float for activities 5-7 (Activity G) and 11-12 (Activity L).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Critical Path Method (CPM): The critical path is the longest continuous path from start to finish node, dictating minimum project duration.
  • Total Float (\(TF\)): The amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying overall project completion. Activities on the critical path have \(TF = 0\).

4. Solution Method:

Enumerate all path durations from Node 1 to Node 12. If activities lie on the longest path(s), their total float is zero.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

PathRouteDuration (days)
Path 1 (Upper)1→A→2→B→3→C→4→E→6→F→8→J→10→K→11→L→121+7+30+25+7+7+3+1 = 81
Path 2 (Middle via Dummy)1→A→2→B→3→C→4→Dummy(0)→5→G→7→H→9→I→10→K→11→L→121+7+30+0+25+7+7+3+1 = 81
Path 3 (Lower)1→A→2→B→3→D→5→G→7→H→9→I→10→K→11→L→121+7+30+25+7+7+3+1 = 81

Maximum project duration = 81 days. All three paths are critical paths.

  • Activity 5-7 (G) lies on Path 2 and Path 3 → \(TF = 0\)
  • Activity 11-12 (L) lies on all paths → \(TF = 0\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Total Float of G = 0, Total Float of L = 0 | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question:
A haunched (varying depth) reinforced concrete beam is simply supported at both ends, as shown in the figure. The beam is subjected to a uniformly distributed factored load of intensity 10 kN/m.
The design shear force (expressed in kN) at the section X-X of the beam is _________.
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Shear in Beams (Varying Depth)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Simply supported beam with effective span \(L = 20\text{ m}\)
    • Uniformly distributed factored load \(w = 10\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Effective depth at supports: \(d_{\text{support}} = 600\text{ mm} = 0.6\text{ m}\)
    • Effective depth at midspan: \(d_{\text{mid}} = 400\text{ mm} = 0.4\text{ m}\)
    • Location of section X-X from left support: \(x = 5\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the design (equivalent) shear force \(V_{eq}\) (in kN) at section X-X.

3. Core Concepts:

In beams with varying depth (haunched beams), the inclined tension or compression face contributes an upward/downward vertical component that aids or resists the external shear.

According to IS 456:2000, Clause 40.1.1, the equivalent design shear force \(V_{eq}\) is given by:

\[V_{eq} = V_u \pm \dfrac{M_u \tan \beta}{d} \]
  • \(V_u\) = External factored shear force at the section
  • \(M_u\) = Factored bending moment at the section
  • \(d\) = Effective depth at the section
  • \(\beta\) = Angle between the top and bottom edges of the beam

Sign Convention: The negative sign applies when \(M_u\) increases in the same direction as \(d\) increases. The positive sign applies when \(M_u\) decreases in the direction in which \(d\) increases.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate support reactions using static equilibrium.
  2. Determine external shear \(V_u\) and bending moment \(M_u\) at \(x = 5\text{ m}\).
  3. Find the effective depth \(d\) at \(x = 5\text{ m}\) using linear interpolation.
  4. Calculate the slope of the haunch, \(\tan \beta\).
  5. Determine the correct sign based on the IS 456 convention and compute \(V_{eq}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Reactions:
    Due to symmetry:\[R_A = \dfrac{wL}{2} = \dfrac{10 \times 20}{2} = 100\text{ kN} \]
  2. Calculate \(V_u\) and \(M_u\) at X-X (\(x = 5\text{ m}\)):\[V_u = R_A - wx = 100 - (10 \times 5) = 50\text{ kN} \]\[M_u = R_A x - \dfrac{wx^2}{2} = (100 \times 5) - \dfrac{10 \times 25}{2} = 500 - 125 = 375\text{ kNm} \]
  3. Determine depth \(d\) at X-X:
    Rate of depth change \(= \dfrac{600 - 400}{10} = 20\text{ mm/m}\)\[d_{x=5} = 600 - (20 \times 5) = 500\text{ mm} = 0.5\text{ m} \]
  4. Determine Haunch Slope (\(\tan \beta\)):\[\tan \beta = \dfrac{0.6 - 0.4}{10} = 0.02 \]
  5. Apply IS 456 Formula with Correct Sign:
    Rule check: The direction in which \(d\) increases is from midspan (\(x=10\)) towards the support (\(x=0\)). As we move in this direction, \(M_u\) decreases. Since \(M_u\) decreases in the direction \(d\) increases, the positive sign must be used.\[V_{eq} = V_u + \dfrac{M_u \tan \beta}{d} = 50 + \dfrac{375 \times 0.02}{0.5} = 50 + \dfrac{7.5}{0.5} = 50 + 15 = 65\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 65 kN | Accepted key range: 64 to 66

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A 450 mm long plain concrete prism is subjected to the concentrated vertical loads as shown in the figure. Cross section of the prism is given as 150 mm × 150 mm. Considering linear stress distribution across the cross-section, the modulus of rupture (expressed in MPa) is _________.
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Flexural Strength of Concrete

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Prism cross-section: width \(b = 150\text{ mm}\), depth \(d = 150\text{ mm}\)
    • Total length of prism = \(450\text{ mm}\)
    • Simply supported span \(L = 450\text{ mm}\) (Supports at P and S)
    • Concentrated vertical loads at Q and R: \(W = 11.25\text{ kN}\) each
    • Spacing between loads and supports = \(150\text{ mm}\) (Standard third-point loading test)
  • Aim: Calculate the modulus of rupture (flexural tensile strength) \(f_r\) (in MPa).

3. Core Concepts:

  • The modulus of rupture is the maximum flexural tensile stress developed at the extreme bottom fiber just before failure.
  • Assuming a linear elastic stress distribution, the flexural formula applies: \(f_r = \dfrac{M_{\max}}{Z}\)
  • \(M_{\max}\) is the maximum bending moment occurring in the pure bending zone (middle third).
  • \(Z\) is the section modulus of the rectangular cross-section: \(Z = \dfrac{bd^2}{6}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate maximum bending moment \(M_{\max}\) resulting from the loads.
  2. Calculate section modulus \(Z\).
  3. Compute the stress \(f_r = M_{\max} / Z\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Maximum Bending Moment (\(M_{\max}\)):
    In a symmetrically loaded third-point loading setup, support reactions equal the applied loads (\(R_P = R_S = 11.25\text{ kN}\)).
    The maximum bending moment is constant between Q and R.
    Distance from support P to load Q: \(a = 150\text{ mm}\).\[M_{\max} = 11{,}250\text{ N} \times 150\text{ mm} = 1{,}687{,}500\text{ N·mm} \]
  2. Calculate Section Modulus (\(Z\)):\[Z = \dfrac{bd^2}{6} = \dfrac{150 \times (150)^2}{6} = \dfrac{150 \times 22{,}500}{6} = 562{,}500\text{ mm}^3 \]
  3. Calculate Modulus of Rupture (\(f_r\)):\[f_r = \dfrac{M_{\max}}{Z} = \dfrac{1{,}687{,}500}{562{,}500} = 3.0\text{ N/mm}^2\text{ (MPa)} \]Note: Self-weight of the concrete specimen is negligible here and is conventionally ignored in such tests unless explicitly requested.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.0 MPa | Accepted key range: 2.9 to 3.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question:
Two bolted plates under tension with alternative arrangement of bolt holes are shown in figures 1 and 2. The hole diameter, pitch, and gauge length are d, p and g, respectively.



Which one of the following conditions must be ensured to have higher net tensile capacity of configuration shown in Figure 2 than that shown in Figure 1?
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Tension Members

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Figure 1: A plate with a straight transverse failure path passing through 1 bolt hole.
    • Figure 2: An alternative plate connection with staggered bolts (pitch \(p\), gauge \(g\)).
    • Hole diameter = \(d\).
  • Aim: Determine the required condition for pitch \(p\) and gauge \(g\) such that the staggered layout (Figure 2) has a higher (or at least equal) net tensile capacity than the straight layout (Figure 1).

3. Core Concepts:

The tensile capacity of a plate is governed by its minimum net effective area \(A_n\). Based on IS 800:2007 (Clause 6.3.1):

\[ A_n = \left[b - nd + \sum \dfrac{p_i^2}{4g_i} \right] t \]
  • \(b\) = width of plate
  • \(d\) = diameter of the bolt hole
  • \(n\) = number of bolt holes in the failure path
  • \(p_i, g_i\) = pitch and gauge between consecutive staggered holes
  • \(t\) = plate thickness

In a staggered arrangement, tearing can occur along two paths:

  • Straight path across one hole: \(A_{\text{straight}} = (b - d)t\)
  • Zigzag path across two holes: \(A_{\text{zigzag}} = \left(b - 2d + \dfrac{p^2}{4g}\right)t\)

The failure path with the lesser area dictates the tensile capacity.

4. Solution Method:

For Figure 1 (straight failure through one hole), the net area is \((b - d)t\). To ensure the staggered arrangement in Figure 2 does not fail prematurely along the zigzag path, the area of the zigzag path must be strictly greater than the straight path area. If \(A_{\text{zigzag}} > A_{\text{straight}}\), staggering the bolts does not weaken the plate below the \((b-d)t\) baseline capacity.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the Inequality:\[A_{\text{zigzag}} > A_{\text{straight}} \]\[\left(b - 2d + \dfrac{p^2}{4g}\right)t > (b - d)t \]
  2. Simplify the Expression:
    Divide by thickness \(t\) (since \(t > 0\)):\[b - 2d + \dfrac{p^2}{4g} > b - d \]Subtract \(b\) from both sides:\[-2d + \dfrac{p^2}{4g} > -d \]Add \(2d\) to both sides:\[\dfrac{p^2}{4g} > d \]
  3. Solve for \(p^2\):
    Multiply by \(4g\) (since gauge \(g > 0\)):\[p^2 > 4gd \]If this condition holds, the staggered path yields an area greater than the straight path, ensuring the net capacity of Figure 2 is not compromised by the addition of the staggered bolt.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(p^2 > 4gd\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question:
Workability of concrete can be measured using slump, compaction factor and Vebe time. Consider the following statements for workability of concrete:

(i) As the slump increases, the Vebe time increases
(ii) As the slump increases, the compaction factor increases

Which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials | Concrete Technology / Properties of Fresh Concrete

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Two statements:
    (i) As the slump increases, the Vebe time increases.
    (ii) As the slump increases, the compaction factor increases.
  • Aim: Identify which statements are TRUE.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Slump Test: Higher slump values directly indicate higher workability (fluidity).
  • Vebe Time Test: Measures time to remold a concrete cone under vibration. High workability → concrete remolds rapidly → lower Vebe time.
  • Compaction Factor Test: Ratio of partially compacted to fully compacted concrete weight. High workability → easy self-compaction under gravity → higher compaction factor (closer to 1.0).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Connect increasing slump to increasing workability.
  2. Evaluate statement (i) by correlating high workability to Vebe time behavior.
  3. Evaluate statement (ii) by correlating high workability to compaction factor behavior.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate Statement (i):
    Increased slump \(\implies\) Increased workability \(\implies\) Less time to remold \(\implies\) Vebe time decreases.
    Conclusion: Statement (i) is False.
  2. Evaluate Statement (ii):
    Increased slump \(\implies\) Higher workability \(\implies\) Better self-compaction \(\implies\) Compaction factor increases.
    Conclusion: Statement (ii) is True.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q15
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question:
Consider the following statements for air-entrained concrete:

(i) Air-entrainment reduces the water demand for a given level of workability
(ii) Use of air-entrained concrete is required in environments where cyclic freezing and thawing is expected

Which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials | Concrete Technology / Chemical Admixtures

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Two statements regarding air-entrained concrete:
    (i) Air-entrainment reduces the water demand for a given level of workability.
    (ii) Use of air-entrained concrete is required in environments where cyclic freezing and thawing is expected.
  • Aim: Determine the validity of both statements.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Rheological Effect (Statement i): Microscopic air bubbles act like flexible "ball bearings," reducing internal friction between aggregate particles and enhancing workability. For a given target slump, an air-entrained mix requires less mixing water than a non-entrained mix.
  • Durability Effect (Statement ii): In cold climates, capillary water inside hardened concrete expands ~9% upon freezing, generating destructive tensile stresses. Entrained air voids act as relief chambers for expanding ice. This is a mandatory code requirement (e.g., ACI 318, IS 456) for freeze-thaw exposure.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Validate statement (i) through the physical lubrication mechanism in fresh concrete.
  2. Validate statement (ii) through the expansion-relief mechanism in hardened concrete.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Statement (i): Air voids improve flowability, so the designer can decrease the water-cement ratio while maintaining the desired slump. Water demand is reduced.
    Conclusion: Statement (i) is True.
  2. Statement (ii): Entrained air prevents spalling and scaling from ice expansion. It is universally required for cyclic freeze-thaw exposure.
    Conclusion: Statement (ii) is True.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

Consider the singly reinforced beam shown in the figure below:



At cross-section XX, which of the following statements is TRUE at the limit state?

The variation of strain is linear and that of stress is non-linear
The variation of both stress and strain is linear

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: The variation of stress is linear and that of strain is non-linear
structuredOptions.html: The variation of stress is linear and that of strain is non-linear

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: The variation of strain is linear and that of stress is non-linear
structuredOptions.html: The variation of strain is linear and that of stress is non-linear

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: The variation of both stress and strain is linear
structuredOptions.html: The variation of both stress and strain is linear

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: The variation of both stress and strain is non-linear
structuredOptions.html: The variation of both stress and strain is non-linear

questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Limit State Design / Flexure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A purely bending section (XX) of a simply supported singly reinforced beam at the limit state.
  • Aim: Identify the correct nature (linear vs. non-linear) of stress and strain variation across the depth of the section.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Strain Variation (IS 456:2000 Cl. 38.1.a): The fundamental assumption "Plane sections remain plane after bending" dictates that the strain profile is strictly linear, proportional to the distance from the neutral axis.
  • Stress Variation (IS 456:2000 Cl. 38.1.c): The stress-strain relationship for concrete in compression is highly non-linear. At the limit state, the code uses an idealized parabolic-rectangular stress block. Because strain varies linearly, the stress profile mirrors the non-linear material behavior — the stress profile is non-linear.

4. Solution Method:

  1. State the strain distribution based on Bernoulli's flexural hypothesis.
  2. State the stress distribution based on the limit state idealized material properties.
  3. Select the option matching these two profiles.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Strain variation: Strain is directly proportional to distance from the Neutral Axis → Linear.
  2. Stress variation: Idealized concrete stress block (parabola up to strain 0.002, rectangle up to 0.0035) → Non-linear.
  3. Linear strain + Non-linear stress → Option (B).

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: The development length of a deformed reinforcement bar can be expressed as \((1/k) (\phi\sigma_s/\tau_{bd})\). From the IS:456-2000, the value of \(k\) can be calculated as __________.
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Working Stress & Limit State Design / Bond & Development Length

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: General formula for development length of a deformed bar: \[L_d = \frac{1}{k}\left(\frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{\tau_{bd}}\right) \]
  • Aim: Calculate the dimensionless constant \(k\) as per IS 456:2000.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Base Formula (IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.2.1): \[L_d = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{4\,\tau_{bd}} \] where \(\tau_{bd}\) is the design bond stress for plain bars in tension.
  • Deformed Bar Modifier (Cl. 26.2.1.1): For deformed bars conforming to IS 1786, the tabulated \(\tau_{bd}\) values are increased by 60% (multiplied by \(1.6\)).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Start with the base development length formula.
  2. Apply the 60% increase modifier for deformed bars.
  3. Rearrange to match the provided formula and extract \(k\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Base formula:
    \[L_d = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{4\,\tau_{bd,\text{actual}}} \]
  2. Express actual bond stress for deformed bars:
    \[\tau_{bd,\text{actual}} = 1.6 \times \tau_{bd} \]
  3. Substitute and simplify:
    \[L_d = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{4 \times 1.6\,\tau_{bd}} = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{6.4\,\tau_{bd}} = \frac{1}{6.4}\left(\frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{\tau_{bd}}\right) \]
  4. Extract \(k\):
    Comparing with the given formula \(L_d = \dfrac{1}{k}\left(\dfrac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{\tau_{bd}}\right)\): \[k = 6.4 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6.4  |  Accepted key range: 6.38 to 6.42

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question:
The composition of an air-entrained concrete is given below:

Water : 184 kg/m³
Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC): 368 kg/m³
Sand : 606 kg/m³
Coarse aggregate : 1155 kg/m³

Assume the specific gravity of OPC, sand and coarse aggregate to be 3.14, 2.67 and 2.74, respectively. The air content is __________ liters/ m³.
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Concrete Mix Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Mix amounts per m³ of concrete:
    IngredientMass (kg)Specific Gravity (SG)
    Water1841.00
    OPC (Cement)3683.14
    Sand6062.67
    Coarse Aggregate (CA)11552.74
  • Aim: Find the entrapped air content per cubic meter in liters.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Absolute Volume Method (IS 10262 basis): The sum of the absolute solid volumes of all ingredients plus the volume of air must equal the total gross volume of freshly mixed concrete (\(1\text{ m}^3\)).
  • Volume Calculation: \[\text{Absolute Volume } (V) = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Specific Gravity} \times \text{Density of Water}} \]
  • Density of water \(\gamma_w = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)
  • \(1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ liters}\)

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the absolute volume of each individual ingredient in m³. Sum these volumes. The difference between the theoretical target yield (\(1\text{ m}^3\)) and the absolute solid volume sum is the volume occupied by air. Convert that difference into liters.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate absolute volumes (in m³):
    \[V_{\text{water}} = \frac{184}{1 \times 1000} = 0.184000\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_{\text{cement}} = \frac{368}{3.14 \times 1000} = 0.117197\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_{\text{sand}} = \frac{606}{2.67 \times 1000} = 0.226966\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_{\text{CA}} = \frac{1155}{2.74 \times 1000} = 0.421533\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Sum the solid volumes:
    \[V_{\text{solid}} = 0.184000 + 0.117197 + 0.226966 + 0.421533 = 0.949696\text{ m}^3 \]
  3. Find air volume and convert to liters:
    Target volume of concrete batch is \(1\text{ m}^3\).
    \[V_{\text{air}} = 1.0 - 0.949696 = 0.050304\text{ m}^3 \]\[\text{Air content in liters} = 0.050304 \times 1000 = 50.304\text{ liters} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 50.3 liters  |  Accepted key range: 49.5 to 51.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A bracket plate connected to a column flange transmits a load of 100 kN as shown in the following figure. The maximum force for which the bolts should be designed is __________ kN.
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Bolted Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Eccentric Load: \(P = 100\text{ kN}\)
    • Eccentricity from bolt group CG: \(e = 600\text{ mm}\)
    • Number of bolts: \(n = 5\)
    • Bolt arrangement: Quincunx pattern (like '5' on a dice) with horizontal spacing \(75\text{ mm}\) and vertical spacing \(75\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum resultant force on the most critically stressed bolt.

3. Core Concepts:

For an eccentrically loaded bolted connection (in-plane), the force on any bolt is the vector sum of:

  1. Direct Shear Force (\(\vec{F_d}\)): Assumed to be shared equally among all bolts. \[F_d = \frac{P}{n} \]
  2. Torsional Shear Force (\(\vec{F_t}\)): Arises due to the moment \(M = P \times e\). The force on a specific bolt is proportional to its radial distance \(r_i\) from the CG of the bolt group. \[\vec{F_t} = \frac{\vec{M} \times \vec{r_i}}{\sum r_i^2} \] In scalar components: \(F_{tx} = \dfrac{M \cdot y_i}{\sum r_i^2}\) and \(F_{ty} = \dfrac{M \cdot x_i}{\sum r_i^2}\)
  3. Resultant Force (\(F_R\)): \[F_R = \sqrt{(\sum F_x)^2 + (\sum F_y)^2} \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Coordinate Geometry of Bolt Group:
    Assign the origin \((0,0)\) to the central bolt (CG of the group). The coordinates \((x_i, y_i)\) of the 5 bolts are:
    Bolt\(x_i\) (mm)\(y_i\) (mm)
    Top-Right7575
    Bottom-Right75-75
    Top-Left-7575
    Bottom-Left-75-75
    Center00

    \[\sum r_i^2 = 4 \times (75^2 + 75^2) + 0 = 4 \times (5625 + 5625) = 45000\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Direct Shear Force (\(F_d\)):
    \[F_d = \frac{100\text{ kN}}{5} = 20\text{ kN (acting downwards, i.e., } -y\text{ direction)} \]
  3. Torsional Shear Force on Critical Bolt (Top-Right at \((75, 75)\)):
    Applied moment (clockwise): \(M = P \times e = 100 \times 600 = 60000\text{ kN-mm}\)
    \[F_{tx} = \frac{M \cdot y}{\sum r_i^2} = \frac{60000 \times 75}{45000} = 100\text{ kN (rightwards)} \]\[F_{ty} = \frac{M \cdot x}{\sum r_i^2} = \frac{60000 \times 75}{45000} = 100\text{ kN (downwards)} \]
    Note: The Bottom-Right bolt at \((75,-75)\) experiences \(F_{tx} = 100\text{ kN}\) leftwards and \(F_{ty} = 100\text{ kN}\) downwards — the vertical summation is identical, making both right-side bolts equally critical.
  4. Resultant Force (\(F_R\)) for Top-Right Bolt:
    • Total X-force: \(F_x = F_{tx} = 100\text{ kN}\)
    • Total Y-force: \(F_y = F_{ty} + F_d = 100 + 20 = 120\text{ kN}\)
    \[F_R = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2} = \sqrt{100^2 + 120^2} = \sqrt{10000 + 14400} = \sqrt{24400} \approx 156.205\text{ kN} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 156.20 kN  |  Accepted key range: 155 to 156.3

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Prestressed Concrete & Losses
questions.question: Consider the singly reinforced beam section given below (left figure). The stress block parameters for the cross-section from IS:456-2000 are also given below (right figure). The moment of resistance for the given section by the limit state method is __________ kN-m.
questions.explanation:
RCC Structures | Flexure Limit State

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Beam dimensions: Width \(b = 200\text{ mm}\), Effective depth \(d = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • Materials: Concrete M25 (\(f_{ck} = 25\text{ MPa}\)), Steel Fe415 (\(f_y = 415\text{ MPa}\))
    • Tension Reinforcement: 4 bars of \(12\text{ mm}\) diameter (\(4\text{-}12\Phi\))
  • Aim: Calculate the Moment of Resistance (\(M_u\)) of the section using the Limit State Method.

3. Core Concepts:

According to IS 456:2000 (Annex G):

  1. Area of Steel (\(A_{st}\)): \[A_{st} = n \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times \phi^2 \]
  2. Depth of Neutral Axis (\(x_u\)): Found by equating total compression to total tension: \[0.36\, f_{ck}\, b\, x_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st} \]
  3. Limiting Neutral Axis Depth (\(x_{u,max}\)): For Fe415 steel, \(x_{u,max} = 0.48d\)
  4. Moment of Resistance (\(M_u\)): If \(x_u < x_{u,max}\) (Under-reinforced): \[M_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\, x_u) \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Area of Steel (\(A_{st}\)):
    \[A_{st} = 4 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times (12)^2 = 452.39\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Find Actual Neutral Axis Depth (\(x_u\)):
    \[x_u = \frac{0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}}{0.36\, f_{ck}\, b} = \frac{0.87 \times 415 \times 452.39}{0.36 \times 25 \times 200} = \frac{163335.8}{1800} = 90.74\text{ mm} \]
  3. Section Classification:
    \[x_{u,max} = 0.48 \times 300 = 144\text{ mm} \]
    Since \(x_u = 90.74\text{ mm} < x_{u,max} = 144\text{ mm}\), the section is under-reinforced.
    Sanity Check: For an under-reinforced section, steel yields before concrete crushes — using \(0.87f_y\) is strictly valid.
  4. Calculate Moment of Resistance (\(M_u\)):
    \[M_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\, x_u) \]\[M_u = 163335.8 \times (300 - 0.42 \times 90.74) \]\[M_u = 163335.8 \times (300 - 38.11) = 163335.8 \times 261.89 \]\[M_u = 42{,}776{,}013\text{ N-mm} = 42.78\text{ kN-m} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 42.78 kN-m  |  Accepted key range: 42 to 43

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: For formation of collapse mechanism in the following figure, the minimum value of \(P_u\) is \(cM_p/L\). \(M_p\) and \(3M_p\) denote the plastic moment capacities of beam sections as shown in this figure. The value of c is __________.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Plastic Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Fixed-fixed continuous beam subjected to a point load \(P_u\)
    • Left segment: Length \(= 2\text{ m}\), Plastic moment capacity \(= 3M_p\)
    • Right segment: Total length \(= 1\text{ m} + 1\text{ m} = 2\text{ m}\), Plastic moment capacity \(= M_p\)
    • Load \(P_u\) applied in the middle of the right segment (at \(3\text{ m}\) from the left support)
  • Aim: Find the coefficient \(c\) for the minimum collapse load given by \(P_u = c\,\dfrac{M_p}{L}\).
    Note: The problem dimensionally implies \(L\) is a unit length placeholder of 1 meter to map to the diagram's explicit meter units.

3. Core Concepts:

To find the true collapse load, we apply the Kinematic Method (Mechanism Method) of plastic analysis. We equate External Work (EW) to Internal Work (IW) for all possible independent and combined mechanisms. The one yielding the minimum \(P_u\) is the true collapse mechanism.

  • \(EW = \sum P_i \delta_i\)
  • \(IW = \sum M_{pi}\,\theta_i\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Mechanism 1: Global Collapse
    Plastic hinges form at: Left Support A (capacity \(3M_p\)), under the load C (capacity \(M_p\)), and at Right Support D (capacity \(M_p\)). Let deflection under load = \(\Delta\).
    • Segment AC length \(= 3\text{ m}\): \(\theta_A = \dfrac{\Delta}{3}\)
    • Segment CD length \(= 1\text{ m}\): \(\theta_D = \Delta = 3\theta_A\)
    • Relative rotation at hinge C: \(\theta_C = \theta_A + \theta_D = 4\theta_A\)
    \[EW = P_u \times \Delta = P_u(3\theta_A) \]\[IW = 3M_p(\theta_A) + M_p(4\theta_A) + M_p(3\theta_A) = 10M_p\theta_A \]\[EW = IW \implies P_u = \frac{10}{3}M_p = 3.333\,M_p \]
    Verification: The moment at the step-change B (2 m from left): \(M_B = -3M_p + \frac{2}{3}(4M_p) = -0.333M_p\). Since \(|-0.333M_p| < M_p\), the section is safe — this mechanism is statically admissible.
  2. Mechanism 2: Local Collapse of the Right Segment
    Plastic hinges form at: Step-change B (capacity \(M_p\)), under the load C (capacity \(M_p\)), and at Right Support D (capacity \(M_p\)). The left segment AB remains rigid.
    • Segment BC length \(= 1\text{ m}\): \(\theta_B = \Delta\)
    • Segment CD length \(= 1\text{ m}\): \(\theta_D = \Delta\)
    • Relative rotation at C: \(\theta_C = \theta_B + \theta_D = 2\Delta\)
    \[EW = P_u \times \Delta \]\[IW = M_p(\Delta) + M_p(2\Delta) + M_p(\Delta) = 4M_p\Delta \]\[EW = IW \implies P_u = 4M_p \]
  3. Conclusion:
    Comparing both mechanisms:
    MechanismCollapse Load \(P_u\)
    Global Collapse\(3.333\,M_p\) ← Minimum (Governs)
    Local Collapse (Right)\(4.0\,M_p\)

    Matching \(P_u = c\,\dfrac{M_p}{L}\) with \(L = 1\text{ m}\): \(c = 3.33\)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.33  |  Accepted key range: 3.30 to 3.40

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q48

questions.question: An earth embankment is to be constructed with compacted cohesionless soil. The volume of the embankment is 5000 m³ and the target dry unit weight is 16.2 kN/m³. Three nearby sites (see figure below) have been identified from where the required soil can be transported to the construction site. The void ratios (e) of different sites are shown in the figure. Assume the specific gravity of soil to be 2.7 for all three sites. If the cost of transportation per km is twice the cost of excavation per m³ of borrow pits, which site would you choose as the most economic solution? (Use unit weight of water = 10 kN/m³)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earthwork Cost Optimization

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Embankment: Volume \(V_{emb} = 5000\text{ m}^3\), Target dry unit weight \(\gamma_d = 16.2\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Borrow Pits Data:
      SiteVoid Ratio \((e)\)Distance \((D)\) km
      X0.60140
      Y0.7080
      Z0.64100
    • Soil Properties: \(G_s = 2.7\), \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Cost Relation: Cost of transportation per km (\(C_t\)) is twice the cost of excavation per m³ (\(C_e\)): \(C_t = 2C_e\)
  • Aim: Identify the most economical borrow pit site.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Phase Relationships: The volume of solid particles (\(V_s\)) remains constant during earthwork operations. \[\gamma_d = \frac{G_s\,\gamma_w}{1+e} \quad \text{and} \quad V_{\text{total}} = V_s(1+e) \]
  • Total Cost Formulation: \[\text{Total Cost} = (C_e \times V_{\text{site}}) + (C_t \times D_{\text{site}}) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the void ratio of the target embankment (\(e_{emb}\)).
  2. Calculate the invariant volume of solids (\(V_s\)) required.
  3. Compute the excavation volume required from each site.
  4. Evaluate the cost index function for all three pits to find the minimum.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Void ratio and Volume of solids for the embankment:
    \[16.2 = \frac{2.7 \times 10}{1+e_{emb}} \implies 1+e_{emb} = \frac{27}{16.2} = 1.6667 \implies e_{emb} = 0.6667 \]\[V_s = \frac{V_{emb}}{1+e_{emb}} = \frac{5000}{1.6667} = 3000\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Excavation volumes required from each site:
    \[V_X = 3000(1 + 0.6) = 4800\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_Y = 3000(1 + 0.7) = 5100\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_Z = 3000(1 + 0.64) = 4920\text{ m}^3 \]
  3. Cost Function Optimization:
    Given \(C_t = 2C_e\), the total cost is:
    \[\text{Total Cost} = C_e \cdot V_{\text{site}} + 2C_e \cdot D_{\text{site}} = C_e(V_{\text{site}} + 2D_{\text{site}}) \]
    Minimize the cost index \(f = V_{\text{site}} + 2D_{\text{site}}\):
    Site\(V_{\text{site}}\) (m³)\(2D_{\text{site}}\) (km)Cost Index \(f\)
    X4800\(2 \times 140 = 280\)5080 ← Minimum
    Y5100\(2 \times 80 = 160\)5260
    Z4920\(2 \times 100 = 200\)5120

    Site X yields the minimum cost index, making it the most economical choice.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Site X  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Bond, Shear & Torsion in RCC
questions.question: A column of size 450 mm × 600 mm has unsupported length of 3.0 m and is braced against side sway in both directions. According to IS 456: 2000, the minimum eccentricities (in mm) with respect to major and minor principal axes are:
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Column Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Cross-sectional dimensions: Width \(b = 450\) mm, Depth \(D = 600\) mm
    • Unsupported length: \(L = 3.0\) m \(= 3000\) mm
    • Bracing condition: Braced against side sway in both directions.
  • Aim: Calculate the minimum eccentricities (\(e_{\text{min}}\)) with respect to the major and minor principal axes according to IS 456:2000.

3. Core Concepts:

Minimum Eccentricity (IS 456:2000, Clause 25.4): To account for construction inaccuracies, all columns must be designed for a minimum eccentricity along both axes.

The formula for minimum eccentricity is:\[e_{\text{min}} = \frac{L}{500} + \frac{\text{Lateral Dimension}}{30} \]subject to a strict absolute minimum condition: \(e_{\text{min}} \ge 20\) mm.

  • Major Axis: Bending occurs about the axis parallel to the width \(b\), so the lateral dimension resisting bending is the depth \(D = 600\) mm.
  • Minor Axis: Bending occurs about the axis parallel to the depth \(D\), so the lateral dimension resisting bending is the width \(b = 450\) mm.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the minimum eccentricity for the major axis using \(L\) and \(D\).
  2. Check if the computed value is at least 20 mm.
  3. Compute the minimum eccentricity for the minor axis using \(L\) and \(b\).
  4. Check if the computed value is at least 20 mm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Minimum eccentricity with respect to the major axis (\(e_{\text{min},x}\)):\[e_{\text{min},x} = \frac{3000}{500} + \frac{600}{30} = 6 + 20 = 26 \text{ mm} \]Check code condition: \(26 \text{ mm} \ge 20 \text{ mm}\) ✓ (Condition Satisfied).

Step 2: Minimum eccentricity with respect to the minor axis (\(e_{\text{min},y}\)):\[e_{\text{min},y} = \frac{3000}{500} + \frac{450}{30} = 6 + 15 = 21 \text{ mm} \]Check code condition: \(21 \text{ mm} \ge 20 \text{ mm}\) ✓ (Condition Satisfied).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 26.0 mm and 21.0 mm  |  Correct option: (B)
